reviews.text: The campsite was terrible. The only space in the site was a gravel pullout on the side of the road. Not even a spot to park safely.
reviews.author: Cody M.

reviews.text: Such a amazing campground, close to our favorite part of the lark, Paradise. I noticed the frequency of staff cleaning the bathroom facilities and was super impressed. We’re already talking about our trip back next summer!
reviews.author: John B.

reviews.text: Restrooms cleaned every day. I was amazed at how many camp sites  were closed. The sign said hazardous trees… However I believe they were just trying to keep the population down in the campground.
reviews.author: William W.

reviews.text: It seemed the campground was short staffed, as there was no one selling firewood at the firewood station, and bathrooms weren't cleaned for a few days.
reviews.author: Jack G.

reviews.text: wonderful campsite within an 8 mile drive of Paradise. and then the trails around the mountain.  the campsite was tidy and campers were quiet at night. the bathrooms were quite clean, except late in the evening when one of the toilets apparently stopped up. taken care of by the next morning.  also it was great to have the telephone # of the cougar campground staff as earlier in the summer we needed to cancel 3 nights of reservations and we could contact them immediately and allow other campers to use the site.  we honor the service of all who are in the park service...the best government use of tax funds. but the national parks need more funds to upgrade the facilities and trails and resume educational programs  for visitors.  I believe more public tax funds should be designated for these national parks...the jewels of our America.
reviews.author: pamela d.

reviews.text: This was a lovely campsite. I thought being front country it would be louder or more crowded, but it wasn't. The campsites were nicely spaced and there was a nice spot for the tent. There were many trees and the bathrooms were clean.
reviews.author: Hope P.

reviews.text: great campsite.  our site is a pull through site, easy for RV parking.  restroom is very clean. 15 min drive to Paradise visitor center.
reviews.author: Chaojun L.

reviews.text:
My husband and I camped at site C15 and enjoyed our time there. It’s a partially shaded site at the end of the loop, so there’s decent privacy. This particular site is better for an RV/camper as it has a spacious pull through driveway. We were tent camping and could only find one small area that was level enough for our tent. We walked around the other loops and it seems Loop D has more sites with true tent pads. 

Bathrooms were well-maintained and clean. There is good garbage disposal and recycling for select items. Any staff we interacted with was very friendly. Location is great in terms up getting up to Paradise and other big sights. No cell reception for Verizon or T-Mobile, but we were able to get service by Paradise Inn.

Firewood is only sold at Longmire general store and it’s a bit pricey ($15 a bundle). I’d recommend buying firewood from somewhere nearby to get better bang for your buck.
reviews.author: Tulsi P.

reviews.text: This campground is beautiful!  The rangers and the camp host were so polite and personable.  We stayed in loop C and this loop has a very tight turn at the end of it and we barely fit.  The trees had damage so other people have definitely hit them multiple times.  Our site was C28, a very long pull through.  We have a 30 foot trailer with a 20 foot tow vehicle.  We could not pull through this site due to a tree, but we were able to back in the trailer with ease.  Any longer than us would probably not be able to successfully drive through the loop.  Out site was huge and quite far away from other campers.  The kids loved how much room there was to play under the trees.  This is a very wooded campground and it was wonderful to relax under the trees.  This campground is within walking distance of the Carter Falls trailhead, I highly recommend this hike as well as this campground!
reviews.author: Katie M.

reviews.text:
Cougar Rock campsite A11 (Loop A) isn't an ideal "tent" campsite.  The pad for the tent is only 30-40 yards from the main road leading up to Paradise - lots of traffic.  In addition, the position of the campsite in relationship to the Loop A access road stinks . . .     (It is in the direct line of all on-coming vehicles; and, after dark, I can't tell you how many times I was blinded by some bonehead with his/her/their bright lights on . . . )   My buddy and I scoped out the other loops available in the Cougar Rock Campground and will definitely be choosing Loop B, Loop C or Loop D in the future.

On the other hand, the Rangers on duty around 2:00 p.m., Thursday, October 5 were great . . .
reviews.author: Jeff F.

reviews.text: BEAUTIFUL CAMPSITES!!! Thoughtfully made campsites with details like rock steps or stones and logs to sit on. Must see Paradise hiking / walking trails through the wildflowers. Must walk single-log bridge, with a pretty railing , across main road from Cougar Rock campground, & just South along the River. No showers, but it’s a drought there, and it’s COVID, so that is perfectly ok. Firewood is at the gift shop / general store in Longmire, during COVID. All COVID rules were followed well by visitors and staff. Very friendly staff.  Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Jeannine P.

reviews.text:
Campsite E19. Right by the road, lots of car noise all day. This campsite is easily 1/3 the size of other sites in the campground. It is a vehicle only site, and when you pull in, your car is 3 feet from the firepit, not ideal. We had room for a 10x10 pop up behind the van, also dangerously close to the fire pit due to the small campsite. And uneven behind the parking area. Trees limit the use of any other space on the site. Claims 2 parking spaces, there is no way you can fit 2 vehicles there. 
If you book at cougar rock, do not choose site E19.
reviews.author: Jeff K.

reviews.text: Site E14 was one of the best in the E loop! It is tucked away on its own, away from adjacent sites, and has a 2-tiered set-up. Super nice! (The tent pad is on the smaller side, so just double check if you happen to have a big tent.) I would also strongly recommend E6 and E8, both of which descend via steps to a very private spot in the "valley" within the loop. If you don't want to be close to neighbors, avoid 16, 17, 18, and 19. The whole loop is generator-free, though, which is awesome!
reviews.author: Jill S.

reviews.text: We stayed at site C15 August 6-9 and it was the perfect spot. Many sites were closed due to hazard trees, which meant we hardly had any neighbors and it was the most peaceful campground we've been to all summer. Great to be inside the park on the weekend to avoid entrance lines too. We also hiked to Comet Falls through Rampart Ridge directly from the campground.
reviews.author: Monika C.

reviews.text:
If you will visit the paradise visitor center ,this is the best place for camping. It’s almost 20 mins drive.

Campsite with full shade and privacy, enough space for tent and parking.

Without cellphone signal nearby, but T-M obile works in the paradise visitor center.

We want to come back again.
reviews.author: Xuesheng S.

reviews.text: I enjoyed Cougar Rock campground and Mt Rainier National Park. The location of the campground was excellent for going to the Paradise trails and the nearby trail to Carter Falls was an excellent hike. I enjoyed seeing all of the wildflowers on the Paradise trails, even in late august.
reviews.author: Jack H.

reviews.text: Lots of trees, shade, greenspace and no mosquitoes, blackflies or other bitey things. Nice and quiet, good recycling, picnic table and firepit in top condition - the only limitation is no showers... had to go for a swim in Bench lake instead :)
reviews.author: Gillian V.

reviews.text:
My wife and I were comfortable at the campsite. It had plenty of room and a nice fire ring. The restrooms were in very good shape only about 50 yards away. 
We hiked the Comet Falls trail which was well worth the effort.
reviews.author: CHAD R.

reviews.text: Great view of the Mountain from the camp ground. Walk across the street to River and Carter Falls hike, great for kids. Camp sites are very small. A, B, and C loops only a handful of sites could fit a camper.
reviews.author: John S.

reviews.text: The campsite B19 was a bit humid since it was close to a stream, but really lovely on the whole. It was perfect for social distancing since there was plenty of space between other campsites.
reviews.author: Breana M.

reviews.text: Mount Rainier National Park and Cougar Rock Campground are the best.  Many hikes for all capabilities close by.  The campground is beautiful forest, respectful people, quiet, and friendly.
reviews.author: Rob G.

reviews.text: We had two side by side campsites (E15 and 16), big enough for three tents and 9 people.  Bathrooms super clean.  Checking in was really easy.  Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Debra S.

reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful campground, with a view of Rainier on the main walking path between loops. Group sites 1 and 5 are my favorite. Coming back here asap :)
reviews.author: Sarah K.

reviews.text: Great location with a helpful staff. Site D008 had a great pull through space for an RV if you have it and can comfortably also fit a tent
reviews.author: Thomas H.

reviews.text: Very easy check-in process (you just show up), well-maintained campsites, and very easy to find. We loved our stay here!
reviews.author: Charles S.

reviews.text: Cougar Rock is very convenient to Paradise Visitor Center.  Great spot!
reviews.author: Kimberly H.

reviews.text: A lovely campground. Well maintained. I love it there.
reviews.author: Rebecca R.

reviews.text:
Cougar Rock Campground is beautiful!   We took our 2 kids (9 and 11) and 18' travel trailer to camp there and as the descriptions say it can get pretty tight in there- rocks and trees right alongside the roadways.  The bathrooms were clean and well stocked.  We also appreciated the  water spigots right outside of the bath house.  There was a little room with an odd looking sink (think utility-tub meets toilet, meets bidet...) for waste water from dishes, etc. in the bath house.

We really enjoyed that just across the street from the campground was the best place to view Mt. Rainier in our experience.  Its along the river and is one of many places that you can hop onto the Wonderland Trail.  One evening we took our bag chairs and relaxed next to the river overlooking Mt. Rainier. 

We also got on the Wonderland Trail and headed for Longmire where we hiked the Trail of the Shadows.  It was a pretty hike, just be prepared for a lot of trees.  That stretch of the Wonderland Trail is also very pretty and not terribly difficult.  There are bathrooms and a general store in Longmire.

We went up to the Henry M. Jackson V.C. and the ranger there was FANTASTIC!  That part of the park was still under snow and being from Michigan we didn't stick around (we've had our fill...)  ;)  I was bumming that we wouldn't get to see the wildflowers, but even in the end of June they just weren't ready yet.  Our kids did the Junior Ranger program and they have new books that were engaging and fun to do.  *If you are not sure that you'll be able to get back to a Visitor Center by the end of your trip, tell the ranger when you pick up the book and they will usually let you take the badge with you on the condition that you promise to have the kids take the pledge before you hand over the badge.

Waterfalls: Christine Falls and Narada Falls are really beautiful with rainbows when the sun comes out.  Be prepared to get wet at Narada Falls as there is a lot of mist.
reviews.author: Melissa M.

reviews.text: The campsite we reserved had been closed due to dangerous trees but we were not notified in advance to our arrival of the change.  Either the site was not tagged upon our arrival, or we did not notice the sign, or the sign was posted after we set up camp, either way, we did set up camp and a park ranger even drove by and waived at us as we were sitting around the camp fire.  At 6:00 am the following morning, we were awoken by a loud female voice yelling at us that we had to move to a different location.  It was one of the camp hosts and she told us to check with the ranger station to find out where we were supposed to move to.  From that point on, we were harassed by the camp hosts at our new location.  Training should be provided to your camp hosts to include harassment.  This was my second camping trip to Mt Rainier and it will be my last because of our experience at Cougar Rock.
reviews.author: Anne W.

reviews.text:
Camping Facilities were clean.  We chose campsite A-10.  Fairly level and easily held our 8ftx9ft tent.
Park Rangers were awesome!  Very helpful and informative!
Very close drive to Paradise Visitors Center (20 minutes)
Just across the road from Cougar Rock Campground is the Wonderland Trail.  Incredible mountain view and walk along the Nisqually and Paradise Rivers on the easy to moderate hike. You can hike up 1.1 miles to the Carter and Madcap Falls. Hike an additional 1.5 miles past Carter Falls to see Narada Falls.  (or you can access trailheads via your vehicle on drive to Paradise Visitors Center, but the trailhead parking areas can be crowded in the afternoons)   Recommend doing Reflection Lake early morning as the Sun is behind you and the wind is usually calm that time of day for best pictures.  Tons of hikes originate from Paradise Visitors Center.
reviews.author: Brian S.

reviews.text: Very nice campground. Lots of sites but still feels very private as there are lots of trees between each site. It's nice to have a place to park an RV and a flat spot for a tent or a kitchen area. Nice bathrooms. Easy walk to trails and access to both paradise and Longmire. Only issue is firewood. They state that firewood should come from no more than 50 miles away which is completely understandable.  However the firewood avilable for sale at Longmire is $15 per bundle. They had one bundle available and it had 5 pieces in it. Small pieces....So each small piece of wood was $3. Yet, they are in the process of thining the diseased trees around the campground and there are hundreds of downed trees. Needless to say people have been taking wood from these. When you make something prohibitively expensive you encourage people to use other resources.
reviews.author: Dennis L.

reviews.text:
Great location for RV campground close to Paradise & Longmire.  We spent 4 days and hiked to see many beautiful waterfalls with beautiful weather.  Mountain was visible every day.   Staffing in the area is an issue like everywhere else but they did a great job in town.  Example:  Gift shop in Paradise Inn was closed Tuesday & Wednesday due to staffing issues and dining at the Paradise Inn was limited.   Roads are narrow and winding thru the park... just have to take  your time.  
Many camping sites are not level so be prepared.   Camp rangers were very friendly and park was well taken care of.   We would definitely camp here again.  
There is ZERO cellular signal at the campground.   Nearest signal is in Paradise and limited spotty signal in Longmire.
reviews.author: John O.

reviews.text: The campground is in serious need of repair.  Many of the sites are closed.  Streets have pot holes, pull throughs are not level.  I have been camping at Cougar Rock for more than 50 years, and a total of 60 years at Mt. Rainier.  I first was camping with my family at the Longmire campground and then when Cougar Rock was new we started camping up there.  Obviously the park is underfunded.  I would  double, or triple fees and start putting money back into the campground and have park rangers available.  The other thing you could do is send emails like Yellowstone does and requests gifts towards specific projects.  I would easily donate if I knew where my funds were going, ie. trails, camping sites, restoration etc.
reviews.author: Richard B.

reviews.text: Lovely experience at Cougar Rock for our first time there. We particularly love the ranger programs and our kids (7 and 9) liked the amphitheater... they put on their own play and invited everyone to come see it :) . The bathroom path in loop B inexplicably runs right through another campsite (literally the middle of their driveway), which was a little awkward. Overall there isn't a lot of privacy between campsites but it was more "line of sight" other people rather than "everyone is on top of us," and that's what we expected to find at a popular campground. We enjoyed a four-night stay with hiking nearby and easy access to Paradise.
reviews.author: Julie H.

reviews.text: The campsite had no shade for most of the day. The ground was pretty level,  but rocky and hard to put stakes through. The proximity to the bathrooms was appreciated, not too close and not too far. It was a short distance to the Wonderland Trail, which made it convenient to make a day out of hiking to beautiful Carter Falls, Narada Falls and Reflection Lake. The rangers were friendly and helpful and I enjoyed their evening presentations. The lack of shade though was frustrating. Didn’t like coming to a hot tent after a long hike or trying to avoid the setting sun while I was making dinner on the table and bench.
reviews.author: kathleen d.

reviews.text: Overall a good experience, I appreciated the staff at check-in -- it was nice and convenient to have actual employees present at the site, who knew the campground well. While the restroom facilities were very clean and the site itself fine, I was very concerned about the quantity of standing dead trees in the campground -- not just a few, but dozens of standing dead trees, poised above restrooms, campsites, parking areas etc. Some had been marked with paint, but the sites were not closed. I hope that in the future, NPS at this site will take their hazard tree program more seriously.
reviews.author: Camille S.

reviews.text: A memorable trip to a remarkable park and campground. Although our site had some leveling issues, we were able to resolve them and spend two wonderful days at Mount Ranier. Cool weather made for comfortable hiking and the Longmire and other park Visitor’s centers provided all the information that we needed for a great visit. Despite COVID restrictions, park staff throughout the park were very supportive and helpful with their recommendations and the information they provided.
reviews.author: Sue M.

reviews.text: Cougar Rock is a wonderful campground with easy access to Paradise Visitor Center. My husband and I have been camping here for over 30 years. In the last several years the campground seems to cater more to RVs rather than those of us that still tent camp. If you tent camp be aware that this site has a large boulder sitting on the left side of the tent pad. We had to set our REI Dome on the boulder and only use the right side of the tent.
reviews.author: Albert S.

reviews.text: We stayed in Loop B, site 35 a pull through site. The entrance is shared with the site next to it, but we were not close!  A large rig would have difficulty pulling through, but ours was right at 27’. Pull thru pad has a slight slope to the right side. Large campsite and even though the road is on the other side of the site, the noise is almost non-exsistent. We would definitely pick this site again.
reviews.author: Anna B.

reviews.text: Dump station is closed and its very inconvenient since the road through the park to other campgrounds is closed.   Campers need better access to drinking water.   Also, site C12 is used as a cut through to the bathrooms from Loop B because there is no trail around.  It was not great having people constantly walk though our campsite while we were trying to have a campfire or cook dinner.
reviews.author: Stephen P.

reviews.text: This was my first time at Mt. Rainier Nat'l Park and it did not disappoint. It was breathtaking, and the campsite we had was perfect as it had sun for most of the day, and a nice bit of shade, close to the bathrooms, and easy access to the road. Definitely plan on staying here again. We did the Carter Falls hike, Panorama Point/Skyline, Rampart Ridge, and Bench and Snow Lake for hikes!
reviews.author: Aly Q.

reviews.text: Great campground with lots to do close by and easier access to Paradise. Facilities are alright - need a bit of TLC, but nice to have flushing toilets and proper dish cleaning area. While we were surprised there wasn't a fire ban, you can no longer buy firewood at the campground and need to buy at Longmire for $15!! Seems a bit steep when it's typically $5 elsewhere...
reviews.author: Justine B.

reviews.text: Be aware that after labor day couger rock campground closes loops. If you have a reservation on Labor day in loops B,C, or D and want to stay another day - they close those loops the next day and you will have to move. To move you will have to battle about 30 other campers and get in line at 6am the next day to get a site as they move everyone into A, E, and R loops.
reviews.author: Matthew G.

reviews.text:
Had no problem getting our 30ft RV into loop E. Stayed at site 25.
Spots are relatively close together, not much privacy. Still, a beautiful location and you can see Mt. Rainier peeking through the trees. 
We had three teenagers and a dog and everyone was very happy! We’d totally stay here again.
reviews.author: Shauna  Y.

reviews.text: Exceptional campsite, in the middle of the dense forest. It has no bear box, so you have to put everything back in your car. No firewood for sale at the campground, the store in Longmire sells bundles at $15 each. Wildlife seen: 1 bunny. Great campground for hiking Panorama.
reviews.author: Alex P.

reviews.text: We arrived at about noon on a Monday in late August and were able to get a campsite.  The ranger at the check in was able to match our site to the type of tent we were camping in.  We had an excellent site and were very pleased with our stay.
reviews.author: Richard C.

reviews.text: We enjoyed our one night stay at Cougar Rock.  The Vault Toilets were clean and campers were pretty quiet.  The level tent areas were a nice touch too.  Bring cash or check for firewood or First Come First Server Registration.
reviews.author: Jon S.

reviews.text: Closest campground to Paradise. Loved it. Would camp there again no problem. No service on the campground but service is available at Paradise, I don’t need cell service but I know some people like having it.
reviews.author: Allison D.

reviews.text: Since the moment we arrived, the scenic view was breathtaking.  The Park rangers were very personable and friendly, and could answer all questions.  Waterfall under the road is a must see.. don't miss it.
reviews.author: Glenn H.

reviews.text: please spend the money and time to remove all the hazard trees. that would open 50 more sites and stop 40 people every am from asking if you are checking out today.
reviews.author: DAN N.

reviews.text:
This campsite is at the end of a row and backs directly onto the serene Ohanapecosh River with massive trees providing cover from the sun. It is drive-up, with packed earth, a firepit with grilling grate, a log for sitting, a picnic table, and bearproof storage locker.

Because this particular site has a neighboring campsite on one side only, and that site was unoccupied, it often felt as though we had the campsite to ourselves. At the nearby day use area there is a wading area in the river where the current slows (the water is freezing!), the bathrooms were clean, and there is potable water near the bathrooms. The firewood person comes by between 5-7pm, bundles are small, include kindling, and are $7.

The rangers are informative and friendly and advised us that we could keep our food in our car (whereas in Yosemite, for example, this is unadvisable). The amphitheater is currently closed due to COVID.

Overall, this is a perfect point from which to explore Mt. Rainier National Park, right at the foot of the road to Paradise. We will definitely be back.
reviews.author: Evan B.

reviews.text:
Site D6 is close to the river, but completely open to site D5. Next time I would want to reserve both sites to have someone I know next to me. This site is close to a STEEP river trail that leads down to a nice quiet spot to relax. If you can navigate the trail, you have a nice little private beach of your own to read a book and catch the last sun spots of the day.

I love this campground because of how close it is to many trails. At times the campground is quite loud...and many of the spots are not private. But, I am on a mission to find a list of the campsites at Ohanapecosh that feel private (to me)...because the area is just so beautiful and amazing. 

This drawback of this campground, like many I went to this summer...is that there were SO MANY empty spots that said reserved. I saw many spots that I would have LIKED to camp in...but they were reserved and NOBODY showed up. So sad that other humans are doing this. It's not that hard to cancel a reservation online. I mean, if you aren't gonna camp...cancel and release your campsite for others to experience the beauty and mental health benefits of being immersed in the outdoors.
reviews.author: Tasha S.

reviews.text: Ohanapecosh was an excellent well maintained campground with friendly and helpful hosts. Some free advice, fill up on gas in one of the towns before you arrive as gas stations are a bit far. Also make sure to make reservations as sites fill up quickly
reviews.author: B. Eric F.

reviews.text: Site C22 is listed as "waterfront" with two tent pads but it is NOT. It's in the center of a loop with no privacy and no tent pads. I tried to add the vacant site next to mine but the staff person said it was booked, but it wasn't.
reviews.author: Jayne R.

reviews.text: Great and absolutely beautiful campground! Lots of space between sites and bathrooms were well maintained. The trail loop to the falls which is right by the camp is completely worth it.
reviews.author: Max O.

reviews.text:
What a gem of a campground and an even better campsite.
A21 is set by itself on high ground. A short downhill walk to the river. Falling asleep to the sounds of the river. Check. Waking up to the sounds of the river. Check. The driveway can be tricky for backing in and leaving (might take a couple reracks). Overall amazing site, beautiful view. Guy sells wood for $7 a bundle and it includes some kindling. He shows up later in the day and makes 2 pass through. I wish he had a bell of some sort to alert us he is driving through. We missed him a couple times.
reviews.author: Maura C.

reviews.text: This was our second trip to Ohanapecosh Campground this summer and we had an absolutely fabulous camping experience both times. Both of our stays were in A loop right on the river and it was a pleasure to see how much the river changed from swift and cold in mid July to a gentler flow in early September. The best sites in the campground are definitely on the river but the location can't be beat for exploring the whole park. Wonderful hikes right in the Ohanapecosh area and easy, highly scenic drives to both Sunrise and Paradise. Recommend!
reviews.author: Caroline B.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground, but site C7 was awful. It is right next to a path down to the water, so all day long people walked right through our site to get to the river. They came in droves, dragging their strollers, dogs, coolers, etc. right through our campfire circle without even a “sorry”. It was obnoxious. Site C6 is supposedly a separate site, but the way the sites are designed their campfire was practically on top of ours. I would not ever book this site again. What a disappointment.
reviews.author: Jeanne C.

reviews.text: Our stay at the campsite was wonderful. The site has all the essential amenities, the site was spacious, the washrooms were clean and there was adequate distance between the sites so that there is no disturbance and/or noise. There are ton of attractions and hiking spots in driving range, we woke up early and drove to sunrise point in the morning which was great.
reviews.author: Vamsi T.

reviews.text: They closed the area of the campground we were staying in without notice and did not inform us it was closed until all the other campsites were sold out. They were unwilling to accommodate. So we had to drive 3 hours back home.
reviews.author: Jessica  C.

reviews.text: Great site overlooking the river. Was able to fit one 4 person tent with room remaining. A short walk to the bathrooms. This site has no neighbors on either side just across from it.
reviews.author: Elma H.

reviews.text:
We stayed in the A loop next to the bathrooms. It would be nice to get the lights to project more on the ground. I work for Redwood National Park and we changed the outdoor lighting at facilities to special night lighting that maintains both dark skies and does not attract insects. 

The bathroom fixtures need to be updated as the faucets were loose. I do like the fire pits being up on a concrete pad where there is better air. I know air inversion is a problem so check on some YouTube videos about creating a fire pit that is smokeless. It exists. 

The path to the swimming area needs to be fixed. There is too much erosion going on so a walkway down to the river bar and revegetating the area would be in order. 

Please keep some sights first come, first served as there are still people who travel this way. It seems to me that since the park is so popular and all the campgrounds only allow smaller campers and trailers that another campground needs to be considered maybe near Longmire so it can be on the same water system. The sights could then accommodate large RV’s and trailers. 

Thank you for good roads in the park, if only you could get Washington to work on their roads. 

Finally, at Cougar Rock campground, the wash basin for kitchen items is very nice. Maybe the same should be made at Ohanapecosh.
reviews.author: Paul S.

reviews.text: A good stay. Five days, four nights. Booked back in February. With La Wis Wis closed this season, my choices were super slim. In hindsight, only A, B, and C loops were open at Ohanapecosh. Grounds crews sawed up fallen trees across the bridge. I waited around for the firewood guy, but gave up on him. Went into Packwood three times, for a total bundle count of 23 bundles. Early June is chilly, 40-50⁰ at night. Not much animal sightings. A couple chipmunks, a crow, two camp robber birds, a robbin, and a finch. There are bear boxes here, so bears do exist. Flushing toilets, and running water sinks. No showers. No campground hosts, but a Visitor Center, with actual Park Ranger, junior ranger uniform staff. Very friendly.
reviews.author: Christopher J.

reviews.text: We love this campground. It is quiet and sheltered in the old growth forest. It is convenient to both the Sunrise and Paradise sides of the park. Within the campground itself are a well staffed Visitor Center and trailheads for a nature trail and beautiful Silver Falls. The Ohanapecosh River runs through the campground and provides sweet rushing water white noise at night. The staff and campground host are amazing.  So why not 5 stars??? Because your chances of finding paper towels in a rest room seem to be less than 10%. We were there for over a week, so this wasn't a fluke or an end of the weekend thing.  So go and enjoy a wonderful, peaceful experience. Just bring your own hand towel.
reviews.author: Vicki C.

reviews.text:
Good site for smaller group. While the site is large, you may struggle to find enough flat space for two tents. Check Google Maps Street View for better idea of what the campsite looks like. High tree cover. Creek is small. The campsite is below the road, and the driveway is on a slope.

Check when the campsite visitor center closes, for us it was 5pm. Silver Falls trail from the campsite is okay for a campsite trail, but I would rather spend the time doing Myrtle Falls or Narada Falls. There is no phone signal at the campsite, but full bars at Paradise if needed.
reviews.author: Max L.

reviews.text: While I liked the campsite, area for text was about 15 feet from other campsites fire pit. Had a nice creek behind the site. Because it was so close to other campsite, I just slept in a hammock by the creek. Worked out well. Good site for tents, not sure about level ness for an RV
reviews.author: James G.

reviews.text: The beautiful setting with the huge trees and the color of the Ohanapecosh River are very relaxing.  There are plenty of trails to wander on and nearby Mt. Rainier National Park to visit.  Well used park as it has been used for 100 yrs or so.
reviews.author: Daina H.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Silver Falls hike was a great afternoon activity and the water is pristine. The nearby town (Packwood) was a great spot to buy some firewood and coffee.
reviews.author: Carly Y.

reviews.text: Our campground was surrounded by a river and beautiful stream with cascading water. The area was gorgeous and serene.
reviews.author: Lisa G.

reviews.text: Snagged a site without prior reservation around 5:00PM mid-week.  Check in at ranger station for available sites.
reviews.author: Clifton G.

reviews.text: Camp site and bathroom were well maintained. Nice location and beautiful hike to Silver Fall.
reviews.author: Qinglin M.

reviews.text: The site was very large and isolated.  It was a a serene experience.
reviews.author: Cass C.

reviews.text: Awesome campground .
reviews.author: Dhurba  A.

reviews.text: The Rangers that were on site were very understanding of our concerns about campers who were disruptive and disregarding the rules that most campers were abiding by.  They, however, did not feel they had the authority to do anything to change the behavior of the campers who had been identified and complained about by many fellow campers.  The disruptions of the 4 tents, 3 cars and 20 or so very loud and rowdy campers in one campsite along with a dog that was left unattended and continuously barking for hours was unacceptable to us and many campers who were trying to enjoy a peaceful tent camping experience in our National Park system.   We decided to leave early because the stress and anxiety that was created because the park was not able to act in a way that protected my rights as a rule following member of society was excessive.  This was my only vacation this summer.  It was destroyed because the lawlessness that was allowed to continue created too much stress for me.  I am disappointed and regret my support of the National Parks.  It has lost its appeal for me as a destination for a nature lover, hiker, and tent camper.  I am 60 years old and have been supporting the National Park for over 20 years.
reviews.author: DARIN G.

reviews.text:
Lovely campground.  We stayed at E005, in late July. Lots of trees and even underbrush. It made for a quiet experience, even though the campground was full.  E005 has room for a truck+trailer, or a couple cars. We squeezed 3 cars in, one night. 
Enough space for 2 tents spread apart, 3 tents if you're friendly.  The fire pit was good, a nice wide level area around it. We fit 7 chairs comfortably. Only a few mosquitos, and only at dusk. Just one of the people in our group got bit. 

The bathrooms are not far from the site, and they were well-maintained by the camp hosts. 

Easy access to the river, if you want to take a dip or a bath.  And there's a nice, easy 3-mile hike right from the campsite, to a scenic waterfall.  You can swim there, too. 

The campground is really close, like a 3 minute drive, to the east entrance (Stevens Canyon entrance) to Paradise. AFAIK, as of 2023 August, the road from that entrance to Paradise is still closed M-F for construction and maintenance. It's open on the weekends. 

We've previously stayed on the D loop, and the H loop.  All the sites seem to be very nice. I haven't had a bad experience. We really enjoy Ohanapecosh, and we'll return soon.
reviews.author: Dino C.

reviews.text:
If you're young and strong, this is a great site as it's a walk-in site, up a big hill, then, down a long path.  I'm female and 60+. Thank God for the Ranger who helped me get all my gear up there with 2 dogs in tow!  
It was the last available site at the park and I had to take it because my dogs freak out from fireworks.  The site sits just above and to the left of its nearest site, making it a great site for close friends who want to camp close but in different sites. The site is small and adequate for 2 to 4 people in one larger tent.  (A family.)  I had great neighbors!
There are bathroom facilities at the top of the hill when you first come up, so it's not far from the site. Bring your own soap!  I don't think there was hot water and there are no showers but there are toilets, and it was clean. 
There was a clearing of tree branches above the site, so great spot for star gazing!!  
It had a nice firepit and table.  
The park itself is beautiful.
reviews.author: Catherine L.

reviews.text: Ohanapecosh is now one of my favorite campsites!!! I had a reservation for night 1, the site was very big and roomie with no neighbors as the next site was closed due to hazardous trees. I then got a FCFS site the next day (Wednesday AM); this was a fairly easy process that required being at the ranger office by around 730 or 800am. I believe they still had FCFS by around 1200p that day. The next site was smaller and closer to neighbors with little privacy. However, the campers were all very respectful of space and its one of the quietest campgrounds I've ever been too, despite how big it is! The creek and river run through the campground and at night you hear the river running which was soothing and glorious. All the facilities are very clean and well-maintained. Lots to explore with the river and Silver Falls Trail Loop right from the campground. Many loops and sites to fit every type of camper's needs. Will be going back yearly!
reviews.author: Krystal P.

reviews.text:
The reservation system had just switched to FF, First Come/First Served, when I decided to camp. I wasn't sure how that would work but I trusted in the system. As I drove up to the Visitor Center a large white board signed explained everything. I checked in with Park Staff and was quickly able to reserve my favorite site from my previous on line review. Staff assured me that I had a good site. I was very pleased when the Staff member asked if I had my senior access pass for the Park. I did and received 1/2 off the site cost. Nice surprise.
I found the grounds clean, quiet, and well maintained. The Staff must work very hard because there were not a lot of them on duty. 
I would love to see Grove of the Patriarch again. It's been since the 1980's I believe. I read it was closed indefinitely.
reviews.author: Pamela P.

reviews.text:
I can't say enough great things about Ohanapecosh Campground. I have been there several times recently and I'm always finding new adventures to take. There are a number of easy and more challenging trails right from the campground, plus the river to explore that runs right through the campground. It is also situated about 45 minutes from Paradise and about 60 minutes from Sunrise, which are both "must see" destinations for further exploring. The scenery is stunning, campsites and grounds are kept extremely clean and the wild flowers in summer are amazing!

I suggest you arrive at Paradise or Sunrise early (before 7AM) on summer weekends and before 8AM on summer week days to avoid lines getting into the parking lots.
reviews.author: Steven J.

reviews.text: Site C10 is large but the table and fire pit are incredibly close to the neighboring site. The trail to the amazing swim hole in the river is right next to this site so expect hundreds of people walking by on a busy Saturday. Maneuvering my small trailer was slightly impaired by how close the garbage station is to the driveway. Silver falls is worth the walk- we passed about about 50 other folks on the trail. There are flush toilets here.  My daughter liked the ranger station there are a lot of stuffed creatures. I tried to get a next day permit for Sunset and Paradise by using the WiFi at the station at the 7 pm release but it wouldn’t work. Overall a good experience but we probably won’t come back.
reviews.author: McCalester L.

reviews.text: I have camped at Ohanapecosh for 64 years I always try to spend my birthday there and was able to do that this year with my grandchildren what I love the most there is the trees have been there since my grandparents used to come to the Hot Springs resort back in the 30s and 40s when they bring my mom and her sister camping there and my mom brought us I brought my kids and now I bring my grandchildren so for five generations the same trees are there. Staff was helpful exhibit at the visitor center are wonderful and still there and we really enjoyed going up to Paradise and Box Canyon. Thank you for being good stewards of the park I hope it will be there for my grandchildren’s children!
reviews.author: Anna L.

reviews.text: This campground is different than most others I have visited. Upon arrival if you do not have reservations you are supposed to go to the rangers office and pay for a site. If you have an RV they do not have a place for you to park to go to the office and they had no signs saying check in first. I wound up parking in a site that had no reserved sign on it and then hiking to the rangers office to make my single night purchase. When I was purchasing my site they said I need to come to them before occupying it kind of passive aggressively. Other than that the campground was clean and beautiful. The visitors center was pretty neat and I would visit again if the opportunity arises.
reviews.author: David C.

reviews.text: Although the campground was beautiful and well maintained, the experience was ruined by the massive amounts of people coming in and looking for open campsites all day. The area around the ranger station was dangerous with cars parked on every spare inch waiting to get a spot.  The ranger station would be better placed farther up the road, away from the camp sites. And possibly better communication to the public that specifically all of the FF sites are full early in the morning, and driving loops around the campground all morning are a futile attempt at getting a spot.
reviews.author: Sara M.

reviews.text:
I needed to cancel my 2 night reservation within a day of arrival.  It was impossible to figure out how to cancel via the website and when I searched for the ranger station's phone number, Google listed the incorrect phone number and I was never able to get in touch to cancel my site.  Sadly, this probably meant at least one night this site went used.  Hopefully someone was able to use it the second night of our reservation as demand for camping is high.
Please include the ranger station's phone number on the email confirmation sent a few days before arrival.
reviews.author: Beth Z.

reviews.text: The staff was wonderful and the campground gorgeous.  The only problem was the reservation people put "first come first serve" on all the campsites in sections D.E, F. H so everyone who had a reservation up to Sept 6 assumed they could stay as first come first serve.   Actually the park closed all those sections and people got up at 6 am to stand in line to get a place at the park for the Sept 7th on.  The staff even handled that well, but there was no excuse for the reservation problem.  All they needed to do was code the closed sections, unavailable.
reviews.author: Floris M.

reviews.text:
Upon arrival, the information center has clear instructions for reservation holders. The sites are well kept, clean, and spacious. Bear boxes are provided for food storage. The bathrooms were clean and had lights. 
The river is gorgeous and there is a beach and a rock for jumping into the bracingly cold water! Within the park is a wonderful trailhead for Silver Falls. It's an easy 2.7 mile hike and the payoff is a raging waterfall view. There is an additional short path to the rocks by the falls.  Gorgeous! I want to go back ASAP!
reviews.author: Anna A.

reviews.text:
This is a beautiful site right on the water BUT a path down to the most popular part of the river is literally right next to the fire pit. Enjoy 50-100 people walking through your campsite (even when at the top of the path there is nowhere to walk other than right through your campsite past your car because there are bushes that corral people in that direction) during the day and into early evening. 

It really is a nice site but this was very bothersome for us, but hey maybe your party won’t mind meeting some new people!
reviews.author: Ryan O.

reviews.text: Our site at Ohanapecosh campground was absolutely beautiful. Towering mossy trees surrounded the site and aquamarine colored river ran next to us, which was very soothing for sleep. Site was well equipped with concrete picnic table and fire circle. Bathrooms were clean and easily accessible with fresh water available as well. Ohanapecosh provided easy access to the short hot spring trail, and the silver falls trail. The falls were stunning, lots of power. Definitely an experience I would suggest!
reviews.author: Ashley S.

reviews.text: One of the most beautiful campgrounds we have experienced, even with most of the loops being closed either for the season or because of tree-falling danger.  Hiking options directly from the campsite are a bit limited, but many trailheads are accessible with a short drive.  Access to the Grove of The Patriarchs is closed because the bridge is out, but you'll still be awed by the scenery.  Site and facilities are clean, campsites are fairly large and bear boxes for everyone!  We'll be back.
reviews.author: Russ P.

reviews.text:
Couldn't be better. Rangers were all friendly and campsites clean and bathrooms great. Silver falls was a delight and my husband even swam down below where they were fishing even though no fish caught that day.
My only complaint was when I tried to get 2 days on the website, it only gave me one and when I went back on, the second night was gone. I guess I was too slow and others grabbed it.
Looking forward to the Grove of the Patriarchs when we return next year or later.
reviews.author: Marne T.

reviews.text: Quiet and peaceful family oriented with lots of easy bicycling around the loops. Plenty of hiking trails nearby from super easy to difficult. Nice, well kept bathrooms with a dish sink and water fountains in each loop. Wonderful helpful rangers but sadly no more evening presentations due to COVID. We stayed almost a week with different people coming and going in the sites around us and we made some great friends!
reviews.author: Paul D.

reviews.text: Beautiful site with a great path down to the Ohanapecosh river. Tall trees are persistent through the entire campground and provide canopy coverage from the sun and light rain. The site next to ours was closed for administrative purposes, otherwise there likely would not have been enough privacy between the two sites as the firepit rings are located closer together. Highly recommend for small group camping.
reviews.author: Alexander S.

reviews.text:
The site was very spacious and flat. Loved that there was a lockable bear box available for each site. Bathrooms, water and trash were fairly close by. Flush toilets is always a plus! 
Only minor downsides would be that the sites on the inside of the loops are less private and when large groups stay up late and party the sound travels throughout the campground (bring earplugs just in case!)
reviews.author: Megan S.

reviews.text: When we arrived the ranger said he needed to do his rounds and to go ahead and pick out a camp site. He said he would be back in an hour to get us checked in. We set up our site. About 45 minutes later another family showed up to our site and said it was their site. When we went to speak with the ranger he said there was nothing he could do. Seriously disappointed this trip.
reviews.author: Marian B.

reviews.text:
Beautiful trees but no privacy as there isn’t much of an understory (bushes, etc.) in most sites, so no visual barriers between sites. For us this meant a family of 10-12 people just ten feet away who frequently walked right through our campsite and the next one to get to the bathrooms and water. 

The river and trails are beautiful.
reviews.author: Rebecca K.

reviews.text: The campground is WONDERFUL - the ranger station is great and has really good programs for all ages (I have a 4 year old and she had a blast). We hiked to the hot springs and Silver Falls, both accessible from the campground, and they were perfect hikes for us. We are big fans of this campground and will definitely be coming back <3
reviews.author: Tessa R.

reviews.text: loved that there were trails at the campsite and places to cliff jump and swim in the river. there were so many people in the water which was so fun to watch! good accessibility to the river bank as well if you just want to hangout and not swim. has a visitor center which is great and fire wood for sale too. lovely!
reviews.author: Camryn W.

reviews.text: This campsite located east of Mount Rainier is great! It is relatively close to some great Mount Rainier lookout spots such as Sunrise. All of the typical amenities we needed for camping was available at the campground and the ranger at the visitors center was very helpful in answering all of our questions.
reviews.author: Allison  F.

reviews.text: Considerable vehicle traffic and the fire pit is close to the road. Tent area is tucked away in the site but there is a considerable root in the middle of the tent area. Campground is still great and the rangers are awesome. Will be camping here again in a few weeks, just not at this campsite.
reviews.author: Josh J.

reviews.text: We were not able to reserve a site until a couple of days before our trip. It was a lovely site. There seems to be more spaciousness around sites than in years past. Everyone was friendly and relaxed. Thanks so much for doing what you can do to keep up the grounds with less budget.
reviews.author: Liv M.

reviews.text:
We had an amazing time at Fairholme! It really is a magical place and one of the most beautiful places i've ever camped at. We stayed in site #85 one of the walk-in spots right on the lake. I was so thrilled to get one of these spots by being up first thing in the morning when the reservations opens up.  

Somethings to know about this site, while its stunning and you are literally right on the water you have to walk up and down a pretty steep hill, I would recommend bringing a wagon for your gear or all your stuff is going to go flying down the hill when you pack to leave like I saw with several others. The site is located right at the entrance of the path down to the lower walk in spots on the lake so there will be people walking right past your site constantly. It would be nice if they oriented the picnic bench on the opposite side of the site instead of it facing directly into the neighboring camp site, kind of awkward. 

Minor things that I easily looked over because we spent most of our time on the shore of the lake with the cute ducks or in the water. The general store was well stocked with a good selection of items too.  We had a fabulous time and can't wait to return and try out one of the other sites!
reviews.author: Nicole R.

reviews.text:
Beautiful area.  Ecosystem was very different than anything I'd ever seen.  Campground was clean and well maintained.
Negatives:
- no Verizon cell coverage
- site generally not very level
- logging trucks were very noisy early in the morning, primarily from the compression brakes they're not supposed to be using!
reviews.author: Jerry R.

reviews.text: We had reserved site 20B. Unfortunately, the parking spot was so sloped we could not level our small RV. We had to scramble to find another spot at a different campground further down the road. Very nerve-wracking in the middle of a camping trip. It would be a great thing if spots that are good for tent camping (the campsite had a lovely spot, level and smooth, behind the picnic table--perfect for a large tent), and not so great for a van or small RV could be designated as such.
reviews.author: Lilly W.

reviews.text: Lake Crescent is magnificent. The campground itself leaves much to be desired. Neighboring sites are far too close together and, as an outdoor enthusiast, I find that overwhelming human presence detracts from the experience. I really wish our National Parks system would take this into consideration when designing the layout of campgrounds. I understand the idea is to meet demand, but opportunities to stay and enjoy nature the way I prefer are so limited. If walk in sites could actually lead a decent way out from other campers, so one wouldn't feel self conscious about holding a normal conversation, around a fire, while waiting for the stars to come out, that would be an amazing thing. Also having people's enthusiastic children scream and run through your site all evening detracts from the feeling I am after.
reviews.author: Eric D.

reviews.text: Site: 53C: very spacious site where you definitely have room to park 2 vehicles and 2-3 tents. You have some partially obstructed views of the lake through the trees. Close to one of the bathrooms which looks to have been remodeled recently and reasonably close to the Loop C bathroom as well. Only downside is the lack of privacy: the site 54 has a pretty clear view of your site and you're right above the walk-in sites below. Since the site is wide you also are pretty exposed to the loop road so not much privacy from other campers that are walking to/from their campsites.
reviews.author: Shaw W.

reviews.text:
Amazing place- Being right in front of the lake and surrounded by so much nature makes it beautiful and magical. 
No need to drive anywhere if you’d like to hike as there’s a trail nearby. The Sol Duc Springs are a 5min drive away. The nature around the area gives this place all the stars it deserves.
Aside from the trail- I wish rangers were more present- at least do a round at night as some campers are very inconsiderate: drinking, being loud and letting kids run around with flashlights pointing them into others tents… 
This campground doesn’t have showers and the ladies restroom ran out of toilet paper - it took them TWO days to put some in- there also isn’t any soap.
This is my 5th National Park visited (I started during the pandemic) and Olympic National Park is in serious need of maintenance. The rangers are all very young and maybe they are knowledgeable- but when you have questions they provide minimal response, or say ‘idk’ or are not friendly (very different from other NP were rangers are eager to share knowledge).
In summary: The place is gorgeous - the lack of maintenance and ranger activity is extremely poor.
reviews.author: Farah C.

reviews.text: The campground is beautiful, we camped at spot 72 and it had a great view. The only downside of this campground is the proximity to the main road that goes around the lake. The logging trucks are super loud, which I wasn’t expecting, and impacted the magic of camping in such a beautiful location, which is a shame. Other than that it was a great place to camp at, I would love to go back when it’s warmer and I can take the paddle board out on the lake!
reviews.author: Sofia B.

reviews.text: B27 is a really good site. Our small pop-up camper fit fine and was easy to back in and level. B27 is one of the more private sites with beautiful ferns and trees. Site can also accommodate a large tent and is similar to B loop sites 29 and 31. Lots of small campers, small RVs, and camper vans at Fairholme, despite contradictory and confusing info on the recreation website and customer service regarding trailers and campers!
reviews.author: Jill B.

reviews.text:
Choose your site carefully depending on your camping vehicle. Many of the parking areas at the sites are not level as the campground is sloped. This may not be a problem if you are tenting and just parking a car but it is more problematic with an RV. More work should be done to level the parking spots on the sites.

There are new flush toilet restrooms but sadly no showers were built in these brand new structures.
reviews.author: Donald P.

reviews.text: Very difficult to get a two night stay: we had to await release of a campsite (at exactly 7:00 AM) to get the first night, then again at 7:00 AM the next day to get the second night.
reviews.author: Alden J.

reviews.text: Must pack handsoap. No formal pad sites. Sites are very close together. Campground Loop A is portapotties but B has proper restrooms. No showers.
reviews.author: Alex S.

reviews.text: It was beautiful here, just on the lake, and the facilities were good as well. I cannot wait to book this campground again when I go back.
reviews.author: ALEXANDRIA B.

reviews.text:
This is not a great representation of the NPS. If you're just looking for a jump off point to Sol Duc entrance or even Hurricane Ridge—Elwha is closed—then go for it. We stayed in site A11. 
Pros: On a lake, some nice trees, 2 miles from Olympic entrance (NPS pass) and Olympic Discovery Trailhead (need WA pass), Most sites are shaded.
Cons:
• Connected to, but not part of the camp is a boat landing/swimming area that was packed despite warnings for swimmers itch posted, and both dog and human poop on the ground.
• The sites are on top of each other with zero privacy. Sites are not level.
• There is only one camp host (there are other host sites that just have cones in them) to serve a three-loop camp which leads to other issues including dumpsters being overloaded & trash just tossed on the ground nearby (bears?). The sites aren't being cleaned between guests, bathrooms were not cleaned during our stay. There was no soap or antiseptic. The bathrooms were filled with bugs, 1000s of bugs that swarm out of the toilet when you try to use it.
• Speaking of bathrooms...The A bathrooms are closed for repairs. That was no disclosed before we reserved the site in A loop. Probably because they have porta potties which: 1. are so full, poop is coming up OVER the toilet seat. 2. They are on a hill and urine is running out and down the road into other sites. 3. Someone notched peep holes over the end units looking at the urinal. WTF.
• Finally, there is a camp store. The store is currently cash only. Not a big deal in itself, but there are signs listing prices on things like food and ice and stickers, etc that are all wrong. So when you go to the register you get charged way more than expected. When you say, "Hey, why am I being charged so much? The sign says 'X'" the response is a shrug and a,"Whattya gonna do." Literally, pointing out that you're 20 miles away from other options, so pay the $9 for wood.
reviews.author: Ryan W.

reviews.text:
The process of getting a reservation at Fairholme by using the website recreation.gov was a nightmare.  I ended up calling them by phone and after 1 1/2 hours finally got a warm body to answer.  After reserving the site with one individual she passed me to someone else to pay for it.  Another 20 minute wait.  Also, the site map of the campground is incorrect.  I pointed this out to the two “rangers” I dealt with while staying there.  They both knew the problem but had no way of fixing it.  Half of my time spent in the campground was dealing with other campers that didn’t know about the new process and couldn’t find a ranger to deal with.
The Park Service should run, not walk to try and get their money back that they paid this contractor to set up this website.  The Park Service didn’t do the American people any favors by going with the lowest bidder on this setup.
There is a good chance I will never go to this campground again which is a real shame because I’ve always had a good time in years past.
Trying to use your recreation.gov website is like going for a colonoscopy.  Not a good time.
reviews.author: Jerry F.

reviews.text: DO NOT book this walk-in site or the sites left and right of this site, the entire site(s) is on a rather steep slope (for a camp site)! There is zero flat area for a tent, seriously uncomfortable. The photo of the lake is accurate and as pretty in person, that is the only nice thing about this site. Noisy is an understatement, it is a busy campground and top that off with hearing every car pass by on the 101 24/7 and headlights shining from across the way. Our trip was amazing and wonderful until this camp site tarnished the adventure. They work hard to keep the restrooms clean; again a busy campground and the 100s of guests aren’t always tidy and supplies do run out. The site is compact and no area for a tent to be a safe distance from the fire pit. The walk-in in portion had a few ways into the site and were simple yet steep. Everything you use must be hauled back to your car or use a community bear box with your bear containers. The Rangers are super kind and helpful.
reviews.author: Stephanie S.

reviews.text:
I was very disappointed the photos/map/description for this site state it's a drive through campsite. That being said i was expecting the campground to be a one-way loop, as it was... someone had moved the cement table into the middle of the drive through preventing any easy access. we had to go wrong way through the campground to back our 16ft trailer into the spot. some spots are level and some are total slope, hit or miss what you get when you've never seen it before. this spot was not terrible but had a slope. 
I wouldn't have cared as much but being a "national park" 80% of the people visiting were rude and acted very entitled towards camping spots. I have traveled through many states and almost every national park in the central/ western states and this park by far was the rudes people i have met, let alone the park itself is not worth the drive. 
We were suppose to stay 2 nights however it turns out the trip was a bust.
reviews.author: Rachel H.

reviews.text: The campground and bathrooms are clean. Water spigots are conveniently located throughout, plus some outside the toilet building. The lake is very beautiful with clear aqua water. Food lockers to discourage bears are plentiful but I did not see anyone use them. There were people who kept their food coolers out all day and overnight.  While the lake  is pretty, it is anything but serene. There is a very busy highway that runs along the lake. The traffic noise is very loud and I found it disturbing. My campsite was a walk-to that was along the lake's edge. The campsites here are quite small and so close to one another your tents are practically on top of each other. I had to wear earplugs to sleep because the traffic sound so so loud and the next tent had a snoring person in it. The lake is worth a visit, but I do not recommend camping here if you like peaceful settings with even a modicum of privacy.
reviews.author: Laurie C.

reviews.text:
Someone stole the spot that the friends of my son had reserved. The host told them they could have another site that was supposed to be empty but someone had stolen that site too!!! The site they were finally given was extremely tiny compared to the one they had originally reserved. 

The "neighbors" at the site above us were EXTREMELY loud, talking and laughing at the tops of their voices, until well after midnight, even though quiet time starts at 10. They also ran a very loud generator for about 4 hours a day! And to top it off, they had a large campfire even though there was a burn ban on. The guy was very aggressive when I told him that there was a burn ban on. I finally had to make a complaint with a Ranger. Why are there even hosts when they can't do anything about noise or stolen reserved spots?!!
reviews.author: Cynthia M.

reviews.text: I booked this so we could ride the Olympic Discovery trail sections on the north side of Crescent Lake because our previous experiences had been stressful drives on 101 on the south side of the lake. I didn't realize that our campsite had a view of logging trucks on 101 and loud vehicle sounds and lights during the night. This is obviously not the campground or NPS' fault,  but my own miscalculation. The campground itself was well maintained and everything went very well... except being woken in the night by lights and horns that made it sound as if - as I could hear the person in the next site remark - "I thought a train was going to hit our tent." The lake itself is stunning. The store is a fun amenity. The Olympic Discovery Trail could use a whole lot more signage, but was fabulous once located.
reviews.author: M M.

reviews.text: This might not *technically* be rainforest but it seems like the lines are fairly blurred on the penninsula for what is and isn't rainforest because we visited some rainforests and this really seemed like one to me. Altitude is higher though than Hoh, Sol Duc, Kalaloch, and Mora though so it was very cold at night. Our site was pretty far from the bathroom and walking through the forested path through the campground to get there in the middle of the night felt kind of spooky. Lots of ravens and interesting mosses and fungi. Fire will be a challenge due to the wetness. Like all the other campgrounds we stayed at in Olympic, soap, paper towels, firewood, and staff all hard to find. Still very lovely and I'm glad to have had the opportunity to stay here.
reviews.author: Margot F.

reviews.text:
Site 83 is beautiful and next to the lake. It is shaded, which is nice for hot days. You are right next to a little beach, so you can easily launch from there. The only thing to consider is the site is slanted, so we could not lay flat. The ground is so slanted, things kept rolling down the table. The picnic table looks really old, but served its purpose.

The site is close to the potable water spigot, only a walk up. You have to hike down a bit to get to the site from the parking lot. You have to hike up to the bathroom, but we were not bothered by this.

I have Tmobile and I had about 1-2 bars and 5G the whole time.
reviews.author: Maria M.

reviews.text: Campground location is convenient for visiting Lake Crescent, Sol Duc Falls area, Mount Storm King, and Port Angeles. The walk in campsites do have access to a reserved park spot, shared bear boxes, and water spigots. However, they are kind of far from the nearest bathroom. Walk in sites have a slight grade, but not enough to make it uncomfortable. Site 81 does have a partial lake view. Not much privacy from neighboring sites but still overall a great site. You do hear the traffic from the highway during the day but overnight the roadway isn't very busy.
reviews.author: Cameron P.

reviews.text:
Campground is great. Lake and docks are within an easy stroll. Bathrooms are clean; no showers, but flush toilets. 

This campsite was a short, steep walk-to from parking (<50ft). Small, shared bear box was available a short walk away. Campsite overlooks the lake through a few trees and is very shady and level.

The only reason I couldn't rate it 5 stars is due to the amount of road noise from across the lake. Thankfully, it does ease off later at night, but I wouldn't say this site qualified as "quiet". Still peaceful overall, though.
reviews.author: Rachel S.

reviews.text: I was camping at site 83 and I would have to say it's one of the best site there right on the edge of lake. It would have been nicer if it was flatter but it was acceptable. Also, there was s food storage box right on the site as well. It's a bit of walk but for the scenery you get, I didn't mind it at all. Also, very close to the general store and boat launch so if you are planning on going into water, it's probably the best one on the campground. Overall, very happy with my stay.
reviews.author: John K.

reviews.text: Easy access right off 101 at the tip of Crescent Lake. Small campsites with some located on an incline. Arrived while one of the restrooms was under construction for maintenance, but luckily did not feel crowded in the remaining restrooms. Potable water was clean and fresh tasting. Lack of shower facilities was less of an inconvenience than expected. The noise of traffic through the day and night was much louder than expected.
reviews.author: Lisa K.

reviews.text: Very nice campground on Lake Crescent.  Site 27 was okay for our 26 ft Airstream and Ford F150. Need to back to the passenger side to allow more room.  Nice picnic area above the site.  Near a nice bike path that was an old RR track. Good base camp to get into the west side of Olympic National Park.  Go to “Hole in the Wall” trail, and  beach #4.  Ruby Beach is very crowded.
reviews.author: Dennis F.

reviews.text: Noise from 101 kept us both from sleep on night one, even though we had a campsite further in, the logging trucks are constant, but erratic and very loud.  Night two ear plugs (the kind provided on international flights) helped. But wouldn’t bother camping here again. Site was also barely big enough for our vehicle, tent and kitchen tent; our van is only 12 ft long.
reviews.author: Craig J.

reviews.text: What a beautiful campground! Fairholme is situated in a lush, green forest on the shores of Lake Crescent, which provide a stunning landscape to camp in. The amenities are great and the campsites are well-spaced and well-sized. Only downside for me was the nearby US101: I was awoken frequently throughout the night by cars driving by Lake Crescent.
reviews.author: Paul F.

reviews.text: Overall a great campsite right on the edge of the lake. Was able to fit two 4-person tents with plenty of space to walk around. Only had neighbors on the right side (site 89). There is a site right above this one that has a clear view down. The walk to the bathrooms and car is a little steep. There was no food storage box for this site.
reviews.author: Elma H.

reviews.text: This is a great campground with easy access to Lake Crescent for watersports, the Spruce Railroad Trail for bicycling or walking, and myriad of hiking opportunities within a few miles.  Since this campground is across the lake from Hwy 101 you will hear traffic; if camping a tent you may sleep better with ear plugs.
reviews.author: Colin F.

reviews.text: This not actually a level site for a van— the pull-through would probably work better for a small trailer that has some jacks to level it, but then also the rest of the site is above the trailer, it's a bit awkward. So, maybe this would just be a better tent site. I would not take this site again for our camper van.
reviews.author: Knox G.

reviews.text: Nice walk-in spot right on the water. Only downside is there's very little room for a tent and only a small one at that. The only reasonably flat-ish spot was right next to the trail. If you've got a one or two person backpacking tent you could fit but there really isn't space for anything bigger than that.
reviews.author: Marie B.

reviews.text:
The walk-to site I unfortunately reserved was really bad, because it was tiny and everybody walks right past/thru your site to access the other lakeshore sites or the lake itself. The site next door is so close you can hear your neighbors pass gas as they take a leak in the lake.

Be warned!
reviews.author: stephen m.

reviews.text: great pull through spot, all the other sites you have to reverse in and out. Good space for a bigger tent, but the ground is a little hard for the stakes. Other than that it's a very beautiful and green spot with a good amount of privacy. Super dark walk to the restroom.
reviews.author: Edaena G.

reviews.text: Lovely forested campsite about 30-45 minutes away from Storm King and Sol Duc trailheads. Not the most privacy I've had at a site, and the bathrooms were busy due to the number of sites they serve but there was a nice beach/dock area nearby to sit and watch the lake.
reviews.author: Joelle S.

reviews.text: Sites 90 and all the 80s are stunning waterfront walk-in sites (2 min) with incredible scenery. We had 88, which was flat and amazing. Some have angled tent pads. Noise from the highway wasn’t ideal, but the beauty made up for it. I would return in a heartbeat.
reviews.author: Lissa E.

reviews.text: The campground was great and the lake is just breathtaking. Sadly, our neighbors pulled into the spot at 11pm and stayed up drinking and partying until 3am. We didn't get good sleep, but that was only because of our neighbors and not the site itself!
reviews.author: Collin J.

reviews.text:
This is a lovey campground in a treed forested area on a lake. Nice to walk around with dogs. It is set into a hill and some of the spots are quite small.
I got lucky and my 18’ trailer fit fine, was pretty level.
Bathrooms were very clean
reviews.author: Jacqueline  M.

reviews.text: Being on the water absolutely made the steep hike to and from the bathroom worth it. We have a wagon which made trips to and from the car much easier and I couldn’t imagine camping here without it.
reviews.author: Rebecca P.

reviews.text: The campground is beautiful and well maintained. Very close to the water so you can walk out to the shore on there is a small dock. Bathrooms are well kept. We had a great experience!
reviews.author: Morgan R.

reviews.text: Great spot!! Just be hesitant with any of the lower waterfront spots, it is quite a walk and hilly if you have lots of gear or can't get around well. Beautiful quiet campground.
reviews.author: Lindsay B.

reviews.text: fairholme campground was really nice. the campsites and bathrooms were clean. and of course, crescent lake is beautiful!
reviews.author: erin p.

reviews.text: Amazing campground setting, lots of privacy, very easily oriented for shared bathrooms, trash disposal, etc.
reviews.author: Genevieve A.

reviews.text: Big campsite, can fit a 9x14 tent easily. Conveniently located near bathroom, but without too much noise.
reviews.author: Quoc T.

reviews.text: Someone was in my tent site when I arrived even though we reserved the site
reviews.author: Mannika K.

reviews.text: This campground is so beautiful, well spread out and bathrooms are clean
reviews.author: Megan P.

reviews.text: Great campsite with awesome views and good facilities.
reviews.author: Phillip A.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground and lake.  Some traffic noise.
reviews.author: Douglas C.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground. No cell service.
reviews.author: Leah C.

reviews.text: Very close to neighbors
reviews.author: Claudio G.

reviews.text: This is an incredibly busy campground in the summer with people loudly enjoying outdoor movies outside their giant RVs, projecting LED lights into the surrounding trees (obscuring the stars and setting moon), and drunkenly playing "Never Have I Ever" at top volume. Basic campground etiquette appeared to be a foreign concept to the vast majority of campers, and the number of campfires merrily dancing during a total burn ban smacked of the self-centered entitlement of FOMO fueled, social-media-obsessed 'campers' that seem to have taken over natural spaces over the past years. Why so many people drive many hours to the edge of a wilderness coast full of beauty and natural history to blast Ariana Grande and never look up from their red solo cups is astounding.
reviews.author: Zowie A.

reviews.text:
I have been camping at Kalaloch my whole life and this year has been on of the worst years!  Between the Rangers and camp hosts patrolling the campground for violations and not maintaining the campground it’s not a the great place it used to be!
The website never mentioned that the bathroom by E loop was being remodeled (the whole week were there not on person was working on it.) This was my childhood favorite place and the last few years it hasn’t even remotely been the same.  The Park Rangers need to go back to educating and being their for people not jus Law Enforcement!!
reviews.author: Kerry B.

reviews.text: As always, Kaloach is a magical place and we love to visit here. However, the Campground host, Gene makes the magic disappear. As we were told by the rangers, we are not the first ones to have issues with him and he seems to get many complaints. Without going into detail we felt like we were somewhat targeted by him and had to get the rangers involved for him to back off and leave us alone. The other campground host was great and we highly recommend talking to him or the rangers instead of Gene.
reviews.author: Rachel E.

reviews.text: Kalaloch is a beautiful place to walk the beach and look at tidal pools during low tide.  There were three problems I noted during my recent stay.  The first and most serious was the terrible condition of the restrooms in the campground.  There was no soap.  There was filth, everywhere.  The smell was overpowering.  Granted, they need to be completely redone (the facilities are beyond repair) but still, they could have installed some soap dispensers and cleaned them once in a while.  The second problem was that Kalaloch suffers from what I call "Washington dog owner carelessness" and by that I mean well over half of the visitors to the place bring their dogs and many do not use leashes despite the requirement.  They're running amok on the beach and cause a distraction to what would otherwise be a great experience.  Finally, despite the clearly labeled "no campfires on the beach" signs, there were multiple groups with campfires on the beach, some of them quite large, and no visible enforcement of the rules.  Despite these shortcomings, we had a wonderful time and I'd encourage people to visit.  But...Kalaloch needs to know that they can improve, particularly by putting soap in restrooms.
reviews.author: David W.

reviews.text: While the locale was amazing as a whole, and the beach was absolutely picturesque, the camp host was so overbearing, exacting, fussy and belligerent, we left disappointed and unsure about a return trip. This host was working overtime to ensure every possible minute guideline was being followed, in many cases exceeding and overriding not only the printed rules and regulations, but also the park rangers themselves. It was beyond frustrating to deal with, and ultimately left a bad taste in our mouths overall. Think twice before camping in a spot at the campground.
reviews.author: SHANE R.

reviews.text: Great place to camp. Near Ruby beach and more. Sounds of the ocean put me to sleep. Great staff...very clean.
reviews.author: John D.

reviews.text: This site (A13) is one of the more spacious sites with an ocean view. The double driveway was able to fit two pickups plus my Aliner trailer. Sites vary greatly and I would not camp here in a site on the road- the log trucks are unbearable. 4 stars because the bathrooms are not good. The one closest to us was in disrepair with only one working stall so there was always a line. No soap (as usual) and the dryer didn’t work. There was no tp for a day and a half. Overall a beautiful campground and beach but camping is a bit rough due to weather (hope for sun), wind (comes with the view sites) and sand. Shout out to ranger Janet Jackson who got our friends a site last minute and took no bull from anybody.
reviews.author: Shelly M.

reviews.text: Great place to camp! It was quiet, clean, and excellently located if you want to explore all the beaches nearby. Our site was great, too!
