It was in the perfect location where we were adequately blocked by trees and bushes so you couldn't see other campsites as much. We were so close to the bathrooms and the beach, both! We did notice that not all the sites were like this and some were either right next to each other or were easily visible through the trees. I wouldn't put much stock in trying to get beach view sites. They were teeny!
reviews.author: Keegan R.

reviews.text: Unless you get the very best of sites, I’d recommend skipping this campground. The sites next to the road are incredibly noisy, with trucks traveling on 101 at near highway speeds. The ones next to the ocean are quiet, but not the one we had in the back. Otherwise site was beautiful, bathrooms were clean, and accessibility to the beach was great.
reviews.author: Christy D.

reviews.text: A027 must be one of the best campsites here. Totally private. The ocean is so loud, you can't hear any other people. There's a big tree on the campsite, which you can climb for a great sunset view. The trail to the beach is just one campsite away to the south.
reviews.author: Alex P.

reviews.text: We had a private site with a view of the water. It was a short walk to the beach and our boys loved playing in the wooded area. Sites along the road looked less desirable.
reviews.author: Corrinne H.

reviews.text: Campsite is right next to the road, where large trucks pass at high speeds. It would shake our entire tent and kept us up all night,
reviews.author: Lynda J.

reviews.text: Get used to the reservation system.
reviews.author: James W.

reviews.text: This was our first campground during our PCH road trip, and we did tent camping at A048. This campground was nice and the campsite was pretty spacious. It wasn't the biggest site we've stayed at and we did have neighbors on both sides, but we still had room to move around quite a bit and it was blocked by enough vegetation to provide some privacy. We booked around 2 months in advance and really wished we could have had a beach view, but the website would not let us reserve those spots for some reason. However, we had a lot of beautiful tree coverage, which was nice because it was still in Washington's rainy season. We loved that it was right next to the beach and not far from a lot of places we wanted to go to (i.e. Tree of Life, Ruby Beach, Hoh Rainforest, Big Cedar Tree, etc.). The people were polite, the bathrooms were clean, and they had a pump with drinking water at the beginning of the loop. I thought this location had showers, but we were not able to locate them (we didn't look very hard because we got in late and left early). I wish we could have had more time here.
reviews.author: Katarina V.

reviews.text:
These sites are somewhat small and compact, but they're clean and the area is very nice. Good bathroom facilities and water spigots.

Our site specifically (A008) had a broken grill on the fire-ring, which was inconvenient but ultimately we were able to make it work. The canopy protects pretty well from light rain, and overall the area is damp, so it stays nice and cool. Be sure however to bring kindling wood or a firestarter if you plan on burning wood. Additionally, consider having a good means to pound stakes into the ground, which was mostly embedded with lots of small gravel and dense earth.

The sites also have great access to the beach; our site was maybe 150ft from the beach entrance, and many of the sites even overlook the beach, which I would highly recommend if you can get them.

Finally, there were a lot of families and the campground seems very popular in the summertime, so if you're looking for a bit more privacy this isn't the best choice, however everyone was overall very polite and respected quiet hours and their neighbors well.
reviews.author: Alexander S.

reviews.text:
Kalaloch has been my favorite place to camp since I first encountered it 56 years ago.  Lots of years tenting and many more trailering.  
The beach is miles long with no vehicles, huge driftwood logs, clean sand.  At low tide you can explore tide pools around huge rocks that are submerged at high to medium tides.  Eagles are seen multiple time a day, and this trip we saw three gray whales cavorting near the shore one morning.
Every site has a campfire ring and several have spectacular ocean views.  There were at least as many tents as RV's this trip.  
Kalaloch is about 40 miles from the fascinating moss-covered Hoh Rain Forest and 70 miles from beautiful Lake Crescent.  35 miles the other direction is Lake Quinault.  Kalaloch, Lake Crescent and Lake Quinault all have old-style timber lodges with rooms for rent, and each lodge has a decent sit-down restaurant.
Plan several days.  If Kalaloch isn't on your bucket list it should be.
reviews.author: Gary D.

reviews.text:
The campground itself is very basic, and wedged between busy US Hwy 101 and cliffs that provide minimal views of the ocean due to shrub and tree growth.  Although you can't see the ocean from most of the CG unless you have one of the very few view sites, you can hear the ocean when not drowned out by logging trucks and other traffic on 101.  There are a few paths down to the ocean and beach which, in this stretch, is fairly unremarkable but easily walked at lower tides.  The campground does provide a launch pad for driving to other beaches which are more interesting and fun.
Very limited fresh water sources in the CG.  Dump station requires RV's driving through much of the CG (both going and coming on single road) to the "pleasure" of campers on that road.  Limited restrooms.
reviews.author: Frank P.

reviews.text: The Kalaloch Campground is ideally situated on the Washington Coast with easy access to the Hoh Rain Forest, Lake Quinalt and the most stunning beaches. The campground has potable water, restrooms, and firepits. Unfortunately, most of the campsites are built for cars with big cement slabs and the firepits are placed without thought for where a tent should go. We had a campsite along the edge of the water but no view due to lots of shrubs, and we had to push our tent into the bushes to get it set up. There are only a handful of sites that really work well for tents and only a couple of them with views. Getting a reservation here is almost impossible and after 3 years of trying it was a bit of a disappointment.
reviews.author: Blair d.

reviews.text: Hard to reserve, but worth the effort.  Lots of tree cover, so solar was not working the entire time.  Cool temperature on the coast when inland was 100.  A bit too close to the 101 for my taste, traffic noise is very noticeable at 0600.  Obviously the sights overlooking the cliff are the best, and the most difficult to reserve.  Smaller is better here, large RV and rigs just won't fit in many spots.  Very disappointed in the lodge next door.  Walking there requires you to walk on the 101 hyway shoulder.  With children 1-10 this is a heart pounding effort trying to keep them clear of speeding traffic and large trucks driving south.  A protected pedestrian section would be helpful.
reviews.author: Daniel B.

reviews.text:
While I understand that the campground just opened, I feel there was enough time to prepare the restrooms with soap and/or hand sanitizer dispensers, as well as paper towels. Also, I don’t understand why NP campgrounds inside the parks don’t all provide coin operated shower facilities! We had to go to National Forest campground in the area to shower. We are visiting many NP’s this summer- some have great restroom /shower facilities within the park and others don’t. This needs to be a priority in the future.  
As for the campground itself, I love the location and the sites themselves! Enjoyed the Park immensely!
reviews.author: Nicholas Z.

reviews.text: This area is spectacularly beautiful, with the beach and the forest. But the site we reserved was pretty bad. It was the last one available so we didn’t have a choice. Site 069; it was right by the bathrooms and garbage dumpsters, so the smell was pretty bad. And highway noise, including loud logging trucks, kept us up at night. The sites along the bluff are amazing and you’d be lucky to snag one! I’d go back if I can manage to reserve a site away from the highway. Very busy when we went in August, and every spot was taken. I wouldn’t chance going without a reservation!
reviews.author: Shannon W.

reviews.text: Kalaloch campground along the coast of Olympic National Park was very enjoyable.  Beach walks at Ruby Beach and Beach 4 north of the campground are not to be missed.  The coastal geology is most educational.  The NPS does a nice job with the placement of waysides to explain what one is looking at.  The restrooms at Kalaloch were the BEST and cleanest I’ve seen in a month of travels through the park system.  Understand the restrooms where recently renovated.  Thank you NPS!
reviews.author: Christopher S.

reviews.text:
This is a very quiet campground, with lots of trees and shrubs to create nice campsites. The access to the beach is quick and easy. The toilets were clean, the whole campground is free of trash and debris, very pleasant to walk about.
The RV dump costs $10, $5 for seniors. There is a tiny convenience store at the nearby Kalaloch Lodge, as well as a restaurant and a souvenir shop featuring artwork by local tribal members.
reviews.author: Magdalena B.

reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay at Kalaloch campground which is right off the beach. Beach can be windy and cold even in summer but the campground is tucked in and protected except for the sites adjacent to the beach. Sites are quite close to each other and that’s what you can expect from a popular campground. Nice place to go with a group of families. Kids can bike around and play on the beach. Host was amazing!
reviews.author: Shalena S.

reviews.text: Too many dogs. Dog barking woke me up every morning and dogs were not on leases on the beach. Over four days trying to watch birds, the dogs were always interfering. I went to Ruby beach low tide only to be greeted by a unleashed Doberman pincher at the top of the trail, it scared and angered me. Not what I want to experience after this early morning outing!
reviews.author: Pam  B.

reviews.text: Campsites were clean and well maintained, close together but still gave you plenty of privacy. Nature walking trail across the street was mindblowingly beautiful, the walk along the shore to the incredible Tree of Life was also beautiful. meditating on the beach was so peaceful. CANT WAIT TO COME BACK !!
reviews.author: Randi J.

reviews.text: This is hands down one of the best campgrounds I’ve ever stayed at! We loved it so much, we came back a week later and took our chances on a waitlist! Site 11 was perfection- spacious, water views, a little path to enjoy beach view, etc. Can’t wait to come back some day!
reviews.author: Jennifer  P.

reviews.text: This campsite was amazing! What more could one need? You have the beautiful ocean, the clean air, and a billion stars above. Relax with the sound of the waves crashing, while hearing the wood in the fire pit crackle. This place is magical.
reviews.author: Teresa B.

reviews.text: The location was perfect, loved hearing the sound of the waves all night. The sites were clean and nicely spaced. It was a wonderful experience for me and my family.
reviews.author: Malisa  A.

reviews.text: The campground is great, with amazing views and clean toilets but D038 is not the best spot. It's actually half the size of a regular one, squeezed in the space.
reviews.author: Adriana G.

reviews.text: Kalaloch is my favorite campsite in all of Washington.  Sure, it's not as fancy as a lot of campgrounds, but the location can't be beat.
reviews.author: Lance S.

reviews.text: Absolutely terrible, nothing like sleeping 5 feet away from the constant roar of diesel trucks. This is not camping. Awful experience.
reviews.author: Nicholas  R.

reviews.text: Great campsite location, close to beach access and short walk from toilets. No soap in the restrooms.
reviews.author: Camilla C.

reviews.text: Site F002 was good location but short and skinny. We found it very private.  The map indicates it is on the shoreline but there is no view due to vegetation.  The walkway access to the beach is near the overflow lot. Easy walk down to beach where we saw lots of interesting things.   I parked the truck sideways in front of trailer to fit in.  Got a note on my windshield from our host that I had to move to the overflow lot.  Walking around the campground I saw at least 10 other tow vehicles which had also parked in front of their trailers as I did.  I was the only one with a note I could see and the only one who moved to the overflow lot.  GRRRR but ok.  This campground is shady.  Not enough sun to keep batteries charged with solar. The bathrooms were clean and had running water.  Also used the dump station once, which was easy access. You will need to exit by driving through loop D of campground to turnaround.  There was also a fresh water fill past the dump station at a safe distance from the dump.  It was great to see the fresh water was not right next to the dump station. In all we had an enjoyable visit and I would return here. Ruby Beach was the highlight of our adventures here.  We went twice at low tide and once at high tide.  Lots of ocean life like starfish to see here.  I understand the access to Ruby is closing July 2022.  Try to schedule your visit to avoid this closure.  We also went to the Hoh Rainforest one day.  Make sure to take your rain gear up there.  Stop at the little store/cafe on the way up.  It is an interesting  visit.  They serve a great breakfast.  We enjoyed the morning hikes at Hoh.  The afternoon got very crowded.
reviews.author: Rand C.

reviews.text: Coming from East Los Angeles, I wasn’t sure what to expect from Kalaloch. But my expectations were surpassed. This campground was so close to the beach, just a couple minutes walking distance. Not only that, but the restrooms were fairly close to my campsite, which was C002. The one thing that made me give 4 stars instead of 5 was that the campgrounds were fairly close to one another. I would have wanted some more privacy with my fiancé, especially with the lady adjacent from us who who had a dog that wouldn’t stop barking. All. Day. Long. And not only that, all we could hear he say was “BARKELY, STOP BARKING.” Maybe she shouldn’t have named her dog BARKley. So it was her dog barking and her barking as well. Other than that the Kalaloch campground was one I won’t forget about. It was very fun and a great memorable experience. I won’t ever forget it. Additionally I would like to add that the atmosphere here in Kalaloch is majestic. The lush trees and bright green atmosphere felt something out of a fairytale. No pictures, videos, or any online images with do this place justice. You just have to experience it for yourself. That being said… Kalaloch, until we meet again. ;)
reviews.author: Abraxaz S.

reviews.text: Kalaloch has always been the most wonderful place! This visit was no exception as we had amazing weather the whole time we were there. Just a few things to note. The bathroom near the E loop is under construction. So there is one bathroom for D,E and F!  The whole week we were there, there appeared to be no urgency to get the project done. The construction crew was there only a few times for a few hours. The bathrooms were kept clean but there were no modifications made for the Pandemic ( no soap provided-they are still using the cold hand dryers??? - some parks have discontinued the use of them because of spreading the virus through air) Sometimes you had to wait in line for the bathroom:<(     The grate on our firepit was missing, the kind ranger said  they had some, and the only maintenance man on staff would try to find the time to bring it to us. the week went by and it never arrived. Not sure if these issues are federal funding problems or what? All that said, Kalaloch is a magical place -our family has been every summer for decades :)
reviews.author: Jennifer  M.

reviews.text:
Very peaceful and relaxing. The individual campsites have a fair distance between for good separation between campsites, they are tidy and well cared for, the fire pits are in good shape with a grate, and bathrooms are fairly close, clean, well kept and orderly.  Nearly all sites are in shade not all sites near the bluff have a view of the ocean so you'l want to make sure you have that in your reserved site if you are expecting it. 
The beach was vast, clear, smooth, free of debris and trash of any kind, and sprawling for miles. We thoroughly enjoyed our 3 night trip. The shade areas really did cool off the sun in the campground. The campground overseer or caretaker was very pleasant and good spirited. We really enjoyed our time speaking with him about the area.  Keep up the good work park services!
reviews.author: Brian R.

reviews.text: Well-maintained campground that was surprisingly not as busy considering how popular the Kaloloch beach area can be (granted this was a trip during the week). Easy to find and navigate campground, host is right at the entrance (easy to find), plenty of facilities and trash dumpsters. Wild animals are not an issue, but I wouldn't just leave things lying around either. Easy beach access (3-minute walk from any campsite tops). One downside for some people is that many campsites are across the road from another, so there is not much privacy. You often have to parallel park at most sites though, so you can use this as a bit of a wall. Does get chilly once the sun goes down, even in the summer. Bugs not too bad.
reviews.author: Bryan G.

reviews.text: We had a wonderful stay at southbeach.  We had reservations at Kalaloch but had a great water site at South Beach and decided not to move.  The camp host at South Beach are the best.  They are golden in everything they do.  So many friendly people there. I'm sad to hear South beach may go to reservations.  We drove thru the main park and saw so many no shows and prime sites sat open for days. You need to fix your reservation cancels.  I received a conformation 1 week ahead of our reservations, you need a confirmation reply button so people and say yay or ney if they are coming.  It was hard to see people turn away when spots were left open. Kalaloch is the best have been coming for years. Be back soon.
reviews.author: Fred A.

reviews.text: A peekaboo view of the water and a great spot to rest between Olympic adventures. The water spigot close to this spot wasn’t in service when I was there (6/26). The ladies room close to A011 was down to one stall. The next bathroom block had 3 stalls and the heat was working. There are no showers at this location- closest are Queets trading post or Bogachiel state park- if you opt for Bogachiel you need to have a Discovery Pass. There wasn’t a way to organize one on site. Sites on the bluff can be very windy! But the beach is a lovely sandy beach and is home to the Tree of Life. It’s not giving up!
reviews.author: Deena M.

reviews.text: Beautiful experience for me! My campsite was spacious and allowed for my brother's family to tent with room for my RV. The younger boys had so much fun exploring the beaches and trails. I have limits on my mobility but was still able to easily view the beach from the trail top and even got down and back up the beach stairs once (with help). Although the camp ground was full, the beaches never seemed crowded and the Rangers and Hosts were always friendly and helpful. Loved that there were no vehicles racing up and down the beach. Relieved a lot of worry while the kids were playing in the sand.
reviews.author: Barbara C.

reviews.text: We had a full beach view, which was beautiful. There was limited shade at our site, but enough to get by. Many of the sites have excellent shade, but don't expect any given site to have good shade: If you plan to park a vehicle midday in the summer, make sure there is nothing heat sensitive or it may cook, even if the outdoor air temperature is in the 70's. The other campers were a little loud, opening and closing car doors well past 10 pm, but other than that, the ocean provides almost perfect white noise. We plan on returning to Olympic national park largely because of this campground!
reviews.author: Jonathon K.

reviews.text: We had a wonderful stay at the Kalaloch camp ground.  So beautiful as always.  We also spent 2 days at South beach.  The camp host in both locations were amazing.  John and Denise at South Beach are the best.  The campground was very well kept.  There were fisherman that left a mess, so bad no one would want to camp in that spot because of the smell and mess.  John and Denise got right on it with help of the rangers and was brought right up to specs.   They handle things very professional.  You are blessed to have the wonderful host.  We will be back.
reviews.author: Fred A.

reviews.text: The location is convenient, easy to get to beach and restrooms. The campground was clean, bathrooms too. The four stars come from the location, convenience, and general cleanliness.  The convenience and proximity to bathroom and beach trail is what makes this particular site. Be warned this particular site doesn’t have a good space for a tent a safe distance from the fire pit. Parking was tight for a Toyota Corolla. Spaces are close together. There is noise throughout the day, includes screams kiddos.  Quiet after everyone goes to sleep.
reviews.author: Stephanie S.

reviews.text:
Kalaloch Campground was beautiful!  Bathrooms were clean as was the campground in general.  Just a couple of suggestions.  The campsite was good but it was obvious that previous campers had driven off the pavement as there were tire tracks in the wet ground.  It would have been nice it if the space were raked or something to remove those before we arrived.  Also, the table was at quite a slant and the space seemed to have better possible locations for it.  

Appreciate all the park hosts do for a great camping experience!  Thank you.
reviews.author: Mary K.

reviews.text: By chance we got the booking when someone cancelled one night before and we got it in the A loop which was an amazing spot to be in, the spot was clean, bathrooms were near and clean, the ocean sound at night is amazing, you have neighbors camping all around so you dont feel alone even though you have a private spot. Its an amazing setting, parking with the spot, a private fire pit and picnic table. We were camping the first time and never had a single issue during our stay. Will start coming here every year.
reviews.author: Ali H.

reviews.text:
We stayed at the Kalaloch Campground, site C005. This site is in the forest, so it has plenty of shade and wasn’t too windy. There was a bit of highway noise, though. There’s no view of the coast from the site, but it isn’t a long walk to the beach. This site was close to the bathroom, but it wasn’t too noisy.

I strongly recommend trying to get to beach 4 (3 miles north of here) at low tide. It’s a bit of a scramble to get to the bottom, but this is a good rocky beach for tide pool viewing.
reviews.author: Jeremy S.

reviews.text: we absolutely loved this campground!! the bathrooms were some of the cleanest i’ve seen at campgrounds i’ve been to. it was amazing to be staying just steps from the tree of life (must see) and the beach was so beautiful. we stayed in the D loop at site 34 and it was perfect. it is set back from the bluff but you can still see the ocean from it, much less windy than the sites right on the bluff and felt spaced out enough from the neighbors to have a little privacy.
reviews.author: amanda r.

reviews.text: This year this campground was quite a bit noisier that in years past.  That's find during the day but we had to remind folks of quiet hours and twice we were awakened in the middle of the night by a screaming child.  Perhaps a little more notification about quiet hours would be helpful.  We love camping here and have done so over the 4th for 8 years now.  We will be back and hope maybe some of the campers next year will be a bit more considerate.
reviews.author: Marsha K.

reviews.text: Very nice visit, bathrooms were spotless, campground clean. GOOD LUCK getting the camp site you want., it took me weeks...spaces go in less than a second after being released, I reserved one spot and seconds later received a message letting me know that the space was no longer available due to high demand???  I would like to see a little more transparency within the Recreation.gov reservation system.
reviews.author: THOMAS Q.

reviews.text: We arrived to find the camp site we specifically chose multiple weeks ahead was taken. We wanted to camp on the water and celebrate my partners birthday. Unfortunately we were directed to a much larger site that wasn’t directly on the water.  This delayed us about an hour and we lost sunlight fast. Had to setup camp in the dark, and the firepit we were given had trash and debris in it. To make it up to is the camp host said we could stay as long as we wanted? But we work regular jobs and just wanted to camp on the water one night to escape our chaotic lives. Overall disappointed with organization and would not return. We don’t have a lot of money so it’s pretty upsetting when these small luxuries don’t work out. Thanks for reaching out to hear about it.
reviews.author: Sydney S.

reviews.text:
You don’t get 4 reserved parking spaces, you get 4 passes and hope your guests can find parking. That was extremely disappointing as I booked the site only because the reservation said we would get 4 reserved spots. There are also no signs pointing you to the reserved day use area, we drove around for 20 minutes before we found it. 

The pavilion was beautiful however and worked well for the birthday party we planned.
reviews.author: Megan R.

reviews.text:
The day use area is swamped.  One can tell that the area is boing 'loved to death'. We counted 65 rafts on the lake at one time on a Friday.  The attendants were available and prompt.  Restrooms cleanish.  Why don't campgrounds sell wood anymore?  Thank goodness there was running water.
Beautiful area and the sites are big enough that you can hear your neighbors, but not see them.  The campers are not all 'real campers'.  For example, playing music and being quite loud with their conversations.  City recreationists.
reviews.author: Elizabeth L.

reviews.text: Great campground, lots of natural space between sites.   One of the camp hosts could benefit from a 'people skills/cheerfulness' class.   One pit toilet was without odor, the other not so much.   One camper truck with house on top ran their very loud generator all night against the rules.  I think the other 4 cars stuffed into that same site had a discussion with the idiot and the next night was silence.
reviews.author: Troy B.

reviews.text: We were able to switch our reserved site for an open site (#12A) which was closer to the water. Pit toilets were clean. Nice paved parking spots on sites.Amphitheater near our site was neat.  The rain overnight gave way to amazing views of Mt Hood in the morning reflecting in Trillium Lake. This campground was well worth the stay.
reviews.author: Cal P.

reviews.text: Lovely park.  Expect a very busy visit. Day use often has a line of cars waiting for parking spots.  The campsites are kept clean.  Pit toilets are well maintained.
reviews.author: Ann K.

reviews.text: So much busier this year than in years past. Campsites were jam packed with cars and people.
reviews.author: Carrie T.

reviews.text: The campground has lost some of its charm over the years. The grounds crew who trims trees just leaves the branches and debris on the ground so you have to clean it up if it is in the way. It also seems like a massive fire hazard. The campsite itself was horribly undulated which makes putting up a tent difficult especially if you have more than one tent. Our campsite had three massive holes by the picnic table. They were fixed when we were there but only after we asked. Also, the camp host entered our campsite on more than one occasion without asking if she could come in. She should ask before entering sites.
reviews.author: Amy P.

reviews.text: I have wanted to stay here since I was a young girl. We finally snagged a spot and it was perfect. There was still a bit of snow around, but the campground was very peaceful. Spots are perfectly level and very private and the walk around the lake was beautiful and just the right amount of exercise. The views of Mount Hood are just spectacular and they park host very friendly and helpful. It was really nice being there when it was so quiet as I’m sure it gets very crowded once summer gets going.
reviews.author: Cristina S.

reviews.text: Such a beautiful lake and a nice quiet campground. I camped here with my parents and my baby who just turned 1. It was so much fun. The vault toilets were clean. The campsite we had was very private (although it was laid out weird). The roads and parking spaces are all paved which I think helped with the bugs. We brought a double kayak and spent so much time in the water. I would 100% come again.
reviews.author: Jessica  T.

reviews.text: Trillium is such a picturesque place.  We were surprised how large our campsite was, since it was the last one available when we made our reservation.
reviews.author: John S.

reviews.text: Great camp site for 2 couples and 2 tents. Had a boat and fished every day. Good fishing and ate trout daily. Some rain but didn't spoil the event.
reviews.author: Alan C.

reviews.text: One of my favorite places since I was a little girl fishing with my Grandpa- now I get to pass on these experiences to my kids!
reviews.author: Sharon M.

reviews.text: We had a great trip. Our spot was the smallest one there, but plenty of space to roam.
reviews.author: Brynna F.

reviews.text: had the perfect little wedding ceremony at trillium amphitheater. it was perfect!
reviews.author: Nicole B.

reviews.text: Even when the day-use area is busy, this campground is quiet and beautiful!
reviews.author: Cindy V.

reviews.text: Big private camp sites. Beautiful lake and view of Mt Hood.
reviews.author: Pietra W.

reviews.text:
This campground is amazing! I was very happy with my spot and the time on the lake was breathtaking! My spot was a couple deep away from the lake and I think that worked out perfectly. There is a trail that goes around the lake and if you get a spot that is as close to the lake as possible, you are basically on that trail. Being a couple spots deep felt like there was no one near us. Especially nice since you can’t hear the lake either and it can get super busy. The campsites are spaced out well and I liked that the campground has its own ramp access with parking. While we were there, there was a fire ban so unfortunately couldn’t use the very nice looking fire pit. The bathroom was pretty decent for what it is. Everything else was perfect and it was a great time!

We also went over to rent kayaks which was nice and easy. The lake wasn’t too cold so we also swam a bit in it. The only slight negative to the day use side of the lake was that there was so many influencers. It didn’t bother me much at all but it was definitely noticeable. The amazing views make sense for it as well.
reviews.author: DJ P.

reviews.text:
While the views were absolutely spectacular, the campground management was nonexistent. We stayed for 3 nights. After showing up, it rained the first night. We looked for the camp host to try and locate some firewood. We walked the ground 3 times, and all 3 hosts' sites had a sign "off duty" on them with no host in sight. We drove 20 minutes to buy some firewood.
On the second day, a host stopped by our site and asked if we needed anything. We explained what happened the night before. She apologized, said that we are lucky that our site looks the way it does because just a few weeks ago we wouldn't even be able to start a fire because our firepit was full of ashes. After that encounter, again, no host in sight for the rest of the trip.
On day 3, toilet paper ran out in all nearby bathrooms and it was clear that they stopped being cleaned on day 3 as well.
We camp a lot, this was the most poorly managed campgound I have ever stayed at in California, Oregon, or Washington states. A shame because the scenery is gorgeous.
reviews.author: Nadezhda A.

reviews.text:
We had zero issues locating the site. Basically, you just look for the boat ramp and turn left into the small parking lot. The rangers put 4 orange cones with Reserved sign in our parking spots. So super easy. Everyone after the 4th car had to look for parking on the first-come basis, which was somewhat a hassle, but doable.
The large shaded pavilion had 3 picnic tables, a couple benches and an assigned water spigot. Bathroom was nearby.
The site is not directly on the lake, the lake access is probably 20-30 yards down the path. The lake is visible from the site. A short walk away is a boat ramp which make is very convenient for putting in boards and canoes.
This day use site is way more private than the amphitheater one. People are walking by not right through the site like in the amphitheater. 
The picnic tables and benches as well as shaded area are great as well.
The only downside is limited assigned parking and no direct waterfront. So there are pluses and minuses but all in all - great experience.
reviews.author: Nadejda K.

reviews.text: We reserved a lake front tent site for end of July and it was amazing!  Literally just 50 ft from water.  The camp site has walking paths around the lake and around the campgrounds to help people get to the lake easily.  Only negative about our campsite (#6) is that there are a ton of people who walk the path around lake - and you feel a little like you’re on display when you’re hanging out at your site.  Otherwise, campsite was quiet and clean.  We took paddle boards and could drop them in super easily and really enjoyed the lake!  My son gives Trillium Lake a 9/10 for fishing opportunities.  His advice was to “get onto the water with your pole”. (Rainbow Trout).  Take the walking path and enjoy the sites around the lake.  My favorite spot is at the boat ramp and the dock area.  Stunning views.  Also make sure you check out the amphitheater!  Great swimming, fishing and weather for our trip!  Check the weather before you come- but we had highs in high 70s and lows in mid 50s—-perfect!
reviews.author: Nicole C.

reviews.text: We reserved a day use site for $80 (including fees) so that we would have a spot to be with multiple families. This charge is much more than a camping spot. We could not find the location of the day use site and walked the premise for about 2 frustrating hours, unable to find someone who worked there to help. The spot we were supposed to be at was completely on the opposite side of the part (did not follow the map on Recreation.gov at all) and our name was not posted on the site. The phone number listed on the reservation was a non-working number. There was then no parking in the day use area and the spot was supposed to come with 4 parking spaces. We were told we could go online for a refund but could not figure out how to do so. So we paid $80 for absolutely nothing and cannot get a refund. I highly advise against reserving a day use site. Rent a camp site instead, it will be cheaper and easier to find. Very frustrating, but it was a beautiful day and we made the best of it.
reviews.author: Torrey L.

reviews.text: Park host was very nice and super helpful. We stayed in site #6 on the water. The sites picnic table was broken both benches not attached at all. I had my mom with me who is disabled. Asked several park hosts and rangers for a new table. I was told that it’s the forestry department. This was a super bummer as the table could only be used to store stuff on. They did offer me another site but when I went to look at it #9 the table had holes in it. Would say the site was a bit dirty with trash but I let that go as I knew short staffing. Trillium is one of my favorite places to visit. Another disappointment was how empty the park was most nights I stayed for a week and the sign read full all but 2 nights but on any given night 6-14 were empty. The signs all said reserved. One spot was empty 3 nights. It’s a bummer they couldn’t let others stay in spots that were no shows. Over all it was a great experience. Love love Trillium.
reviews.author: Candee S.

reviews.text:
The lake and campground and hosts were great. Major complaints are the amount of dogs that are off leash mostly from the day use people walking the trail. The dogs run ahead and enter campsites while the majority of campers actually follow the rules. We had over 5 different occasions where dogs came into our site during our stay. While my own dogs were leashed in our site. Also a few campsites thought it was fine to leave their dog off leash in their site but when walking our dog leashed around the road, dogs would run out onto the road from campsite. I understand when people feel their dog is friendly and would never hurt a fly however they don’t know if the dog on leash is not as friendly or may have fear aggression, if everyone could just follow the rules it would have been more enjoyable. 
The camp hosts did the best they could to enforce the leash law but they can’t always see what is going on.
reviews.author: Shannon K.

reviews.text: We have been camping here for almost 30 years. The decline of management is concerning. We did not see ONE camp host the entire 9 days. The day use users are out of control, COMPLETELY! They are taking over every parking space at the camp side dock area, the beaches everything. It is insane! They are over taking campers on beach areas with no regard at all. There needs to be at the very least signage coming from the day use area trails into the camping area stating CAMPERS ONLY, NO DAY USE. There used to be camp hosts at least controlling this matter some what for vehicles driving into the camping side, No longer. There should also be a controlled limit of vehicles allowed to enter the day use, on weekends ESPECIALLY.  It is wrong for campers paying a good price to not even be able to have a space at the boat ramp and beach area. I really hope this gets addressed, It is out of control.
reviews.author: Diana K.

reviews.text:
When we drove up there were rangers to direct us to our campsite.  047 was a great camp spot near the boat ramp for close and easy access to carry our SUP to the lake. 
Area was clean and good size.
The night that we arrived was super cold and cloudy that hit in the low 50’s to high 30’s and unfortunately campfire was not permitted.  The next morning was clear blue sunny skies and the view of Mt Hood was breathtaking.  Saw a bald eagle the first night and the next morning as well as a Hawk.  Bathrooms are more like an outhouse, but was clean and big.  They had many throughout the campgrounds.  It didn’t seem busy, but maybe it was because it was on a cold weekend.  So it could possibly be busy on hot days.  I reserved my spot several months in advance as it gets booked fast.  Will definitely come back as I enjoyed paddling on the lake with the beautiful view.
reviews.author: Suong L.

reviews.text: We reserved spots 17, 19, 26, and 32 for us and several friends. Our friends in spot 32 moved to spot 9 because it was open and pretty much waterfront. Spots 17 & 19 were great- very large and fairly private. Lots of shade and room for several tents. Spot 19 has a large double driveway, enough for probably four vehicles. Spot 17 could house two vehicles. Spot 9 was great for the proximity to the water but not as much tent space and it was sloping down towards the lake. Spot 26 was fine, we didn’t spend much time in it. Overall a great camping experience except for the fireworks, which was annoying but not unexpected. If you get a spot near the lake and main trail, be sure to lock up your stuff. We heard someone had their hammock stolen out of spot 4, which was the spot we decided we would like next time both for size and proximity to the water.
reviews.author: Dawn S.

reviews.text: Reserved the Day Use site for an end of the school year party. There were not clear maps or signs at the entrances to the park on where we should go. We walked around and found a covered picnic shelter, but there were no signs indicating that is was the Day Use site. Another group had set up there and we talked to them about our situation - we had a reservation for a Day Use area and these seemed to be the only structure to fit the description, but they brought up it wasn't marked and couldn't be sure, so we ended up sharing it with them. The site also claimed to come with 4 parking spots, but none were available or marked as going with the Day Use area. Overall, not worth the fee - not easy to find, no ranger nearby to ask for info, not marked, not easy to get to, no clear directions for the group to find it.
reviews.author: Simone N.

reviews.text: Overall, we enjoyed our 2 night stay. It was quiet, spacious, and the outhouses seemed well maintained. Unfortunately, we had to clean up a bunch of scattered trash from the previous users before settling in.  Our first night there, all the water spigots were turned off with plastic bags wrapped around.  No one had emailed about disconnected water, so we had to go back to town to stock up on bottled water. The ranger station knew nothing about water troubles at Trillium, and they recommended we ask the camp host about it. The camp host was not in their designated campsite and was nowhere to be found. Luckily, the water came back on in the middle of our second day there. Be prepared to not have the amenities they say they'll provide...
reviews.author: Justine A.

reviews.text: This is our 3rd year of coming to Trillium Lake.  Our first time camping 2 weeks.  We were in the far end of the campground away from the water so we didn't see alot of the people that swarmed the lake over the 4th of July weekend.  But it did make it hard to find a spot to play in the water or fish because of so many people.  The hosts were great and seemed to be right on top of everything.  The bathroom by us was pretty stinky and it ran out of tp a couple times but for the most part it was ok.  My daughter, grandson and I rented kayaks one day and had a great time.  The price point was reasonable.  Fishing was good, weather was perfect.  Looking forward to next year.
reviews.author: Janice D.

reviews.text: Great time. Lake is gorgeous. Bring something to get in the water. Spot was good and with two parking areas. Lots of trees and right next to the water. The spot is in a culdesac like area of the campground with only 2 other spots. Bathrooms and water are close by. We had 3 tents and a van and ended up putting one of the tents on the end of one of the parking spots because we thought this was a better option then unlevel ground. Nice fire pit and double barbecue pit with a flat cast iron top that we grilled on multiple times. Definitely would go back.
reviews.author: aren s.

reviews.text:
We have been going to Trillium for 40 years. It saddens me to see how "overused" this lake has become. Boom boxes on paddle boards seriously?  Rentals should not be allowed. Entry to day use strictly limited. Perhaps reservations for day use like Multnomah Falls. The water in the lake was actually brown - ick. 
However, the campsite was clean and the pit toilets well maintained. Hosts should be more visible. As we were leaving at 7am one of the groups had a fire 🔥 so much for honoring our national forest!! 
Let's do better next season.
reviews.author: Jennifer N.

reviews.text: We have been going to Trillium for years and I have to say that it has gone downhill the last couple of years.  Last year our spot did not have a picnic table and this year the picnic table was unsafe to sit on.  There used to be a nice trail around the lake and now you can’t use it.  It seems to me you have more visitors than ever but absolutely no upkeep.  The camp hosts don’t even bother giving you your car pass and aren’t around if you need them. Definitely considering not going next year and finding somewhere nicer.
reviews.author: Timothy V.

reviews.text: What a deal! Space for so many people in a beautiful and well maintained yurt. At least one of the beds was memory foam. There were 2 full sized beds, 4 singles, and a futon. We felt so lucky to grab this spot that was probably released from someone who made reservations months ago. Room for improvement: 1. door on yurt did not secure normally, we learned afterwards to “life the door up” for it to secure. A sign would be nice. 2. Our fireplace did not work so we were a bit cold, reported the problem. Otherwise, lovely!
reviews.author: nicole w.

reviews.text: Clean and spacious. Lake was a short walk from the camp ground. It looks like it only goes about 10 feet deep at most, makes it great for kids to swim in and great for fishing in hotter weather. Has a dock to reach deeper water for trout when it's hot. Kayak rentals are available at the second boat ramp. Great views of Mt. Hood on clearer days. Plenty of other lakes and streams around trillium to go to. Bunch of lodges close aswell if you get tired of camp food. Nothing motorized on the lake, very peaceful.
reviews.author: RYAN G.

reviews.text:
Pros: This is one of our favorite camping locations. Beautiful forest and that view of Mt Hood from the lake is breathtaking. It is also a great place to set up and then visit Timberline Lodge or spend a day on the alpine slide at Ski Bowl. Also, the toilets were super clean!
Cons: Our picnic table was broken and there was a camp setting off fireworks across the lake late at night. Also, the camping beach access had quite a few non-campers on it. Those are why I gave only 4 stars.
reviews.author: Sanna B.

reviews.text: Trillium campground is PERFECT for access to one of the most popular lakes in Oregon & Mt. Hood. Lots of sites with 1 pit toilet and water per ~10 sites. Sites vary from big enough to support big campers to only tent sites. Fire pit, tent pad,  charcoal grills, and picnic tables all included in each site, no electricity access. Other campers were friendly and mainly kept to themselves, lots of families and dogs. Close to government camp if you need anything last minute!
reviews.author: Sawyer B.

reviews.text: We love camping at Trillium Lake. The campsites are big enough. The lake is beautiful and the sky at night is amazing! Watching the sunset on Mt. Hood and star gazing is a must.  The bathrooms were kept clean. There were chipmunks that would run around our site. We enjoyed watching them. We could've done with out the carpenter ants though. This was the first time I've seen them. We took a trip into town for something we needed. I can't wait to come back!
reviews.author: Jeanine W.

reviews.text: Very nice that the campground wasnt full!  Woudl be nice if the park rangers/hosts were reasonable about parking in teh driveways.  Seems like they have nothing better to do than ensure that tires are on the asphalt.....while we were there during a fire ban and campsite next to us had a raging fire.  Seems the fire is a bigger risk than a tire 3 inches off the edge.  But they dont go around after dark to see what really goes on....
reviews.author: Danielle M.

reviews.text: Spent 3 nights here - peaceful, clean campground and had a short walk to the lake from our campsite 56. Bring paddle board or kayak and you can get out on the lake before the Day Use visitors get there! One of the mornings we went up to Timberline Lodge (15 min drive) and after exploring the lodge we took the Miracle Mile ski lift up for $20/person and had amazing views and hiked back down (you can take the lift down too).
reviews.author: Cindy R.

reviews.text:
One of the employees ran his generator all day every day. He verbally assaulted and threatened one of our campers. 
Nothing was done after having our complaint go to the lead manager. 
They told us he’d be gone that night, not that didn’t happen either. He was allowed to continue to run the generator all day. And each day he wasn’t even at his site to benefit from having it running from early morning to late night.
reviews.author: Tina H.

reviews.text: My family and I totally enjoyed our time at the lake.  I love that the trail around the lake has been completed.  The camp hosts do a great job.  Not so happy that dumpster divers went through every dumpster Sunday night around midnight looking for cans and bottles. They made so much noise, but at least they cleaned up after themselves! Campers have been courteous as well. Great place to camp and enjoy the mountain.
reviews.author: Jacquie P.

reviews.text: We really enjoyed many things about this campground. We had a well-appointed campsite, with easy access to water and bathrooms. The fire pit was nice and the picnic table was large and sturdy. The campground was clean and well cared-for. One thing we did not like was the generator noise from the RV in the next campsite over. Also there was no firewood for sale (though there was good kindling around the site).
reviews.author: Ruth B.

reviews.text: Trillium is a great place to camp with excellent sites - they are all great.  The main problem is that it is crazy hard to get a reservation.  I wish they would switch to the same platform the state parks use. Don't think to stroll up for one of the walk in sites.  I think people come in on the first day and never leave.  We always see people getting turned away. Bring something to float on the lake with!
reviews.author: Walter A.

reviews.text: My favorite place to camp! But This  trip we reserved site #35, which is a disabled site, for my friend who has a disability. The giant picnic table was blocking the wheelchair ramp, and was too heavy to move. The vault toilet smell was so strong it burned our lungs and we had to wear masks. Normally I have zero complaints about Trillium Lake, we just will not reserve that site again.
reviews.author: Jennifer C.

reviews.text: The day use area at this campground gets pretty heavy use.  I does get crowded around the campsites near the lake.  The upside is you'll get wonderful views of Mt. Hood on the south side of the lake.  Take your camera, if you hit it early without a breeze you'll get a great reflection of the mountain off the lake.  I also saw some nice Rainbow Trout taken.
reviews.author: David P.

reviews.text: Huge yurt! Three bunk beds and a futon give plenty of space to stretch out. There's no electric lighting or plug-ins, but that adds to the charm. The gas stove kept the worst of the cold out and was relatively straightforward to figure out. No showers but the bathroom was kept in stock. Beautiful place to spend a summer weekend.
reviews.author: Justin R.

reviews.text: The camp site was overall amazing and the staff were out of this world. The generators are the killer. Wish people knew how to camp/survive without them. Now a days there is solar wish people could just convert. Hate sitting at my camp listening to it and  breathing in the fumes from the campers Nextdoor.
reviews.author: Traci J.

reviews.text: We stayed at site 043 on 8/26 during our cross country roadtrip. This was a beautiful wooded site very well spaced out from the neighbors with a short secluded walk to the water. We were only here for a short time in the evening and morning but it was perfectly quiet and I would love to stay here again.
reviews.author: Emma K.

reviews.text: No camp site is on top of the other, each site has great privacy. The bathrooms leave much to be desired, but for pit toilets they were very clean and well stocked. Definitely would recommend! Friends also linited out of fish and we found some huckleberry.  BEST CAMP EVER!.
reviews.author: MELANIE M.

reviews.text: Why can't people camp without generators? Why do they need to hang christmas lights? Why have rules if nobody enforces them? Why are camp hosts even there? These shouldn't be rhetorical questions. We paid to camp at Mora, and NPS presumably paid a private company to manage Mora. So shouldn't NPS take some responsibility to ensure that everybody gets what they paid for?
reviews.author: Eric A.

reviews.text: This site (84E) was freaking awesome. HUGE site with views of the river and great privacy. You could fit 4 medium tents here no problem. Room for maybe 3-4 cars too. We used the restrooms at C loop across the street which was a 1-2 min walk. Easy access to Rialto Beach via 6 min drive.
reviews.author: Samantha P.

reviews.text: There are many positive attributes of Mora campground, but one seriously dangerous note.  First, the clean,  quiet campground had fresh water, flush toilets, and other nice amenities.  The campground alongside the Quillayute River gave our 19 foot RV a good spot to visit the area between  Kalaloch and the Hoh rainforest area.  As we arrived at the campground, a sign stated “ No RV parking at Rialto Beach” so we parked at Mora, set up, then took the signed “trail to Rialto Beach.”  It was late afternoon, and we hoped to watch a beach sunset.  The trail signage at the camp did not state that the trail was actually a 1.4 mile walk along a narrow, winding road with lots of steep curves, narrow bridges and only an occasional small brushy shoulder.  Lots of traffic made walking dangerous. For two adults, it was manageable, but NOT if we had a child with us.  For safety, we left the beach before sunset, to get back along the “trail” before dark, which was wise, as the traffic exiting the beach at sunset  made that little road dangerous.   We would advise better warning signage at the campground, as well as in official write-up in the Recreation.gov website.  As we arrived at the beach, we DID see RVs and parking lots! If we had known that, we would never had ventured the “trail.”  Next time, we will drive to the beach first, then go to our camp and park.
reviews.author: Norman S.

reviews.text: Mora is a beautiful place made terrible by this reservation system. Mora is in western Washington, it rains here, it's foggy, cool and gray. The reservations shows it as sold out all summer but the campground is often half full. People want blue skies and warm weather, most of the time that won’t happen here. People don’t show up or they leave early but don’t bother to cancel their reservations so no one can use their space. This system fails the locals who depend on the campers sending locally. It also fails people who have been coming to Mora for years but now can’t get reservations.
reviews.author: CONSTANCE K.

reviews.text: In many ways a beautiful campground but also deceptively restrictive.  It is located right on a beautiful river, except there is no access to the river.   It is a mile from the beach, but if you have a motorhome or RV, you are not allowed down the road to the beach as their is no large vehicle parking.  The staff have very limited and restricted hours.   A quiet and clean campground but a very restrictive and limited vibe.
reviews.author: Michael H.

reviews.text: A bit out of the way if you intend to visit Hurricane, Sol Duc, and Hoh Rainforest regions, but perfect for the beaches. While most people would prefer to get a wilderness pass and camp on the beach, most of that is shut down during COVID and Mora campground is the best campground for quick and easy access to the beach. Facilities were very clean, although I wish there were a shower. At least I didn't find one...
reviews.author: Dennison L.

reviews.text: Nice campground and bathrooms were really clean. Main complaint is there isn’t a walking trail from the campground to the beach. It’s less than a mile away but there’s nowhere to walk, except on the road. The least they could have is a trail alongside the road.
reviews.author: Jenna S.

reviews.text: Great campsite among giant trees. Cool and foggy but closest campground to Rialto Beach. Excellent evening Ranger talk.
reviews.author: Joseph C.

reviews.text: Great wooded campsite, close to Rialto beach, highly recommended, good privacy, flush toilets, helpful hosts
reviews.author: Josh B.

reviews.text: Nice size, clean site with helpful camp hosts
reviews.author: Donald B.

reviews.text:
The campground visually was very nice with lots of trees and plenty of shade. The loops are all paved with mostly smallish sites. There was so much shade that my solar received very little charge throughout the day. We ran our generator around 8:30am and 5pm for about 30 minutes each to keep a minimum charge. Our neighbors did the same. Overall, the park was quiet, especially after sundown.
Current update: Water is only available if you do NOT need a screw on hose connection. We asked the on duty ranger about a screw on water supply a threaded access point and was told they didn't have one, and if that's what I needed I could "go into town to the local hardware store to buy the required connection". I was shocked at his response! This was the experience we had with all park staff while staying at the Mora location. Our experience at Mora was dramatically different than the friendly and helpful rangers we encountered just a few days earlier at another Washington State campground. I don't understand the unfriendliness. And for $5 they could have altered their water hose to accommodate any park guest. The dump station was in working order.
The nearby Rialto Beach is a great location to beach-walk with an abundance of interesting driftwood. Parking is a challenge around mid-day, but we found space in the morning and later in the day.
Hurricane Ridge is about a 90 minute drive but well worth the experience and the view. You can select from various trail hikes or just enjoy the amazing view right from the parking lots.
Hoh Rainforest is about 45-60 minutes from Mora campground. Arrive early (before 10am) to avoid the miles long line at the park entrance and waiting for parking. We enjoyed hiking on several of the short loop trails as well as hiking up the Hoh River trail a mile or two. Overall, the loop trails and their informative signs were a great introduction to the location and forest habitat. The short hike up the Hoh River trail was only to say we did it.
reviews.author: Ed S.

reviews.text: I've stayed here several times and have always had an exceptional time. Unfortunately, my most recent reservation in July 2022 was a bit different. There were no park attendants, which in turn resulted in the bathrooms being covered in toilet paper, unclean sinks, dirty toilets, and absolutely zero handsoap for our entire stay. We actually went to the store and bought handsoap to put in the women's restroom. Really unsanitary. The sites are lovely, but the bathrooms were gross.
reviews.author: Taylor J.

reviews.text: We stayed briefly at Mora (C-52) but had a nice time. The real highlight was Rialto Beach right down the road. We took our 20 ft Class B camper van by the spot to check it out then went right to the beach. We watched the sunset at Rialto Beach, made dinner in the parking lot, then looked at the stars at night. We then drove back to the spot, set up real quick and quiet, went to bed and had a lovely morning in the campground. Would recommend to anyone.
reviews.author: Kennerly M.

reviews.text: Really enjoyed Mora, though our site (67) was a little shallower and longer than expected. We had some water pooling more than usual in this site, so definitely be prepared for the rain. We had a good hike to Rialto Beach. Note that there is a small trail you can take leaving the campground but then you pretty much follow the road with a small lip to walk on. Just be aware of your surroundings and traffic. Great stay though overall and quite peaceful.
reviews.author: Emily B.

reviews.text: Wish we had more nights to stay. 1min walk to the bathroom. There’s a short cut through the loop. Space was smaller than pictures shown. We had 5 of us and 3 tents fit nicely. 2 vehicles fit perfectly. Quiet, love the nature. Bathrooms don’t have any soaps or toilet cover protectors. Water faucets available outside of bathroom to fill up any water jugs.
reviews.author: Gladys G.

reviews.text: Loved this campground, wish we could have stayed longer! There are a couple of trails directly from the campground that were amazing, so many different fungi and mosses. Close to the beautiful beach as well.
reviews.author: Maria H.

reviews.text: One of my favorite campgrounds! Lots of good sites. Spent our weekend back and forth between the campground and Rialto Beach.
reviews.author: Terra C.

reviews.text:
Stayed in space A-19. Very private and close to the restrooms, yet far enough away where we couldn’t hear anything. Space was large enough for a truck, a 12- person tent, and still had plenty of room to be comfortable. Lots of trees, ground was level where the tent was set up, and our dogs had room to play. 
The restrooms were so clean and modern! I was impressed how well maintained they were and plenty of lighting inside. I wish they had showers, but wasn’t there long enough to be an issue. There are some restrooms at the Cycle Camp up the road and free to use to Mora guests - just leave a small donation. Mora Campground is in a great location to see the surrounding areas. Short drive to the beaches and you’re at Kalaloch, Rialto, or Ruby Beach - all of which are scenic and peaceful! Also 3 or 4 other beaches in between. There’s also a grocery/convenience store nearby up the road on the corner, and if you need more stuff, just drive up to Forks and you’ll find just about anything you need. We went there for dinner one night. Nothing fancy but they had a few restaurants to choose from, I highly recommend Mora Campground. Easy to get to, easy access, and centrally located. We will come back again!
reviews.author: Joe T.

reviews.text: We're an outdoorsy family, often camping in undeveloped places to get away from crowds. We actually really liked the campground itself even with full capacity. It's beautiful. However, when we booked we weren't alerted that there was a massive restoration project on the river flood plain adjacent to the grounds. From 7am-7pm, double rotor helicopters flew low elevation, constantly delivering logs. It was so close and so loud our dog, who is a gun-trained hunting dog, was in obvious pain. For those with kiddos you can imagine how our 1 y/o reacted without ear-pro. Luckily we had plans to leave and hike elsewhere during the day. But first thing in the morning and getting back to camp in the evening was maddeningly loud. This obviously isn't the campground's fault. Restoration of the area is required and important. but, if we had known this was taking place we simply would have gone elsewhere and certainly wouldn't have paid for it. So, the campground is 5-stars. Our specific experience was 0-stars.
reviews.author: Brian B.

reviews.text: It's a beautiful campground with large sites tucked in among huge trees.  It's convenient - there is easy access to Rialto Beach, and you can drive to some other popular places, such as Hoh Rainforest, Sol Duc, and Kalaloch Beach, in about an hour.  But there seems to be no enforcement of quiet hours, group size, or anything else.  We had a one large group partying next to us till 1 a.m. and another right across the street playing loud music.   I talked to the camp host, but they didn't seem to do anything.  The park ranger is off duty at night.  It always amazes me that people go to all the trouble and expense of making reservations, getting camping equipment, and going out into nature just to sit and drink.  The other negative thing is that there are too few bathroom facilities for the size of the campground.  A few porta-potties located around the campground would be very helpful.  All that being said, I would still recommend it if you want to camp in Olympic.
reviews.author: Susan J.

reviews.text: Wonderful and quiet location on the western section of Olympic NP minutes away from Rialto Beach. We drove to Cape Flattery, Makah Cultural & Research Center Museum & the Hoh Rainforest. The Mora campground is wooded & felt private. Our site was #43 in Loop C, included a picnic table & fire ring. The bathrooms appeared to be recently remodeled & were very clean. No handsoap, so bring your own. In the bathroom there are electrical outlets for charging, a hand dryer, and a changing table for little ones. RV dump station and potable water was available & well maintained. Grocery, gas & hardware store down the road in Forks.
reviews.author: Pam C.

reviews.text: Expansive campground. Beautiful area. Dickey River is nearby and looks amazing for kayaking.  We didn't know it was there, so next time, definitely bringing a kayak. No parking there, so you'll have to drop off your gear. Nice bathrooms in campground. If you're looking for hiking trails near the campground, there aren't any, but short .01 walk to James Pond. Drive to or walk along the highway to Rialto Beach. Some campsites are smaller than others, so check the various site loops A, D, E, etc. Loop A are smaller sites and those in loop D or E are bigger, more space for tents, motor home, vehicles, etc.
reviews.author: Emily W.

reviews.text: This campground is great. It is beautiful and quiet. The facilities are very clean. It is close to local beaches... Rialto, Ruby, etc. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because we had the handicapped site which has zero privacy and is directly across from the bathroom. Site 21-B is basically the center of the town square and you are on full display for everyone as they go to the bathroom or get dish water. Most of the other sites were private and looked great, particularly the outer loops. Really lovely campground.
reviews.author: Jennifer B.

reviews.text:
I hate to rate this poorly, as the location was great, the bathrooms were clean, etc.

However, there was a site that was super loud until maybe 2 AM, with music and all.
Then the site right next to us had men who got up before 6, and talked loudly and CRUDELY.  It woke up my 10 year old as well, and thankfully what they were saying was going over my sons head so he didn’t know what they were saying exactly (lots of innuendoes).  At any rate it was so loud, and it disgusted me.  
I didn’t get much sleep at all.
reviews.author: April Y.

reviews.text: Mora Campground is a beautiful place to stay, and I would definitely come back again. I traveled here solo, and I felt very safe and comfortable within the campground. There is no service which is wonderful, but be careful to take care of anything you may need (loading maps/directions, etc) in Forks before entering the area. Being very close to Rialto beach was very nice as well, and seeing sunset on the coast is definitely a must!
reviews.author: Taylor K.

reviews.text: Camped for three nights. It was within walking distance to Rialto Beach, via a road, and along the river. It was a quiet campground until Friday night and then the partiers came and were very loud until about 1am. We had two cars and two 6 person tents. It was cozy, but had plenty of space. We explored Rialto Beach, 1st Beach, 3rd Beach, & Cape Flattery. The Olympic coast is truly magical.
reviews.author: Renee L.

reviews.text: We camp in a 27 foot travel trailer; tow vehicle is a Ford F150. We could pull into this site with no problem; but, could not pull out going forward due to trees on the roadside of the loop. The loop is very short. When attempting to back out we broke the powered stabilizer jacks on a tree root; cost $840 to replace. This site is only good for a very small trailer, pop-up trailer or tent.
reviews.author: Kenneth L.

reviews.text: The site map did not list my space as handicap. While it would have been excellent if you're in a wheelchair, for me it was horrible. I felt like I was camped in a fishbowl. The path to the bathroom directly led to my tent site, so everyone's flashlight shone directly into my tent. That combined with the sound of flushing toilet's led to a sleepless night. I left after one night.
reviews.author: Sharon W.

reviews.text: Unlike Kalaloch, which is undeniably beautiful and off the beach, this place is very nice as well. Big difference is the space between campsites. More room, more trees, more privacy and less on top of each other. Amazing stay. Bathroom was decent as well. Looked well kept and clean over all. Few minutes away from Rialto Beach. Pure treat.
reviews.author: Roxanne L.

reviews.text: Absolutely lovely forrest location.  Rangers taking care of the facilities were on it.  Did a great job. Everything. was stocked and clean.  Camp hosts did rounds and introduced themselves and provided some suggestions on the area.  Did all the hikes from the campground.  Rialto Beach is a must see.  Would love to come back.
reviews.author: Lisa B.

reviews.text: Campsite 2A is amazing! Highly recommend camping here great spot. Right next to Rialto Beach 4mile round trip walking distance, close to the river spotted some bald eagles and wild otters! A short drive away is a nice mini-mart with snacks, booze and firewood! Easy camping experience and gorgeous!
reviews.author: Krista M.

reviews.text: I have been camping at Mora for 50 years and think it is a wonderful campground.  This year the weather was cold and because of the burn ban, we couldn't have a campfire to keep warm.  So in the future, if there is a burn ban, I probably won't go.
reviews.author: Stan T.

reviews.text: Nice location. Originally had reservations at C-46 which the claimed would take a 22’ RV. It would not, but this site A-10, which claimed to only take a 17’ foot RV actually accommodated a 23’ RV.
reviews.author: Samuel S.

reviews.text:
Nice site, a bit more secluded than its neighbors. Road noise was a little annoying. 

Very nice new bathroom building. I only wish it had coat hooks.
reviews.author: Jeff K.

reviews.text: Beautiful and quiet campground. Beach access just down the road. Toilets were clean. Many places to buy firewood along the way to the campsite.
reviews.author: Crisandra W.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground and beautiful, private campsite. Wonderful tall evergreen trees.  Clean bathrooms with toilet paper.  Quiet.
reviews.author: Susan H.

reviews.text: too many barking dogs, screaming kids and drunk women at dusk and early darkness....ruined my zen mojo fire pit time.....
reviews.author: Paul G.

reviews.text: A magical and pleasant grounds, many memories made! Thank you to the camp hosts who took care of the area.
reviews.author: Sarah K.

reviews.text: Easy camping...near Rialto Beach and La Push...great camp sites...and James Pond is cool...
reviews.author: John D.

reviews.text: We love this campground.  Reservation only really changes it in a negative at, however.
reviews.author: Amanda W.

reviews.text: Good site.  Plenty of space for a 23’ RV or larger, and an additional vehicle.
reviews.author: Samuel S.

reviews.text: Beautiful location and campsite. Very serene and not too crowded.
reviews.author: Alejandra L.

reviews.text: Great place; beautiful surroundings; clean bathrooms.
reviews.author: VICKI M.

reviews.text: Incredible campground!
reviews.author: Krista M.

reviews.text: Loved this campground
reviews.author: Katie h.

reviews.text:
We stayed at site 64D in early September for three nights. The only complaints I have about this campground relate to the comfort of the grounds themselves. As absolutely gorgeous and calming as it was to be in the forest, it started getting a bit dreary after a couple of days. It was dark and chilly all day long. We got rained on and made it through just barely, so make sure you have a tent that can really hold up against moisture. The sites, parking, and roads are quite tight, so depending on where you are, trucks and trailers are difficult to maneuver. There isn't much space between sites, either, so I'd give privacy a 5/10. No handsoap in the bathrooms and no showers on the grounds.

My one big complaint is that the ROAD to Rialto Beach is advertised as a "trail" when it is not. There's no shoulder on the road, so it's not the safest for walking or biking, and definitely not safe with kids or dogs.

Overall, however, it's a good place to camp. Rangers are around daily which made me feel safe and shows that the area is not neglected. The bug situation is way better than pretty much any other campground I can think of. Just some mosquitos, but that's to be expected. Convenience stores are a very short drive away and the surrounding beaches are to die for. Beautiful place for sure, but I probably wouldn't stay as long if I ever went back.
reviews.author: Samantha L.

reviews.text:
Beautiful and quiet! The bathrooms were immaculate, which is pretty amazing for a campground. As others have noted, there are no soap dispensers, so be sure to bring your own soap or hand sanitizer. We had rodents (squirrels, maybe?) scampering across the roof of our van's poptop during both nights of our stay, but I suppose that's the price you pay for being in their home. Thankfully none of them broke in. Maybe they were just checking us out. We loved this campground! 

Rialto Beach was full, so we drove down to LaPush and Second Beach. They were both beautiful and not a long drive. At LaPush, we enjoyed taking photos with the beach logs and also spotting seals fishing in the surf. We timed our visit to Second Beach to catch low tide, and the tide pools were incredible! Even the mile-long hike to the beach was stunning. We bought our parking permits (good until the end of the day, so we needed two for our 2-day stay) from the little store in LaPush. There is a QR code that you can use from the parking lot at Second Beach, but we ran into a couple of folks who were having trouble getting a cell signal. I was thankful we'd already purchased ours.
reviews.author: Karen B.

reviews.text: We had a tent site 90 on loop E which we discovered is predominately an RV loop. We were surrounded by RV's that had bright lights on literally all night and way more than eight people per campsite. It was quite noisy and very bright. I checked out the other loops at night and they were quieter and darker and we would have preferred that.  We were hoping to catch some bioluminescence at Rialto Beach, but were surprised to find that the beach was almost as crowded at night as during the day. There were quite a few illegal campfires and again a lot of lights.  After returning to campsite that evening, we heard large explosions of fireworks around midnight which we presumed were coming from the beach... also not very relaxing. It's unfortunate because this really is a nice campground in a good location otherwise. We might return during a less busy time of the year to see if we have a different experience and would definitely pick a campsite on a different loop.
reviews.author: Christine L.

reviews.text: Mora is an old campground designed for tents. It is good for a disconnected camping experience. A few sites can accommodate small trailers or Class B RVs but leveling may be necessary. Sites have some privacy but parking is often limited so that vehicles may be next to the narrow loop road. Facilities are basic and those are often in poor repair. There is central water, no kitchen cleaning dump stations, no cellular service, and little sky exposure for solar power or Starlink. The Loop D restroom had no hot water or hand cleaning facilities, no shelves or hooks, and the stall locks were broken. Stormwater drainage is generally poor. Trails are poorly signed if at all and the beach is a couple miles away. In summary, semi-primitive, tent-oriented camping for those who seek that, assuming one can reserve a suitable site which is a challenge on wreck.gov. Friendly staff such as they are.
reviews.author: Nils E.

reviews.text: The campground is very pretty with all the trees, but it was cold and wet. If you’re tent camping or want to see the sun I’d recommend staying at a different campground in Olympic. Some folks had pop ups or canopies over their tables so their stuff didn’t get wet which I would also recommend if you stay here. The bathrooms were ok. Not the cleanest but passable. There wasn’t any hand soap in the bathrooms so make sure to bring your own. We were in site 35b. It was small and there was no privacy from the road. The people at the site across from us were very loud. Their kids screamed and yelled the entire time and it definitely took away from the peacefulness of the location. The campground is about 30 minutes from Forks. It’s a cute town and has a decent grocery store.
reviews.author: Nicole R.

reviews.text: Beautiful little lake. Boat ramp with access to swimming. Nice quiet little campground. Gravel road has a lot of potholes.  Our 2wd camper van had no problem, you just need to drive really slow.
reviews.author: Claudia H.

reviews.text:
Little Crater Lake is a pond, but a beautiful, magical pond! and now I can say my feet have trekked the PCT trail, okay only a couple of miles, but it was still kind of exciting. 
It also seems to be a jump off spot for the PCT, and kayak outfitters come ripping through the cg by the vanload and park in spaces that are about halfway around the cg. 
Water is from a hand pump before you enter the cg. Kind of a pain for solo's, but I managed. 
I made the mistake of taking the route from Detroit Lake, which involved 20-30 miles of gravel, some not so ok, two traffic lights on the gravel roads because it was one lane, and one work crew stop, and no service so a little scarey to turn around. 
Also there is no view of Mt. Hood from the cg, but I am not sure if that was because of geography or just trees. 
This is a lovely campground and this spot is about as private as they get, but also spacious. I chose this cg over Timothy because it's not by water and thought it would be quieter. And it would have been were it not for the 47,000 children that were everywhere and screaming screaming at the top of their lungs for hours on end. I don't get it. I was a kid. I went camping and did stuff and had fun. But that crap would not have been allowed back then, either by hosts or by parents. To be fair to the kids, the parents were also loud. I could not even listen to a podcast at my normal listening level at 9pm in my SUV! Thankfully a severe storm rolled in the next night and shut them up and some even left.
reviews.author: Julie Reid R.

reviews.text:
As a local, we love Little Crater Lake. The campground is small without a ton of sites. The sites themselves can be challenging as they all have different degrees of being level, tree roots, etc. Our site was #1 and it was a good site for our needs but right by the entrance.

During the day, it gets really busy with tourists and/or PCT traffic so be aware. It is not quiet at all during the day. The trail to the lake, although short, was not well trimmed and was overgrown with bushes. The platform to see the lake was in disrepair. Additionally, the way visitors were treating the lake was absolutely terrible and disgusting -- dogs and people were in the water each time we walked to the lake on our trip. As a result of this poor judgment, the lake was not the beautiful blue color it typically is and it was such a let down to see such selfishness on display -- water entry is not permitted at LCL.

The sites do not have immediate water available. There is well nearby but it was not functional. There are actually 2 vault toilets available -- one across from site 1 and another between sites 9 and 10.
