We had some safety concerns at the lake so we left a little early.

If you go exploring, watch out for barbed wire that isn't easily visible especially along the back of sites 1-5. I did not explore the backs of the other sites to speak if there is barbed wire behind those as well.
reviews.author: Debra F.

reviews.text: Little Crater Lake Campground is a campground for tenters and small RVs. It is amazingly quiet and peaceful.  The campsites are in a wooded area with a lovely meadow just beyond--full of flowers in season, but they were pretty much bloomed-out in late August. The lake itself is beautiful, accessible by an easy trail. A short distance beyond the lake, the trail meets the Pacific Crest Trail. One direction heads through the woods toward Mt. Hood. The other leads on a mostly flat trail to Timothy Lake. So plenty of opportunities to hike--or fish, if you walk to Timothy Lake. We hiked along the west side of Timothy Lake this time--did the east side last visit. Both are lovely hikes with nice views of the lake. Little Crater Lake is a lovely place to escape the noise of civilization and enjoy the quiet.
reviews.author: Susan M.

reviews.text: A small, unhosted campground that is adjacent to the Pacific Crest Trail, a mountain bog, and of course, the little Crater Lake. The sites were large - lots of space in each site. Some sites were mostly unshaded but my site was full shade. The "lake" is a bit of a tourist attraction with many cars parking in the small day-use parking, walking to the lake, and then leaving. Fire ban is in effect so no campfires. Must take your garbage out.
reviews.author: Sue K.

reviews.text: We stayed in spot 7 and it was absolutely perfect! We were close enough to the bathroom to not have to worry too much about the kids getting there, but far away enough not to smell it. The short trail to the lake is directly across the street. Views are breathtaking and only 1/2 mile hike on the PCT to Timothy Lake. My favorite campground in Oregon, so far.
reviews.author: Angel G.

reviews.text: In spite of the fire ban, we throughly enjoyed camping at Little Crater Lake. It is an excellent, quiet spot with a lovely meadow nearby and is a short hike to the Pacific Crest Trail and Timothy Lake as well. The toilets were very clean and smelled great! The crater is a fascinating geological phenomenon with a weirdly aquamarine hue.
reviews.author: Peter  W.

reviews.text: This is quite a cute little campsite. The water is very difficult to pump so I'd recommend bringing a lot of water for drinking and a tub to clean dishes in. The camp hosts were very helpful and kind!
reviews.author: Jacqueline G.

reviews.text: It was our maiden voyage with our new small trailer. We found the campground quiet and clean. Loved the access to the meadow, lake and hiking!
reviews.author: Victoria B.

reviews.text: Great Location, smaller campground, quiet in the evening
reviews.author: Jim B.

reviews.text: Beautiful, sacred, wondrous place!
reviews.author: Tahja W.

reviews.text: The location of the campground is excellent with its vicinity to little crater lake was amazing. We had plenty of space for our large 9 person tent in spot 10. However, the outhouses were not well maintained. They were very smelly especially the one near the day use area and it seemed to be in need of toilet paper and a good cleaning. Also we were a little closer to our neighbors than we would like. There was a fire ban in place and it seemed several people were ignoring that and it was not enforced. There were lots of wasps. Every time we were preparing food we were harassed by them. Over all a great spot surrounded by wet lands, tress and wildlife. Also appreciated it being so close to Timothy lake.
reviews.author: Rachel C.

reviews.text: We love the Little Crater Lake Campground.  Well, in the past we have.  But site 5 was terrible for our needs.  There is no place for a family size tent (four person).  It would probably be fine for one or two smaller tents, or a hammock camper, but it didn't meet our needs.  We would have had to pitch on the parking strip had our family not been in another site that could accommodate our tent with them.  Which is a shame, because the site is pretty, just not functional.  Lots of exposed roots, which is probably erosion due to overuse, because of how pretty this site is.  I get it.  Also, the trailhead pit toilet door lock was broken so that was kinda awkward.  But survivable.
reviews.author: Ralph G.

reviews.text:
A sweet campsite with 9  or 10 different spots to plant a tent or two in among the trees.   It is very close to beautiful Little Crater Lake, which is reached via a trail through the meadow nearby.    And it is close to the Pacific Crest Trail in the forest behind Little Crater Lake.  Beautiful.
The campsite is clean, quiet, and has a pleasant ranger who welcomes people at the entrance of the site.  The toilets are decent, with plenty of paper and a good distance from each other.   There is running water at the entrance of the campground.   
There ws wind that night, so no mosquitoes to bother us.
reviews.author: Elizabeth S.

reviews.text: The ground was kept very clean, the view was nice but it was cloudy so we couldn't see the Hood, but the lake was very nice. Site host came and greeted and gave us a piece of info sheet. The campground was very neat,  out site was sort of small compared with the stay from a night before at Stone Creek and the distance among the neighbors was very short, there were trees but noise from them was pretty obvious. Bush toilet was clean, plenty of toilet paper. All in all, we enjoyed our stay.
reviews.author: Chris W.

reviews.text: Lovely little campground, sites pretty well separated, in a woodsy area. There’s only one water source, close to the entrance. Composting toilets were clean. Short walk to Little Crater Lake, which is beautiful deep blue, more of a small pond than a lake, and a mile or so walk (partly on the Pacific Crest Trail) to Timothy lake, where you can fish or swim (though too cold for swimming this week).
reviews.author: Margaret C.

reviews.text:
Made reservations in the spring, got multi confirmations via email. Arrived to find a couple in our spot who said the spot was open so they took it. Luckily we went to another camp site 
 nearby called Clackamus, which shares the campground host with Little Crater Lake. She found a spot for us. Alls well that ends well, but we didn't get to stay where we wanted.
reviews.author: Leah S.

reviews.text: Beautiful!  Serene!  The bog/meadow afforded unobstructed open sky views at night to enjoy shooting stars, planets,  and even the Milky Way - all visible to the naked eye.  Awesome!  And the short trail past the lake connecting with a portion of the Pacific Crest Trail and on to Timothy Lake was well worth the easy walk!  Thanks!
reviews.author: Theodore B.

reviews.text: This campsite is really beautiful and right off the PCT! Some beautiful trails and lakes, and you can swim at Timothy Lake which is a quick drive. The negatives are that the road there was a little bit of a pain (granted I have a very small car), there were LOTS of mosquitoes, and the bathrooms were really gross.
reviews.author: Isabella R.

reviews.text: Love how close this campground is to a lovely stretch of the PCT but the access trail is in need of some repairs.  Some boards have broken through and large nails are sticking up in a couple places.  It is still a wonderful connector trail, but there are a few places where you have to be very careful.
reviews.author: Karen K.

reviews.text: Camp site has lots of roots. Lots of mosquitoes because around the camp area is marsh. Little crater lake is very pretty. Short walk from the camp site. There are no trash cans on site so you’ll have to haul your trash out. Well water is at the front so you’ll have to drive there.
reviews.author: Phu L.

reviews.text: Beautiful site with 5 minute walk to Little Crater Lake and a short hike to Timothy Lake.  Site 9 was nice, a little close to the next site over and out in the open, there were other sites that seemed more tucked away though. Bathrooms kept clean and the camp host was lovely!
reviews.author: Rachel G.

reviews.text:
Beautiful, quiet little campground. 
Wonderful hikes to Timothy lake. 
Issue: sadly so many peole booked sites that never showed up. Great for people who still came looking for FF but sad for those who just didn’t come because it appeared full online. 
Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Carolyn F.

reviews.text: A nice little campground. Not too far of a drive from Timothy Lake and Frog Lake. Little Crater Lake is a short walk down a trail from the campground. It's beautiful, very blue! From what I could tell almost all the camp spots are flat except for spot #16.
reviews.author: Nancy W.

reviews.text: Bathrooms were not clean, and according the maintenance card, not cleaned for over 10 days. Mosquitos were thick, but was to be expected that close to the marsh. Site itself was clean, with plenty of space. Decent walk to water, with only one manual pump.
reviews.author: Quinn C.

reviews.text: Sweet, quiet little campground. This was our second time visiting, and we had a pleasant stay. Friendly camp staff and camp neighbors. Came prepared for hordes of mosquitoes, but, thankfully, we didn’t see any. We’ll definitely be back again!
reviews.author: Abigail J.

reviews.text: most peaceful campsites I have ever camped at. Deer walked right through our camp at night, with tons of wildlife everywhere. The trail paths within the forest were well-manicured and very easy to accomplish.
reviews.author: Nicholas D.

reviews.text: Toilet paper was out, on 6/10, and never saw a person in the park till the 14th. It rained real hard the whole time was miserable mother nature was not kind. We didn't stay the rest of the week.
reviews.author: Kandace T.

reviews.text: Site #10 was spacious and close to the bathrooms, but not too close (though it was fairly clean for a pit toilet!). The host was kind and attentive. Little Crater Lake is a short walk away!
reviews.author: Stephanie C.

reviews.text: This is a sweet little campground, much quieter than Timothy Lake and an easy drive for a daytrip to Timothy. It would be nice if hand sanitizer could be installed in the outhouses.
reviews.author: Barb R.

reviews.text: Nice and small campground. Some tourist traffic in the campground, but never too busy. Definitely will be back. Hiking trails are great.
reviews.author: Anna H.

reviews.text: Great site with access to the PCT and a very pretty little lake. Good woods, nice view of meadows. Clean bathrooms too, Loved our stay!
reviews.author: Travis G.

reviews.text: Beautiful little campground and just a short hike to the cutest most beautiful lake I’ve ever seen. I will definitely go back again.
reviews.author: Paula M.

reviews.text: Exceptional camp host, Barb. Nice, clean, mostly quiet campground with large campsites. Beautiful walk to LCL and Timothy Lake.
reviews.author: Phylis W.

reviews.text: This is a jem of a site. Be aware that potable water is not close so bringing a large container for water storage is advisable.
reviews.author: Julie J.

reviews.text:
Never saw a Ranger. I was there for 4 days, 3 nights.
I had no phone service, so Thank goodness my neighbors were fairly quiet.
reviews.author: Robert P.

reviews.text: Host is friendly. Little Crater Lake and the nearby PCT are beautiful. Campsite #10 is tolerable. Campsite #9 is a raw mess.
reviews.author: Robert R.

reviews.text: Very loud disrespectful guests on both sides of our site. Drumming, singing, yelling, loud music, 5 tents in one site.
reviews.author: John A.

reviews.text: I had a really great stay there and the camp host was AWESOME!  I hope to get back soon.
reviews.author: Michael F.

reviews.text: The sites are so roomy! Just a quick walk to little crater lake. Had an amazing visit!!
reviews.author: Lyssa B.

reviews.text: A cute and pretty out there spot to go camping at. I like that the bathroom was clean.
reviews.author: Loreley S.

reviews.text: Neighbor had small children they let just scream, but the area itself was VERY nice
reviews.author: Andrew S.

reviews.text: My roommates and I love coming back to Little Crater Lake year after year!
reviews.author: Maria G.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Looooots of mosquitoes near standing water
reviews.author: Jonathan L.

reviews.text: Great home base for exploring the area.
reviews.author: Jeni M.

reviews.text: Super easy spot to stay with a family.
reviews.author: Tessa A.

reviews.text: The campground was very clean and nice.
reviews.author: Chris M.

reviews.text: Really shady and well kempt
reviews.author: Tekiah E.

reviews.text: Beautiful, quiet campground
reviews.author: Hunter K.

reviews.text: My fav campground to date!
reviews.author: Nicole S.

reviews.text:
This campground is beautiful! The campsites are far apart from each other so you really feel you have your privacy. The hiking trail offers beautiful views of the river; it was hot enough to swim in the river after soaking in the sun! There is also a camp store (near Union Creek Campground) walking distance from Farewell Bend, accessible via the hiking trail. We got hot coffees and a few items we forgot to bring. 

Our one not so great experience was a strange occurrence with the campground host. She approached our campsite after we arrived. She claimed we needed to pay for the cars we parked at our campsite. I casually explained that we paid for parking when we booked our campsite and offered to show her our reservation on my phone. She became very cross with me and claimed "the website didn't work" and then said she "was trying to be a welcoming camp host." She said both of these things with sarcasm. The situation quickly escalated and she said several contrasting things. Members of my party realized she was rather intoxicated; I feel foolish for not realizing this earlier. Before she left she disclosed she "had been drinking" and didn't "want things to get ugly." She left  our site claiming she would come by the next day to collect cash for the cars. She DID NOT come by the following day, which made me believe she was trying to scam us for $5-10. An overall weird experience, but I do not think she had the best intentions. An overall great stay, but beware of the host!
reviews.author: Mackenzie K.

reviews.text:
We have called at Farewell Bend every summer season. The bathrooms were will keep up this summer but I was disappointed in the roads, and pads for RV's. They had not been cleaned and we're COVERED in a deep layer of pine needles. I've never seen it that bad. I swept our site clean except under the RV. 
PEOPLE This summer had no respect for camp sites, trudging through our site to get to the river when there was a path a little ways down. Next time, I want to take yellow caution tape and encircle my camp space, telling others to go around. 
Also, this time, several dogs were NOT ON leashes, one running and trying to attack our small dog. My husband yelled and I smacked the dog with my cane! THEN the owner came to retrieve the dog. The camp hosts said hello when we first pulled in but didn't enforce rules or do much maintenance as far as we could see except the bathrooms- and they were clean. 
We'll still go again, probably take a battery powered blower with us!
reviews.author: Libby W.

reviews.text: Loved this campground,  spent 4 nights there,  very convenient  to go see crater later and natural  tunnel.  We camped in site #4 with a 36 ft motorhome, river was right behind us. Very Nice large, level  site. Plenty  of room between  sites. A little  but of road noise  but the river drowned out most of it.
reviews.author: Barbara H.

reviews.text:
I dont usually fill out a review. I've camped here for the last five or six years. The issue I have is with the camphost. The last couple years the camphost has been sub-performing Both trips this year, they aren't present.  They hang up a sign, especially for my second trip, stating "camp host off duty". Friday your off duty?  I was there for 3 days this time, and saw the camphost once.  That says alot seems how i was camping directly adjacent to their site. I watched alot of folks come in then leave. I assume this was because it was unclear on how to get a campsite.  The bathrooms are being cleaned by what appears to be contracted help. Last year there wasnt any TP in the bathrooms. There are notes hanging in the bathroom for 3 weeks that the soap dispensers are empty. The camphost is not selling firewood, but they have built a wall around their camp out of rounds. Probably a few cords worth. 
All of these issues don't actually impact me cause I come prepared, but I have never seen anything like this anywhere I've camped. I had to change my own reservation paperwork on the site markers. This is one of my favorite campgrounds and I feel like there should be a camphost there that, A) Is there  and B) is doing their job.
In my opinion,  I think the current camphost is a "squatter ".  I'm basing this on behavior and the fact their site looks like a homeless camp.
reviews.author: Toby D.

reviews.text: Lovely campground right on the river.  Delightful to fall asleep to the sounds of rushing water.  Despite being next to the water, bugs were not particularly problematic.  Bathrooms but no showers, plenty of water spigots throughout.  Campground host is super helpful.  One drawback is campsites are not particularly private - a number of them are rented as single sites but are set up like group sites and share a common area with another site; even sites with trees between them are barely separated and the foliage is thin.  Campground is just down the road from Union Creek Resort where theres a general store, diner, ice cream and BBQ.  20 minutes to Crater Lake National Park which is an easy and spectacular half day visit (or full day if you are an ambitious hiker).
reviews.author: Tim G.

reviews.text: 2020 camp hosts leave much to be desired.  We were camped directly across from the oldest bathroom, and I never saw the camp hosts go in there to clean even one time over the 3 days we stayed here.  They pulled up to the bathroom in their golf cart, sat there for 20 minutes, never left the cart and then drove on.  We were in a trailer and never used the public bathroom, but I would seriously think twice about camping here if I was in a tent because the bathrooms are not being cleaned during the pandemic.  There was also a lot of trash in our campsite left from the previous campers.  I spent 3 days picking up little pieces of trash.
reviews.author: Nancy P.

reviews.text:
We love this campground, but the bathrooms were not cleaned the whole time we were there.  We arrived on a Sunday and there was dried excrement on the toilet seat, toilet paper on the floor and the wastebasket was half full.  On Thursday when we left, everything was the same except the wastebasket was now overflowing.  We have stayed at Farewell Bend many times and it has never been like this.  What has changed?  Very disappointed in the maintenance, but still love the campground.
It is in walking distance of the Rogue Gorge and the sites are beautiful along the Rogue River.
reviews.author: Rudy H.

reviews.text:
While the bathroom nearest us was “closed for maintenance” and the next closest one was rather basic, the campsite itself was very large, water was available nearby, and the river was just out the back. The river was the highlight with lots of little rapids/falls for the family to explore - it was one of our favorite things on our multi-state trip!
Definitely would recommend and will return!
reviews.author: Jonathan G.

reviews.text: It was just a quick drive to Crater Lake which made it easy to make it there for a sunrise hike. The campsite was right on the river and people definitely go swimming. Clean bathrooms and a quiet campground. Definitely would love to go again and for longer next time!
reviews.author: Sara K.

reviews.text: We have been coming to this campground for over 50 years and it's our favorite. This visit was the most disappointing. The campground host dropped the ball on cleanup as the bathrooms were never cleaned and the women's was out of toilet paper.
reviews.author: Karen H.

reviews.text: We booked this site for 2 nights for 12 adults, 4 dogs and a kid and ended up being 8 adults and 4 dogs. Though the site occupancy is for 16pax, it would have been really tight for that many people. Great location, plenty of open space right next to the site, the dogs enjoyed. It was pretty secluded on both sides with trees, we could not see/hear our neighbors. Water was available 2 sites away and the toilets were located pretty close to the site as well. The women washrooms were super clean at all times, men washrooms had bugs in them and there was no soap in either of the toilets throughout. Overall, a great experience and definitely wouldn't mind visiting again.
reviews.author: Samyucktha K.

reviews.text: I stayed in Campsite 52. It was close to the toilet and quite spacious. Wood was readily available at the host site. Mostly rained half the time, but it was excellent spot to use, very close to Crater Lake.
reviews.author: Ragni M.

reviews.text: We always look forward to camping at Farewell Bend. Beautiful big sites. Camp hosts have always been great. Lots to do in immediate vicinity.
reviews.author: Howard S.

reviews.text: Such a beautiful location near the Gorge.  Great easy hiking and campsites are a generous size. Couldn't have been a better experience!
reviews.author: SALLY C.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Absolutely stunning and loved being right on the Rogue river. Easy access to get up to Crater Lake.
reviews.author: Lucas T.

reviews.text: Absolutely love this campground, will go back.  Nicely spread out and quiet.  Camp hosts were very friendly and helpful.
reviews.author: Fred M.

reviews.text: solid campsite! easy to get in and out. a bit of a walk to bathrooms but nothing unmanageable. Good place to stay!
reviews.author: Veronica P.

reviews.text: Lovely site next to the river and walking distance to the waterfall.
reviews.author: Matthias L.

reviews.text:
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at Farewell Bend. We were there Monday-Friday in our 27 foot motorhome. We had both site 35 & 36. Originally we planned to have friends occupy one site and wed have the other as they are less than 10 feet apart. Our friends backed out, but we kept both sites as they are so close together. I wouldn't recommend staying in only one site due to their close proximity. Overall, the sites are very spacious and reasonably level. Many, like ours, are right on the river. There's a lot of shade, but there was enough sun for my solar panels to fully charge my batteries by 4PM. The water spigot was only 20 steps away. There were several spots between campsites where you can be on the river without being on someone else's campsite. Road noise was minimal, mostly drowned out by the sound of the river rushing by. The bathrooms were clean, and the campground was well maintained. We hiked less than half a mile to Rogue Gorge, which is a fantastic site. I hiked about four miles to Natural Bridge. (Just take the Union Creek trail to the Rogue River trail.) That was even more fantastic! It was a great hike eight miles round trip. I even ran into a black bear about half a mile from the Union Creek campground, but it ran off as soon as I yelled "Hey bear!".
Overall we loved our stay at Farewell Bend. Were already planning for another trip later this year.
reviews.author: David T.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground with adequate services, but with one major negative.  Booked 1 campsite several months early for August visit on recreation.gov, claiming 3 people and 2 vehicles and paid the calculated price on-line.   After arriving at the campsite, I was "held up" by the camp host demanding another $12.50 per night for the second vehicle.  When I showed my recreation.gov receipt showing 2 vehicle claimed, I got this story that there was some USDA Forest Service requirement to pay an additional daily fee for second vehicle that doesn't flow through when making reservations on-line.  If this is actually true, why wasn't this calculated when I paid on line, or next best thing why wasn't there a note on-line explaining  a fee will be required on arrival when making the reservation for this campsite.  If the "bate and switch" fee is legitimate, fix you on-line reservation process to display the correct fee!   Thanks for the opportunity to comment.
reviews.author: Paulette E.

reviews.text: This campground has so much... potential.   Admittedly we went during a time it had posted that they'd thinned trees and had the trimmings visible.   Fortunately, we had a site right on the creek (river?) otherwise it would have been depressing! There were others camped with these giant heaping mounds of trimmed trees and pine needles etc. Our site was lovely, but the campground otherwise felt desolate and sad!   There was caution tape across the host site, with a "want to be a host? call here" sign.   Which was puzzling. Until I learned that the lowest # campsites currently have no water.  Guess a line got cut.  The flush toilets... well the one near us wouldn't flush. Probably that line!  That was the nicer one.   We had to walk quite a ways to the next one (5-7 min walk!).  At least those flushed, but the faucet literally turned in the sink.  As pretty as my site was, I'm saying farewell to farewell bend....
reviews.author: Kelly B.

reviews.text: This campground was great, but the camp host of June 2023 was NOT!  We had reserved and prepaid for 2 nights through recreation.gov.  We returned from Crater Lake NP about 5pm the second night and found another couple in our site.  The couple told us that the camp host had said the site was empty.  When we talked with the camp host, she said that nothing was left in the site, so she assumed we had left early.  My husband pointed out that we were in a self-contained camper van so there was nothing we could easily leave, but we had left a towel to dry on the picnic table.  She claimed nothing was left in the site and instead of apologizing she stated, “I’m the camp host and I can do what I want!”.  I asked what we were supposed to do now.  She said, “I can’t help you.”  (We drove about an hour and found a Snow Park to park the van for the night.)
reviews.author: Christine G.

reviews.text:
Farewell Bend Campground is our favorite by far!! My wife and I can't get enough of it, which is why we spent 7 nights there this summer and hope to get a few more in this fall before it closes. The Rogue River is the biggest reason we love it. We always choose a site on the river, loving the sound and beauty it gives off. But the campground itself is wonderful. The bathrooms are alway clean; the campground is quiet, and the other campers are always fun to meet.

Keep up the good work. Thank you for maintaining this breathtakingly beautiful campground.

Bill Stenberg
reviews.author: William S.

reviews.text: We stayed here for 4 days and it was awesome! Great campsite, #32, right by the river, and plenty of privacy. The hosts are amazing as well. They had raked our campsite prior to our arrival, and were more than accommodating with our questions. We drove up to Crater Lake one day, hiked from camp to Rogue River Gorge, Natural Bridges and Upper Rogue River Trail. The gorge is a can't miss, and is less than half a mile from the camp. No campfires were a bummer, but still one of the nicest campsites we have had in a long time. HIGHLY recommend this campground!
reviews.author: Stephanie B.

reviews.text:
Absolutely beautiful location.     Many people riding bikes around the campground.    Bathrooms were very clean and well kept.   Our campsite was right on the Rogue River so we were able to listen to the roar of this year's bounty of water all day and all night.   Only a mile from Becky's restaurant and Union Creek Lodge and store so we got our fresh pie fix and could pick up anything we needed at the store.    Love it!  
Normally we also include a drive up to Crater Lake but this early in the season the north entrance was still closed due to snow.
reviews.author: Debbie J.

reviews.text: This is one of my favorite parks.  Just far enough away from home yet still close enough for a quick trip!  We stayed in site 47 this time, this will be my go to site if we go alone.  It rained 2 out of the 4 days we were there and this was a first trip with a 10 month old puppy.  He did great despite the rain.  Beautiful campground and they happened to be stocking the Rogue River while we were there.  Great fishing!  Host very friendly and our site was clean upon arrive.  Cant wait for our next camp trip!
reviews.author: Deborah S.

reviews.text: I stayed in site 1, and while it is close to the hwy, it was not very noisy at all.  The sites are well spaced, so you do not feel like you are camping right on top of the next site.  Site 1 is also right along the river, so you have the sound of the water as well. The campground was in the process of some maintenance work, so fallen trees and branches were gathered into piles that would be removed in the future.  I would definitely stay here again if I were to pass through the area.
reviews.author: Catherine C.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Huge picnic table, plenty of room for multiple tents if needed, right across from the bathroom and right next to the river. The only downside would be how some people are going though your campsite in order to get to the river but most of them apologized for passing though and it really wasn’t that big of a deal. Otherwise it’s a huge campground with plenty of space in between neighbors so it doesn’t feel like you’re camping right next to someone
reviews.author: Wes C.

reviews.text:
We absolutely loved camping here! Campsite #18 is right on Rouge River. We fell asleep to the roaring sound of the river, which perfectly blocked any noise we would’ve heard from the highway or our neighbors. The location is oddly convenient. There is a country store minutes away, and plenty of attractions to check out in the surrounding area. 
The camp host is friendly and professional. We’d love to return to this campground in the future. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Mengge M.

reviews.text: Site 42 was wonderful next to the Rogue River. Site was spacious and level. Bugs were minimal (end of July) and the bathrooms were all flush-type. A couple of womens' were clogged though. Drove up to camp host's trailer to check-in. I spoke to the host through a screen door and never saw her, which was a bit odd. Gave us some instructions and we headed to our site. Great campground and highly recommend.
reviews.author: Dan F.

reviews.text: We camped here in a 40 ft 5th Wheel. It was a tight drive through the campground but if your careful, shouldn't have a problem. The campsites were spacious & felt secluded. Bathrooms were fairly clean. It is a wonderful campground, especially for dark sky viewing. Loved the river flowing behind most the sites. It was quiet & relaxing. I would definitely use this campground again!
reviews.author: Debra K.

reviews.text: The campground was nice with large private sites, and  the bathrooms had both flush toilets and electricity.  The soap ran out in the women’s restroom and wasn’t replaced for several days.  The Rogue Gorge and Takelma Gorge were both amazing.  The Upper Rogue trail is well kept and gives a lot of hiking options.  The campground is only 25 miles from Crater Lake for an easy day trip.
reviews.author: Maryann M.

reviews.text:
The campsites and restrooms were very well maintained.   Also, the camp host Kevin was very friendly, helpful. and did a great job.
It's a short drive to Crater Lake National Park from the campground, but even spending the day fishing and hiking along the Rogue River, which runs through Farewell Bend, is a nice way to spend a day.
reviews.author: JEFFREY A.

reviews.text: even though it is somewhat a no frills campground as far as trailer hookups it is a beautiful place to visit.  the Rogue river is right there and has interesting things to see as well as some decent trout fishing.  Most sites have pretty level driveways for setting up trailers and are large enough to set up a tent or 2.
reviews.author: Richard S.

reviews.text: We loved our time at Farewell Bend CG! The location was perfect for visiting Crater Lake and fishing @ Diamond or Lemolo Lakes.  Our site was perfect for us, spacious and right on the river. Quiet on that side, no road noise at all. We would definitely stay here again and recommend this CG!
reviews.author: Deanne H.

reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Clean and well maintained. Our site was very private and quiet. The main road is pretty close but the sound of the river nearby covers any sound from the road. There was plenty of room for a big tent or multiple tents. Would stay here again.
reviews.author: Amy A.

reviews.text: The camp host Kevin is ON POINT! We brought a brand new Blackstone camp griddle and the dang thing was a dud from the manufacturer !!! In comes Kevin: U can borrow my little grill! He brought it to our camp site and we grilled all weekend!!! You Rock Kevin!!
reviews.author: Kyle S.

reviews.text: Campground was amazing! Camphost not so much. Not very friendly and a bit rude. Bathrooms were not maintained the entire time we were there Friday-Sunday! No toilet paper in either bathrooms and the womens bathrooms had a clogged toilet and was never fixed.
reviews.author: Mark F.

reviews.text: Campgrounds were clean. Restrooms were clean. Anti-bacterial was available. Toilets, Sinks and Counters were cleaned daily.  Water spigots were clean as well.  Most campers followed the rules. Quiet time was observed. No problems at all.
reviews.author: Myra A.

reviews.text: Beautiful campgrounds with all the amenities you'll need. The restrooms were clean. The play area for the kids is fantastic, and the location is great just by the Rogue river. The host was very helpful with a couple of questions.
reviews.author: Jacob  S.

reviews.text: Didn’t want to take our chances with FF sites at Crater Lake so we booked here instead. We are so happy that we did because we absolutely loved the spacious sites, creek running through, quiet conditions, etc.
reviews.author: Jennifer  P.

reviews.text: The campsite was great and we are looking forward to going back next year.The only thing that would of been better is if there was a dump station for our trailers that is closer then Shady Cove.
reviews.author: Louis  M.

reviews.text: This campground is the nicest place I have ever stayed. It is right on a creek with little waterfalls and swimming holes. Everything was so clean and the sites were big. Such a happy place
reviews.author: Angela G.

reviews.text: Great place, beautiful area, and great camping. Hardly anyone there due to the conflict with the care giver companies. The forest service ladies who gave me info were great.
reviews.author: David T.

reviews.text: Very beautiful setting.  Would be better with hookups.  Also, Jackson County will not allow dumping of grey and black water at Stewart Park making disposal more difficult.
reviews.author: David D.

reviews.text: The camp hosts kept this campground spotless - clean sites and squeaky clean restrooms. Beautiful spot next to the Rogue River and an easy hike to the Canyon of the Rogue.
reviews.author: Anne P.

reviews.text: Apart from the noise from the highway, the rest of it was pretty pleasurable. FYI: there are uninvited guests (read scorpions) in the campsite
reviews.author: Pramod S.

reviews.text: Such a beautiful spot on the river! Sites are large and somewhat private. Camp hosts kept the campground nice and bathrooms were very clean.
reviews.author: Tammra T.

reviews.text: A great campground anytime of the year! Spaces 1-12 are quite barren now due to the removal of some trees and underbrush.
reviews.author: Suzette W.

reviews.text: We always enjoy camping there.  It's a quiet campground and we enjoy the fishing.  It's our favorite place to camp.
reviews.author: Mary L.

reviews.text: Crater Lake is spectacular and being able to stay in the park is so convenient. We stayed in a large RV full hookup site. The site was level and we could easily back out 41 foot 5th wheel in. The site was littered with trash though. There were plastic water bottles and bits of paper everywhere. We left it better than found.
reviews.author: Robert  W.

reviews.text: Campsite was large and secluded, amenities were excellent. One word of advice: if you’re someone who gets eaten alive by mosquitos make sure you bring your repellent because they were out in force!
reviews.author: Lydia B.

reviews.text: Mazama Campground literally has everything you need, from the 24 hr access to hot showers to restrooms and delicious food at the restaurant! We can wait to return and explore more of the park!
reviews.author: Crystal C.

reviews.text: RV campsites are spacious, lack of generators running was a plus, and access to the activities and sights throughout the National Park as a whole were easy to access. Can’t wait to come back!
reviews.author: Jennifer M.

reviews.text: The campground sites were spacious, the facilities were clean, and the staff was professional.
reviews.author: Joanna T.

reviews.text: Friendly staff, very large site. Clean bathrooms. Loved our stay. Beautiful Lake!
reviews.author: Thomas S.

reviews.text: SO CROWDED!  And so many generators.  Holy cow.  Insane.
reviews.author: Leslie R.

reviews.text: crowded  but nice
reviews.author: Dana K.

reviews.text: Mazama Campground is nicely wooded, and the sites have decent separation between them to allow for privacy. The water and dump fill station worked out great on the way in/out. There is also a water spigot across from the site (not threaded). Site F9 is in one of the best locations with the canyon on the camp side and trees between the neighboring sites. It is a huge site, though it's important to note that it isn't fully functional as a pull through. We have a 27 foot travel trailer and were able to drive in forward and position it well for solar (or shade, if desired). Due to the tree branches at the other side of the pull through loop (at about a 60 degree angle), it's not possible to drive out of the site without the branches coming into contact with the trailer. Instead, we backed out back onto the road, which worked out fine with some time and patience. The other unexpected aspect of this site is that the trail runs right behind it, so you will have people walking by regularly and there are no trees for privacy from the trail. This wasn't a major issue for us. In July, the waterfall wasn't flowing, though the creek down in the Canyon had some water that you could hear, but not see. And, you can get 2 bars of Verizon service about 50 feet away on the trail (not at the site itself). All in all, it was a good campground within about 10 minutes drive to the lake.
reviews.author: Laura P.

reviews.text: This is a lovely campground. We camped in D loop and had a spacious site with lots of tall trees, pleasant surroundings, and a nice walking trail right behind our campsite that looped down into the canyon behind the campground. The proximity to the village store and Crater Lake itself was absolutely fantastic. It was a quick drive to the visitor centers and any hike we wanted to do by the lake. The showers at the village store, just a couple minutes from our campsite, were warm and free. My only complaints concerned the restroom near our campsite and the complete lack of dishwater disposal. There was only one restroom for our whole loop, and it looked like this was the case for most loops at the campground. It was fairly clean, but each side had only one sink with cold water only and a button that had to be held down to keep the water flowing so you could only rinse one hand at a time. Also our reservation confirmation said there would be drains for dish water in front of each restroom and there was not! We couldn't find dishwater disposal anywhere in our loop which made doing dishes a huge pain.
reviews.author: Molly W.

reviews.text: The ground where it was level to place a tent was covered with ant nests and other critter holes, so we moved our tent to the edge of the plot so we wouldn't be camping in ant beds. The first night was delightful with quiet and stars galore. The weather both nights was great. The second night we had new neighbors on one side (the close side) and they stayed up until 11 pm talking loudly, shining their headlamp all over our site (not on purpose), then arguing loudly for another hour.  I did not want to say anything to them, like "Quiet time was at 10 pm" because it was possible alcohol was involved and I did not want to get involved and possibly make it worse.  So I lay in my tent wide awake.  Noisy, rude, clueless neighbors are not in your control, but it ruined the second night.  Maybe next time I'll find a more remote campsite.  On a good note, the bathroom was clean and everyone else was very nice and accommodating.
reviews.author: Michele M.

reviews.text: Warning - this review is brutally honest.  We arrived at the Mazama Village just after sunset on a cold and wet evening. Being our 1st time there, we ventured into the store and checked it out to realize the shop was well stocked and very very expensive. We got some basic instructions from the staff about the location of facilities and were off to our site. The campsite was adequate with poorly maintained roads. Even worse were the very poorly cleaned bathrooms. The next morning we went to the showers. This is after we were in Canada and other locations on the way in Oregon and Idaho, to find the facilities terribly old and so very unsanitary. The shower drain was similar to the open trough system used 20 years ago in sporting arena's. Really think twice before exposing your loved ones to these facilities. Things are poorly out dated and sadly overpriced.
reviews.author: andy s.

reviews.text:
We reserved a RV site  for July 14 with electric power (site F20). When arrived there was no electric power at our site. I went to the registraton office looking for help but the office was closed with a notice posted on the window saying "power outage"; It seems the whole camp ground was out of power that day; there was no light in the bathroom and no hot water for shower. 
I was disappointed that we could not have electric power that day at Mazama Village Campgrounda. Our portable power station was out of juice from the last camp site we stayed and we rely on this stay in Mazama to recharge our portable power station. After Mazama we traveled to another National Park that we need our portable power station to power our refrigerator for the rest of our trip.
We paid for a site with electricity but too bad that we did not get what we paid for.
reviews.author: Brenda  C.

reviews.text: Tried for a spot a couple of weeks before we were heading to Crater Lake and of course they were full. Signed up on the Wait List, never expecting to hear anything. A week before the date we planned on visiting the park, got two notices of cancellations. We were able to secure one of the spots and it turned out to be one of the best campsites we have ever had- F9. (No hook-ups, but we tent, so it worked just fine for us.)  Big, clean spot with a beautiful view of the canyon. Campground was very quiet at night. Picked up pizza from Annie Creek Restaurant by the General Store and brought it back to our site. Nice amenity for a campground!  Bathrooms and showers served their purpose.  Truly one of our favorite campsites and we have been camping for over 30 yrs.
reviews.author: Leslie R.

reviews.text: Mazama Campground benefits from a great location, and because of that, they don't care much about quality. My campsite itself was clean and spacious, but the facilities left a lot to be desired. The entire campground has only one shower area (with an additional shower at the general store during limited hours). The restroom near my site was consistently filthy and never had paper towels. I followed the usual advice to buy firewood locally, but the price at the general store was steep—$13 per bundle. If possible, buy your firewood nearby but outside the campground. Overall, the location makes Mazama Campground worth considering, but the management doesn’t appear to put much effort into maintaining the facilities or creating a welcoming experience.
reviews.author: Giovanni C.

reviews.text:
Staying at this site was a delight! The location was fantastic- quiet at night, walking distance to Curry Village restaurants and shops. The cabin was well maintained, clean, comfortable, nicely decorated and everything worked. Our cabin had 2 beds and a dresser and we were comfortably about to fit a pack-n-play in as well. I’m not a great camper and we have a baby, but the cabin made “camping” very accessible to me. We were really pleased with the whole experience. Never having stayed inside the park before, you get a totally different experience staying inside the park. Kudos to the cleaning and maintenance staff! We can’t wait to book again! 
Also the first weekend of October was a lovely time to visit, low crowds, good weather.
reviews.author: Randena M.

reviews.text: We had a great time and the tent site was really spacious. It was relatively private feeling considering how many sites there are, and there were no street lamps to keep us up at night. The campsite had soft dirt that was easy to sink our tent spikes into, but also a lot of  tree stumps that were very "tripping you in the middle of the night" height. The restroom in our loop was out of service which we were not informed of. I thought it was strange that no one told us that when we were booking OR checking in, I feel like the sites in that loop maybe should have received a discount considering how far away the other restrooms were. But still, overall we had fun and swimming in Crater lake was 100% worth it!
reviews.author: Emily S.

reviews.text: This is a good campground with dense trees. G22 was relatively private, and right on the Annie Creek gorge.  The Annie Creek trail went along the back of the campsite, but there were huge trees down to make a barrier, so the hikers didn’t encroach on the camp site and weren’t a bother. The picture in recreation.gov did not correspond to the site. Many choice spots for a tent. The bathrooms were clean and well maintained.  G22 is near the end of the G loop and the bathrooms are at the beginning.  I measured the distance with my GPS watch, and a round trip to the restroom from G22 was a quarter mile. Water is right across the road from the site. The Mazama Village camp store has free showers.
reviews.author: Anne C.

reviews.text: My first time at the Mazama campground,  not my first time to Crater Lake.   Very nice campground, clean bathrooms, trash & recycle containers emptied daily.  Staff throughout the park was friendly and helpful.   There was however a bathroom on the loop next to our loop that was closed the 4 days we were there, the campers in D loop were using the bathrooms on C loop which in and of itself wasn't a problem,  but they were cutting through our campsite to get to them.  That's weird and annoying when a stream of people are walking in you campsite day and night.   Showers were located next to the Mazama Village store and were pretty moldy.   I showered in my RV instead.
reviews.author: Laura C.

reviews.text: My campground didn’t have a fire ring, yet the previous campers left me a whole bunch of scraps of wood on my bear locker and charred wood and ash in the small grill. They also left me a bag of potatoes. There was no pay phone anywhere on site, and I didn’t have any service the majority of the time. The folks at the store offered to let me use their phone, as I was solo traveling and needed to check in with my partner. The showers were ok. My site was not great for van camping — I could only park on the paved driveway. I was really annoyed by children whizzing about on scooters all night long. It was convenient and comfortable but not fabulous.
reviews.author: Patricia D.

reviews.text: This site is by the dump station which meant there was some traffic during the day but honestly it wasn't disruptive at all. No smells or nuisance, everyone was quick and respectful. It was actually nice to be a bit separated from the other campsites. Clean bathroom right next to the campsite and the showers at the store were nice and hot. The only downside to this site is I found a mouse in my van on my last night. I'm pretty sure he was in and out after he didn't find food in my rig, didn't make his home in my home thank goodness and I didn't see or hear him the day after.
reviews.author: Kelton G.

reviews.text: We were assigned a 50 ft. drive through site for our 26’ travel trailer and thought that should more than adequately fit our trailer and truck. The site was plenty long but the drive in and out areas were bordered by trees, posts and large rocks making it hard to maneuver the truck and trailer into and out of the site. Beware that this campground is not big rig friendly. Our travel trailer is 26”.  Dump station is easy to access. They also charge tax on the nightly fee. We found this unusual for a recreation.gov campground.
reviews.author: Marilyn H.

reviews.text: The campground was clean for the most part, but they are definitely suffering for help. By Saturday, the bathrooms were disgusting and we knew it was because they did not have help to keep up with all the campers. There were a lot of fallen trees throughout all the sites, which definitely helped those of us with axes to cut wood vs purchasing. Our fire grate was literally covered by a tree and we didn’t see it until our 3rd day under the tree. We made a rock pit to burn in the evenings. Other than that, a nice campground.
reviews.author: Doria A.

reviews.text:
We were in Loop G, campsite G2. This campsite is right next to the restrooms which was great, but at night the outside light does not turnoff. This light will shine into your tent, I recommending bringing a sleep mask. You will also get early morning noise with those visiting the restrooms. We were also one of the only campsites without a picnic table. 

The store was great, and nice to have available. They do sell out of ice early. Overall, the campsite was quiet and clean. We would revisit, but pick a different site.
reviews.author: Emily S.

reviews.text: Signage in the campground after “checking in” is worthless.   About as worthless as the guy in the store that didn’t check us in, just told us to go to our reserved spot.  Funny my reservation still shows open (on the app) the night after I used it.   I was told at the gate to check in at the store.   I did, he acted like we (me and a stranger) were idiots.  The signs are nonexistent from in front of the store to the campground.  Me, and two others I didn’t know did the exact same thing and drove past the cabins.
reviews.author: William  R.

reviews.text: The campground was excellent!. Fire pits for S’mores and clean bathrooms were nice after backpacking for 3 days in between the two nights we stayed there.  We were in section G both nights which was quiet and overlooked Annie Creek.  The Annie Creek canyon trail was as beautiful as anything we saw during our 5 day camping and backpacking trip in Crater Lake National Park and having dinner in the restaurant named after Annie Creek after the conclusion of our backpacking was a welcome respite from rehydrated food.
reviews.author: Steven M.

reviews.text: Nice campground within the park. The bathrooms were good. Could use some hangers in the bathrooms. Confused about the First Come campsites. Had to wait until 12 pm to actually get a site. And there was no guidance by the park staff to inform people about forming a line. Just groups of people standing around then chaos at 12.  You should be able to go get an unreserved site and come back to the office and then register that site.. first come. Or a least give out numbers to people so less chaos at 12.
reviews.author: Robert S.

reviews.text: Campsites were okay but bathrooms were very neglected.  I used to own a campground and a resort so know first hand how to clean a bathroom.  The toilets in the building near our site the first night not only had not been cleaned that day but probably not that week or even longer.  For a National Park this is an embarrassment to our Country.  I hate to think what a foreign visitor would think seeing such filthy conditions.  I have photos should you want to see.
reviews.author: Jim R.

reviews.text: We had a wonderful time! The camping store had some great essentials, and the showers were clean and well maintained. Our site, tent site, was well maintained too. Only issue was the grill we had with our campground; it was not cleaned out and the grill portion itself was bent so badly all our cookware leaned making it hard to cook on. Other than that, the bathrooms close to our site were very clean and always had toilet paper. Highly recommend staying here.
reviews.author: Stephanie H.

reviews.text: Overall very happy with our stay at Mazama Village. The sites felt quite private, despite the size and density of the campground. No issues with our electrical hookups; the provided bear-proof cabinet worked great; water and bathrooms were both nearby. Only issue was one of the two showers was out of order and the other had a clogged drain. Still, the water got hot and it didn’t cost quarters like we’d anticipated, so it still got the job done ok.
reviews.author: Bradley O.

reviews.text: It was nice and quiet. Loob B close to the store for back and forth needs. Bathroom, water spout all close by. Neighboring camps sites also close by so it does not seem isolated. We took advantage of the EV charging near park entrance and restaurant. Also a hiking trail near by that we unfortunately did not get to take advantage of. Would recommend and stay there again due to proximity, safety, ev charging source and bathroom/shower amenities.
reviews.author: Orea W.

reviews.text: Only annoying issue with our site B10 was that the electric stand was not centered on the site.  It was down on one end that required us to park closer to it rather than where we would have wanted to park.  We had an extension cord but it wasn't long enough. Quiet campground even as full as it was. Unfortunately the laundry was not functional while we were there.  The showers were greatly appreciated though.  Only had wifi up at the store.
reviews.author: Jennifer T.

reviews.text: This is a lovely campground, with a nice trail accessible from the campground and more trails accessible by car within this gorgeous national park.  Be aware that there are no showers in loop G, where I stayed.  There were three showers in nearby loop F, but all three were closed.  Also, be aware that, while you can buy ice in the camp store, it is $12 a bag, so it's best to stock up on ice and other items outside of the park.
reviews.author: Juanita H.

reviews.text: The campsites were beautiful with lots of room between them.  I especially loved the sites on the edge of the canyon.  Dark skies were very visible with lovely star-filled nights.  My only complaint is the cleanliness of the shower stalls, and the lack of wi-fi.  However, as the desk service person gently stated, here is a place to "disconnect."  Wi-fi is available in the restaurant and at the check-in office.
reviews.author: Barbara S.

reviews.text:
Hike to the Watchman Overlook.
Hike the Castle Crest Wildflower Trail.
Hike the Pacific Crest Trail south from Highway 62.
Take showers in the restrooms next to the camp store.
Get cold drinks, sandwiches, snacks, and ice cream at the camp store.
Have a delicious breakfast, lunch, and/or dinner at the Annie Creek Restaurant.
Enjoy Wifi at the camp store and wifi and cell phone service at the restaurant.
reviews.author: Ted L.

reviews.text: The campground is large but doesnt feel overcrowded. The spots aren't very private but they are reasonably spread out and surrounded by pines. Plenty of water stations and bathrooms, but showers are only at the reigstration building. Only complaint is that site C1 doesn't have a picnic table so we had to use the bear box. Try to bring all supplies with you, the camp store has some but prices are high.
reviews.author: Amanda H.

reviews.text: The person at the registration desk was very unhelpful. He didn’t greet us or even offer us a map of the campground or any other information. When we arrived at our campsite, it hadn’t been cleaned. There was a large piece of used foil left on the grill as well as a huge log partially burnt left next to the pit, not to mention the profuse amount of mosquitoes that together made our stay disappointing.
reviews.author: Monique V.

reviews.text: Great place to stay! Very conveniently located inside Crater Lake Nat Park. Super close to the general store, which I didn't realize had showers and a gas station. Definitely competitive to get a spot, but a nice campground overall with running water and bathrooms. Very clean, had everything we needed. Not much privacy, i.e. not many trees or anything between each campsite, but still very nice.
reviews.author: Alyssa C.

reviews.text: We really enjoyed our stay at this campground. The camp sites were sold out while we were there, but we still felt we were separate and had a lot of privacy. The sites are laced out in a way that you’re not right on top of each other - mind you, we were in a tent only area. It may feel very different in the other areas. We like tent only! The spots and the facilities were clean and well kept!
reviews.author: Wanda L.

reviews.text: The E loop is FCFS, 55 sites. Only drawback is to get a site, you have to wait in line. The line doesn’t start moving until 2:00. We arrived at 1:00, walked the loop for desirable sites. At 1:30, there were already about 15 in line. We got our site at 2:45, it was a very slow moving line. We got the site we requested which was large with shade and sun. Very clean bathrooms. Will visit again.
reviews.author: Barbara H.

reviews.text: I have stayed at many campgrounds and this one is by far one of the most peaceful.  We tent and had a lot of privacy.  The sites were all very large with reasonably close water spigots.  The only negative - the bathroom in our loop could really use some updating.  The staff did their best to keep it clean, but we opted to use the bathrooms near the camp store with the showers.
reviews.author: Laura R.

reviews.text: Facilities were really clean.  It is a beautiful location and the campsites are very well spaced to provide privacy and enjoyment of nature.  The showers were excellent.  We went to 2 ranger programs which were very educational.  We enjoyed the evening program and then watching the meteor showers.  Employees were friendly and helpful.  Had a wonderful overall experience.
reviews.author: Judy M.

reviews.text:
My campsite was a total river. The guy at the reception said there were no other campsites available even though the other attendant SOLD 3 campsites while we were talking. Then he claimed he could not issue a refund since it was past some hour. I ended up sleeping outside of the park. 
Terrible customer service, worst I have ever encountered in a national or state park.
reviews.author: Ewa B.

reviews.text: Had site D 18. Camped in a 32’ fifth wheel. It is a pull through but better to back into with a bigger. Not many sites for bigger rigs so pick a site wisely. Interior roads have lots of branches hanging out but it’s manageable if you don’t mind them rubbing some but no damage. No Verizon service but WiFi available at Manama village gift shop within walking distance.
reviews.author: Brian M.

reviews.text: Had a great experience at Mazama Village Campground. Sites are clean and well spaced out. Bathrooms are clean and really appreciated the free hot water showers located at each bathroom.  The cafe has a good menu for all meals and the general store has everything else. Minutes away from the Crater Lake, Mazama Village Campground really made everything perfect.
reviews.author: Philippe S.

reviews.text: The campground was clean, the employees were friendly and helpful. There were many walks that were easy to moderate, providing wonderful views of the lake and the surrounding areas. Traffic near the Lodge in the afternoon was very busy. My only issue was that the campground store did not stock ice in bags smaller than 16 pounds. Overall had a great time.
reviews.author: Denise B.

reviews.text: Beautiful location amongst the trees. Pull-thru sites are nice but difficult to get in properly for longer rigs because the site pad is narrow and curved with large rocks lining the edges of the site. We have a 35' fifth wheel and had to make quite a few adjustments to get aligned properly. Great location for seeing the park and enjoying the outdoors.
reviews.author: Michael M.

reviews.text: The campgrounds are excellent, and the on-site trail is a must-visit. Some sites inside the loop lack privacy, so if that matters, choose one on the outer edge, which is right on the canyon's edge. The location near Crater Lake is convenient, and although it was very hot at Crater Lake, the trees and shade at the campsite made it quite comfortable.
reviews.author: Johann S.

reviews.text: The staff we interacted with were excellent and welcoming, the campgrounds were clean and easily accessible.  Please keep our national park service funded as well as the teams of people it takes to preserve these natural wonders for generations to come as intended when they were founded.  It was really nice to be able to charge my electric vehicle.
reviews.author: Benjamin S.

reviews.text: Beautiful forested campground with tons of fairly private, flat sites! Lots of garbage receptacles and easy access to spigots. Soap, running water, and paper towels in restrooms, but not enough stalls for the number of tent sites around each facility. Camp store had great selection of beverages and ice cream. About a 20 minute drive from Rim Village.
reviews.author: Jacqueline I.

reviews.text:
I parked by the Lakehouse tap and checked out the beautiful lake, which seems to be packed with fish.

Then I travelled to the trails that I took a picture of. The forest trails are nice and well kept. Plenty of flora and fauna all around. There is also a trail to a quarry pond which is pretty cool.

The lush forest provided excellent cooling shade as I explored the area. The forest loop trail had a very interesting tree that had a hole in it, check it out on my pics.

The lake area had plenty of benches with grills and there was even a boat rental place and a store for goods. Nice bathrooms and accomodations. A very nice park to visit with your friends and family. Enjoy!
