reviews.author: SeekJohn14v6

reviews.text: This campground is awesome. Spots are large, open, and plenty of flat ground for a tent or three. Definitely recommend walking to the lake but the real highlight was the old growth forest trails! Budget out at least an hour or two to walk around the trails but maybe take some extra time! The campground itself can be quite loud on weekends in the summer but the trails were super quiet and peaceful. A little something for everyone. Would definitely go again!
reviews.author: Logan M.

reviews.text: Beautiful Fellowship with my Camping Buddies, Family, and Friends!  They played volleyball, rode their bikes and roller skating, went swimming 🏊‍♂️, and adults and youth raising.  Other campers, kids, and Family joined us in fun activities to including dining with us.  This was a beautiful day.  Thank you to park Staff Gentleman for putting up the Volleyball net because my extended family had a Volleyball ready!  We had three sites together ❤️
reviews.author: Deborah W.

reviews.text:
The lake and trails are great with super friendly staff!  We go every chance we get.  It can get pretty crowded around the water and swimming areas as well as the campsites are pretty full in good weather but it is worth it!

Just watch out for fishing line along the edges of the water.  My dog got caught in some line and I had to go in to untangle him.
reviews.author: J W.

reviews.text: Big chill! Great forest camping. The sites are spacious and clean. The other campers were respectful, some kids but not too loud. Most sites are in the trees and shaded. Lots of trails to walk or run. Bathrooms are nice with toilet paper and shower facility.
reviews.author: Ben S.

reviews.text: A beautiful lake located along the route to Mount Rainier, near the town of Elbe. Its water comes from rivers fed by the melting snow of the mountain, making it exceptionally cold and refreshing. The lake is connected to Alder Dam, which supplies drinking water to the city of Tacoma. It’s a stunning spot for boating, kayaking, canoeing, and jet skiing.
reviews.author: VanTrips G.

reviews.text: It’s a beautiful park with a great view of the lake. I wish there’s a trail to walk / bike around the lake, but there’s no. If you happen to have some extra time during your trip to Mt Rainier, then you can stop by here to enjoy the beautiful view of the lake. The view of the dam is also pretty interesting.
reviews.author: Y.C. W.

reviews.text: Impressive due to silence outside camping season, unfortunatelly the waterlevel was far below average showing a climate  impacted scene.
reviews.author: vlp p.

reviews.text: I grew up on this lake and still love coming back whenever I can, it's still as beautiful as it always was.
reviews.author: Sarah P.

reviews.text: Lake is clean and have a designated area for family swimming.
reviews.author: Crazy B.

reviews.text:
Let me start by saying this is a beautiful place. Nothing can diminish that, except persistent winds, and when the wind dies down in summer plenty of bugs.
I like it in fall, when the colors really come out. Sadly, the campground with the best colors usually closes at the peak of said colors.
My current gripe is more of a system wide complaint - the new system the state parks are using is flawed. We are talking about an electronic (database) system for reservations and registration. The idea is great - reservations up until like 2pm, then FCFS registration afterwards.
The reality sucks. It is NOT functioning right. 3 times in one 5 day trip at 3 different state parks the system failed to work for me.
You are supposed to call and register for your site if you have been unable to make a reservation. What happened to me is that they were unable each time to register me for the open spot of my choosing.
It is ridiculous. Fortunately, at the other 2 state parks, there were staff around to sort things out. Not so at Lake Wenatchee.
Then, their instructions clearly stated NOT to put money in a registratiin envelope, rather to square up at the booth. But the booth is closed for the season. And the ranger I finally discussed this with offered no solution besides call the phone number, which did not solve the problem.
Finally a maintenance worker told me I could put cash in the envelope, so I did.
I really hope they figure this out. At one of the other campgrounds, I got a look at their system in action - they could not put me in my site for another night until refreshing the page multiple times. Could be a very fun camping season at Washington State Parks.
Word of wisdom: bring cash, and you still can put it in an envelope, maybe.
reviews.author: Seth S.

reviews.text:
Unfortunately due to some car issues we didn’t get to spend as much time at the lake as we wanted to. But we did make it up in the late afternoon and I could tell instantly that this would be a wonderful area to have a picnic at. We only visited the beach area but there were plenty of picnic benches both on the beach and in the wooded areas. The view across the lake was majestic and the bathroom facilities were clean and stocked.
Bonus points for having a wheelchair mat down to the water making this mobility challenge friendly
reviews.author: Dyanne G.

reviews.text: Went camping with my husband and two dogs here for the first time. This is the lake that faced my fears. I finally went out on a kayak with my husband! Best choice ever. We will be back! Great camping for children! This camp will keep your kids busy all day!
reviews.author: Marisa L.

reviews.text: Absolutely stunning views! Great place for a stroll outdoors after stopping by Leavenworth. Ample parking space, a boat launch area, warming cabin, campground, playground, and plenty of tables for picnicking.
reviews.author: Julia P.

reviews.text: One of the most beautiful lakes I’ve ever seen. The trails around the park were clearly marked and very scenic. I would love to spend more time here.
reviews.author: Mark P.

reviews.text: Beautiful park with plenty of activities for all ages! There’s a nice playground for kids and a swimming area with options to rent kayaks and jet skis. Campsites are well-maintained, and the bathrooms (with showers) were clean. While most sites don’t offer much privacy, the lake views and stunning sunsets more than make up for it. We even caught fireworks from the lake — such a fun bonus! We stayed at campsite 85 and really enjoyed our time here.
reviews.author: Pooja R.

reviews.text: Chelan State Park is beautiful. You've got a great camping area, solid bathrooms with showers, a generous playground and the beachfront at the base of the stairwell. Designated swimming is blocked off to keep watersports from crossing over into swimmers. Lovely park and would recommend it to anyone looking for some light, family camping.
reviews.author: J B.

reviews.text: Such a beautiful, clean lake.  The bathroom near our campsite had 4 individual showers and clean bathrooms.  Beautiful view of the lake.  Be prepared fir lots of boating noise in the summer, and I mean a lot!  Campsite had great view of the water and the sunrise.
reviews.author: K M.

reviews.text: Beautiful place to go. Mountain view lodge is amazing place to stay with your family including your 4 legged friend. If going for fishing, I suggest a boat before June when the lake is full after June there will be better bank fishing
reviews.author: Shannon K.

reviews.text: Lovely campground! Beautiful Lake! Rented a boat in town and had a few lovely days with the family. Has a swimming area, playground for kids. Only thing I wish it had more of is beach area. A wonderful place to go!
reviews.author: Julie W.

reviews.text:
Glamped here 03/21/25-03/24/25
This is an amazing beach. Our 1st full day was absolutely perfect! Wind was low, the tide was going out, and it wasn't busy at all. The next day, we were in for a good storm! We checked the weather beforehand, and since we live in WA, we knew what we were going into. We watched the storm out our glamper window, which had the beach view. Very impressive!
These sites only have an electrical hook up. There is a dump station. YOU WILL NEED TO FILL UP FRESH WATER TANK BEFORE HAND. The water there isn't for drinking use, so you can't fill up your tank there. They do have water spigots, but they aren't filtered. This was our 1st time without water hookup, and we just went to the store down the road to purchase portable gallons of water. This is our fault for not planning correctly, so I won't docks stars for my ignorance. I just want to point out that there isn't a place to fill up your fresh water tank. The website does, in fact, state this.
The showers were creepy and slightly gross but worked very well. They could use some tile replacement for the broken tiles and a good scrub. The bathrooms were very clean. The bathrooms near the check-in station were closed due to vandalism.
All in all, this park is amazing and we will be coming back!
reviews.author: Tara H.

reviews.text: From my campsite I could sit and watch the ocean or walk to the beach in about one minute. Beautiful views and sunsets. Portable gas/propane firepits are allowed; wood fires can only be out on the beach. I didn't find the campsite to have much privacy. Some of the bathrooms are closed due to vandalism. The beach was not at all crowded; you can walk for miles, fly kites, and star gaze at night.
reviews.author: Wildcraft R.

reviews.text: This was my first visit to the beach for the purpose of clamming. It was also on my first outings in my nearly acquired RV. It was exciting and tons of fun. We kept out along Joe Creek and had a wonderful experience. The weather was chilly Willy, of course, but otherwise clear and pleasant. The park was convenient to the beach and I had no complaints.
reviews.author: Blu O.

reviews.text: Great spot for easy access to the beach. 30 Amp power available for our 5th wheel. For the first time visiting the grass wasn't mowed and there was clam shells from last visitor in our space.The restrooms were clean, though the showers could use some maintenance. Still a fun relaxing place to stay.
reviews.author: Jay G.

reviews.text: Nice view of the Pacific Ocean.  Need Discover Pass to park. Places to picnic. A park station. Was not to crowded in the spring. Can be cold and windy.
reviews.author: Cecil C.

reviews.text: Such a beautiful location, went on a Monday so my group was mostly alone for the time we were there. Arrived and went to the Tongue Point when the tide was going back out and this opened up lots of tide pools. Got to see some diverse wildlife like invertebrates, birds, and fish. We took my seven year old nephew and he was able to climb up and down the rocks but with help. If you have kids I would be aware it might be difficult to get down to the water if they are younger but still doable depending on the tide!! As with any tide pools be careful where you step, there were barnacles, anemone and mussels all over the rocks, I’d recommend water shoes :)
reviews.author: Lola M.

reviews.text: Salt Creek is honestly a PNW Paradise.  It’s where the lush green forest literally tumbles right into the beautiful blue sea. You can spend hours wandering through the old WWII bunkers hidden in the woods, then head down to the fingers below the bluff to find some of the most vibrant tide pools you’ll ever see, teeming with life. It’s one of those rare spots where history and the raw beauty of the coast just perfectly collide. You have to make sure to wander out onto the sand beach at the mouth of the creek too! If you catch the tide low enough, you can actually walk all the way out to the island to explore.
reviews.author: Joshua D.

reviews.text: Tons of parking and fee free during the winter.  So many camp sites with awesome views and nice bathrooms.  Nice playground and easy walkabout.  You can access the rocks and the sea but it’s down stairs and hiking the rocks.  Not for young kids or faint of heart.  Tons of campgrounds above the sea with amazing views.  There is extra parking with a few overnight.
reviews.author: Paldi P.

reviews.text: We spent several months living in Port Angeles and ended up spending more time here playing than any other single spot. It was fun to beach comb, watch sunsets, play in the water or the park. Something for everyone and not too crowded.
reviews.author: P T.

reviews.text: Great place to go camping and spending time with your loved ones. I love how much nature and the smell of sea waking up!! It’s a must go!! So many places to see and check out for days!! Netting new people!
reviews.author: Stephaine W.

reviews.text: This KOA is amazing! We experienced such friendly staff.  They continuously were busy around the campground,  making sure it was clean,  safe and making sure everything was running smoothly... and they always had a big smile on their faces and would wave greeting us everytime. The campground was really clean and the location is impeccable,  with the ocean being just a short walk across the street.  It's also close to several towns for supplies (although the store is fully stocked with anything you'd need as well) and so many beautiful trails.  We stayed in a cabin with 4 people. It was the perfect size,  very clean and nicely upkept,  and fully stocked.  We have older kids, and we still enjoyed the activities as a family,  with mini golf,  beanbags,  the pool/ hot tub and campfires! We highly recommend this location and we will be back!
reviews.author: Jessi C.

reviews.text: We booked a Kabin, which was clean but needs to be updated with some modern amenities (coffee maker, TV, complimentary items, etc.) and not rely totally on the location. We have stayed in many KOA locations, including one recently at Klamath Falls which was excellent, and this was on the lower end. Initially the service was great as we received an early check in notice text, but we could not reach a live person on the phone after making several attempts, although text messaging with another individual seemed to work fine.  This was not a concern when notifying the individual through text. Location is excellent for those wanting to visit nearby Astoria or the Lewis and Clark National Historical Park.
reviews.author: Korey

reviews.text:
We were pleasantly surprised by the 1 room camping cabin. As two adults who spent most daylight hours at others' campsites, it worked out nicely for sleep and storage.

The sleeping pads are more comfortable than they look, I didn't feel the need for any extra padding. In addition to bed linens, I would recommend also bringing your own curtains, as the supplied ones don't do much to block the morning light.
reviews.author: Graham W.

reviews.text: This is the best campground! We have 7 and 9 year old kids and they were in heaven. The facility is top notch, super clean and you never run out of things to do with all the activities and ft Steven’s being right across the street. The staff are all extremely friendly and seem to love their jobs. We cannot wait to return! Take a bike ride through ft Steven’s to the shipwreck, you won’t be disappointed!
reviews.author: Caitlin J.

reviews.text: We had an amazing stay at Warrenton / Seaside KOA Resort! Everything was great, clean, comfortable, and very family friendly. The staff was kind and helpful, and the atmosphere was wonderful. We enjoyed it so much that this is already our second time staying here, and we definitely want to come back again. Thank you for such a great experience!
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.text:
I recently stayed at South Beach State Park Campground, and it’s a great option if you’re looking for a convenient, well-equipped base along the Oregon coast. The campground is massive, with hundreds of sites spread across multiple loops, so it feels more like a small village than a secluded retreat. Despite its size, it’s clean, organized, and fairly quiet overall, with easy access to bathrooms, hot showers, and paved trails. The beach isn’t right next to most campsites, but it’s an easy and scenic walk through dunes and coastal forest, which adds to the experience.

That said, it definitely leans more developed than rustic. Sites can feel a bit close together, especially when it’s busy, so privacy is somewhat limited. If you’re camping near the playground, it can get pretty loud during the day. When I visited at the end of April, the mosquitoes were surprisingly intense, there were a lot of them, especially around dusk, so definitely bring bug spray. On the plus side, the location near Newport is super convenient for food and nearby attractions. Overall, South Beach is a solid, family-friendly campground that prioritizes comfort and location over seclusion, just be prepared for noise and bugs depending on where you’re camped and the time of year.
reviews.author: Vee K.

reviews.text: Cleanest campground we went to on our road trip. The walking trail to the beach was nice, they had a disc golf course, and the showers were free and also clean. Everything was well maintained. The temperature was perfect for cold weather type people like my husband and I. You could hear the crowds of sea lions in the distance, which we thought was funny, though it wasn't disturbingly loud. Slept great with the windows open on the rv. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.author: T T.

reviews.text: went here with family and we got a spot right next to the playground which wasn't really our plan but it was one of the only spots avaliable. the kids at the playground were active until late at night so it was quite annoying but one night the rangers got them. bathrooms are clean, so are showers, no long lines.
reviews.author: London (.

reviews.text: Camping and day use picnic area and beach access. Lots of parking available for visitors. I guesstimate about 100+ spots. Paved trail to a nearby jetty (1 mile).
reviews.author: Xbox U.

reviews.text: Great campsite. Good privacy and nice amenities. Even better than some private campsites
reviews.author: Linfang H.

reviews.text:
Great staff! We reserved 2 tent sites, unseen in person,(online photos), with power/ water. We arrived on a Monday, with the following Thursday as our departure day.
Unfortunately the weather decided to give us a challenge as it rained hard on Monday, we checked in and got directions to our sites. We pull up and discover that it had(&would continue for another 18 hours) to pour down rain.. like big heavy rain drops!
Both our sites were flooded.. like ankle deep water, small lakes exactly where our tents were supposed to go.. the only place they could be set up actually. I found all the tent sights to be on the small size. A larger tent(like anything that sleeps more than 4 would not fit any sites here.. unless set up on the pavement.  Then you can't anchor it down.)
Anyway, so back to the office and advised of the flooded sites. The ranger took a map and searched thru his computer until he found a selection of available sites next to each other for our reservation requirements to choose from. He said go drive the loops and look at the sites once we found the two that would work for us to come back and he got them switched for us.
The next day the rain wasn't as bad and the mosquitoes started looking for their food..aka us!
Make sure to bring bug spray or better still.. use the premithin spray that  lasts 6 weeks or 6 laundry washing on your tents, clothing, shoes, ect. Do not spray it on ur clothes while wearing ur clothes.. follow directions! We had 40% deer and it slowed them down a little.. not much. We also had the thermocell misting machine mosquitoe repellent  and 2 large costco brand citronella candles and finally the bug repellent sticks that you light, stick in the ground around ur site and it slowly burns.. we still got attacked by the mosquitoes  so be aware that there is an issue with the mosquitoes here!
Everywhere but the actual beach where the wind seems to keep them away.
Otherwise, all the attractions at the park are great. The rv sites Great, staff, awesome, plenty of hot water for showers.
Have fun in town lots of shops, attractions to do locally.
reviews.author: Christy S.

reviews.text:
Very nice campground that is well laid out. Close to a lot of different things to do. We used it as a base to explore the area South to Tillamook and over to Astoria, and also to the Washington side of Fort Canby. We especially liked Astoria with the Sunday market and the Astoria column at sunset.
One of the few negatives is the presence of mosquitoes near our campsite on h loop must be pretty boggy in the middle and nearby
The other negative is the cost of the sites with the addition of of fees I.e daily fees and markup for non-residents. This is not a cheap campground to stay at. But relative to the KOA across the street, it's still cheaper.
reviews.author: Hal K.

reviews.text:
Beautiful escape from city-life, just a few miles out. Quiet, peaceful, and easy to navigate.

Nice pull through available for bigger rigs.

$10 to dump, electric and water at the sites.

Elk roaming freely throughout the park, drive slowly and cautiously.

Restrooms close by, firepits and picnic tables all around.

This site shown is Loop F, #235.
reviews.author: JoAnn D.

reviews.text: Wonderful campground! Basic/clean/free hot showers. Paved bike paths, playgrounds, hiking trails. We had a nice, relatively private site : 236 F. Not perfectly level but worked fine. Laundromat just outside the park.
reviews.author: Cathy O.

reviews.text: Fun riding the trails. Bathrooms/showers were a little rough but lots of hot water. Came during fishing season, wouldn't suggest it unless you are fishing too. Loop E has showers.
reviews.author: Carl O.

reviews.text:
Love it here. For such a large campground a lot of the sites made you feel secluded. We came in week of spring break for a few days and then a few days after spring break and let me tell you that place was empty after school started again.
Restrooms and showers were very clean, sites clean, playground super clean. Beach access is near the A “loop if I’m not mistaken and is super easy to get to with restrooms right before the beach(helpful with kiddos).  The check in office is only open from 4-6 and you need to check in but if your checking in late and know it call them to let them know they’re all so kind. Will definitely be coming back knowing there’s a little walking trail by the creek that’s behind some of the sites.
reviews.author: Carlie D.

reviews.text: Had an amazing time this summer for the weekend. The camp sites were as expected and more. The trees and plants were beyond my expectations.  Friendly neighbor’s, lots of kiddos, Clean and hot showers. My Kiddos had a great time exploring, we went to the cookout area and gazed at the stars at night. Our favorite beach is 10minutes away. We were right between Lincoln city and Newport, right off the freeway! So tons of restaurants and grocery store near by!
reviews.author: Elizabeth N.

reviews.text: So this was the first time we've camped here since they reopened the park after extensive repair work. And I must say so happy to be back. Upgraded utilities, repaved most areas, and trimmed some bad trees out. Feels great, love this park, definitely recommend staying!
reviews.author: Clayton's R.

reviews.text: Fantastic forest/beach access campground. Great restrooms with hot showers. It's our favorite camp spot!
reviews.author: skip a.

reviews.text: Big parking lot! Easy access to beach. Trail could use improving. But great stop!
reviews.author: Jimmie F.

reviews.text:
This state park is a hidden gem in Washington. The beach is very beautiful, with sandy shores, stunning views, lighthouse in the backdrop, and easy access to the waterfront. Lots of jelly fish wash up to the shore - something unique. The state park has several fun hikes. The ones worth mention are the hikes to the Dead Man’s Cove and the one leading all the way up to the Lighthouse. Dead Man’s Cove offers some amazing secluded views, and the hike up to this spot is fun and moderate. The hike leading up to the Lighthouse tends to get a little steep towards the end, but is worth it. The views from the base of the Lighthouse are breathtaking. Lots of natural beauty, variety of birds, and sounds of nature to sit back and enjoy from your campsite.

We stayed in one of the log cabins and had a great experience. Our cabin was very well maintained, had fully functional heaters, electrical points, and some additional furniture. Just like any other log cabin, you’d need to bring along your bed supplies to make it comfortably to the bunk beds. The only thing we didnt like was the close proximity of the other camp sites. It offered very little privacy. There are several dining options in the area. We went to the Salt Pub and had a very good experience. The food and drinks were great, hosts very welcoming.

Overall, I’d highly recommend this state park, and the camp sites - its a nature lover’s delight.
reviews.author: Shubhro B.

reviews.text:
Lovely views all around! Roads were reasonably well-kept and easy to navigate for most vehicles. Some pretty patchy areas that may not be fun on a motorcycle, so if you're a rider keep your eyes out.

The North Head Lighthouse (pictured) was a very easy walk to get to, fully pathed and only gentle slopes. All the parking areas had easy turnarounds, well kept notice boards, and plenty of bathrooms around.

A very nice place to check out while you're in the area!
reviews.author: Julia F.

reviews.text: Beautiful Park with some amazing old growth trees. Lots of trails through the wooded area for bike or walking there is a steep incline. Most views are from the cliffs. The beach access and campground were closed at the beginning of April. Saw lots of birds and sea lions from a far on the cliffs. Bring your binoculars. Coast Guard area is not open to visitors.
reviews.author: Cheri P.

reviews.text:
As you have likely heard, you won't be disappointed... unless it is a cold wet rainy PNW day and you dressed wrong.

So, dress right and have fun - whatever for the weather (good luck, its always changing. Personally, rain jacket and pants stay in the car.)

Of course, I was lucky to be there on a lovely sunny day 😛
reviews.author: Nati's T.

reviews.text: What a beautiful place to sight see, hiking trails to explore, 10$ to park I think, I visited this to go to bells viewpoint for the first time and it did not disappoint, first time at a light house too
reviews.author: Jessica E.

reviews.text: While planning a trip from Northern California to Washington, we found Tumalo State Park Campground, in Tumalo Oregon. We were able to book a Yurt for one night. So, we did. This was our first time visiting Tumalo State Park and the campground. Booking was accomplished on line, with Reserve America. Check in was super easy, as I was sent an email with a code for a lock box, which had the key to the Yurt. The Yurt was clean and had a twin over full bunk, a futon, a coffee table and a table with two chairs. Electricity and electric heat, along with a ceiling fan. Also, an air purifier/fan. The Yurt was clean and neat. Bring your own bedding. Nothing but mattresses on the bunks and futon. Water was nearby, along with modern, clean restrooms and showers. However, my wife found the locks for the stall doors in the women's restroom were in need of maintenance. Across the street from the campground is the day use/picnic area, along the Deschutes river. What a great place. Overall, a nice place to camp and visit. In my opinion, the day use area was great. The campground was okay. The sites were too close for my liking. Not a lot of privacy or feeling of being away. Everyone was respectful, which makes for a good camping experience when in close proximity to other campers. That was my experience. Pictures are of the day use area.
reviews.author: Chris E.

reviews.text:
TIP: If you have a (normal-size Class B) campervan like a Ford Transit/Sprinter, and you find an available spot along the river in the A loop, it is indeed OK to camp there even though it's marked as a hiker/biker loop. The website says that the loop road is narrow, but vans are fine. (I emailed them to confirm that it was OK, and they replied that it was.) IMO, during high season it would be nice to reserve those spots for hikers/bikers, but we were there in late September so we felt OK about it. The A loop has flush toilets, sinks, and a trash can, but no lighting or other amenities.

We spent two nights in this campground on our way from Washington to Nevada and back. One night was on Loop B (25) and the second night was at a riverside spot on Loop A (87). Neither site had any privacy to speak of, but the setting was lovely, the sites were clean and relatively spacious, and the services were excellent. Flush toilets, electricity, even large outdoor sink areas to wash dishes (on Loop B). Cell coverage was minimal to non-existent but we were OK with that. We explored the day use area across the road and along the river, and had a really pleasant experience. You would never know that you're only a few minutes from Bend. Highly recommended!
reviews.author: Emily G.

reviews.text:
Tumalo State Park is hands down one of the best camping spots out there. The bathrooms are super clean, with great showers and toilets – a big plus when you’re camping. If you’re staying overnight, the yurts or cabins are definitely the way to go for comfort and convenience.

The Deschutes River runs right through the park, and it’s perfect for floating on tubes or rafts during the summer. We even saw plenty of wildlife, including adorable rabbits hopping around – five-star entertainment!

Another big bonus: Costco is only about 3 miles away, and you’re just 15 minutes from Old Bend. Easy access to everything you might need while still feeling like you’re out in nature. Absolutely my top pick for camping
reviews.author: Orlando M.

reviews.text: This is the nicest state park campground we have ever stayed in. Nice location, close to town. We enjoyed Tumalo, fun food trucks. Great cider at Tumalo cider.  The grounds are meticulously maintained. All amenities function properly, showers, bathroom, faucets, etc. We look forward to the next visit.
reviews.author: Marney T.

reviews.text: This is a beautiful campground, especially for being so near populated areas. The bathrooms are clean, warm, smell nice and there are also private showers. The campsites were well maintained and perfectly raked when we arrived.
reviews.author: Jesselyn G.

reviews.text: Definitely one of the best state park campgrounds we have stayed at. Right on the beautiful beach at Cape Lookout - there is six miles of beautiful beach for walking and relaxing, and the whales came to play every evening we were there. They were so close you could see them from the beach! We had a full hookup site for our trailer but there are a range of tent, RV and varying hookups available across the campground. Many of the camping sites had a great privacy hedge between the sites - felt like we had a little private garden of our own. Definitely a highlight of our trip down the Oregon coast!
reviews.author: Emily P.

reviews.text: I absolutely love Cape lookout. They have many very large sites that are full hookup. Cabins, yurts. Make sure you make reservations pretty far in advanced. They are usually very busy. Weekdays not so much, but once summer hits it's very busy. Absolutely beautiful beaches that are close. Great camp hosts. Showers bathrooms. Water spigots everywhere. One of my favorite places.
reviews.author: Jamie T.

reviews.text:
We had a great stay at Cape Lookout Campground! The best part is the location—just a short walk to the beach, making it so easy to enjoy the ocean anytime.

We also really appreciated how clean the restrooms were. The campground is peaceful, well-kept, and perfect for a relaxing getaway. We’d definitely come back!
reviews.author: Ha P.

reviews.text:
Cape Lookout has well equipped day use area. Some picnic tables are more accessible than others.

There is plenty of parking.

The bathrooms were well maintained. The path to the bathrooms is paved.

Access to the water is down a dirt trail below the picnic area.
reviews.author: She A.

reviews.text: Always liked it. Staff is ways courteous. Been coming once a year for 8 years. Unfortunate that they started inflating the price by 25% + to anyone coming from out of state. This is why I only give it 4 out of 5 stars.
reviews.author: D. K.

reviews.text:
We had a 3-night reservation here and were really looking forward to our stay. Unfortunately, we experienced a motorhome breakdown while traveling and were delayed waiting on parts to make our coach drivable again.

We stayed in communication and provided updates throughout. While they did offer the option to arrive later or extend our stay, those options would have required us to pay additional nights and didn’t actually solve the situation.

We even offered to accept a credit and return for a future stay, and were willing to provide documentation of the repair and parts delay, but that was not an option. In the end, we were charged for the full 3-night stay despite never being able to arrive.

We understand policies are in place, but RV travel comes with unexpected mechanical issues, and flexibility in those situations is extremely important.

Based on this experience, we would likely choose a property that is more accommodating to real-world travel challenges in the future.
reviews.author: sara B.

reviews.text:
I can't rate this resort low enough based on the service. I made the booking through a third party website which did not make it known that only RV's of a certain age and quality would be permitted. As Canadians, this came as a complete shock and we were left with nowhere to stay at peak season. In addition to losing our accommodations, no effort was made to reimburse or relocated us and we were out $650 for literally nothing.

This is the American stereotype manifest, small print that leads you to another small print document that has clauses buried. Just a malicious scheme that is completely outside of my understanding.

Do not book this location unless you've already got a $300,000 RV, but then again, if you've got that much invested already, who cares about losing $600.
reviews.author: Nicholas T.

reviews.text: This is a gorgeous RV Resort!!  We’ve come here many times over the years and the views are exceptional!  The crew keeps the grounds and common areas immaculate!  The bathrooms are spotless as well. (However one of the men’s toilets in the Clubhouse didn’t flush properly and needs to be fixed). The only complaint we have is that all restrooms don’t open until 7:30 am. They should be able to be open by 6 am at the latest. It seems many other guests felt the same way. Or keep the clubhouse restrooms open with the code 24 hours and keep the doors to the pool locked. It would certainly be a great improvement. Overall though, a fantastic place to spend at the ocean!!
reviews.author: Claire S.

reviews.text: If you own a class A or C coach, and we noticed class B also this trip, this is the place for you!  All of the RV sites are awesome, we particularly like the oceanfront ones, and the amenities are the best! This property is kept up perfectly at all times. People are friendly and respectful. The office staff, particularly Lisa, are amazing, helpful, fun, and make it so nice for everyone!!! We’ve stayed here about 50 times over the years and it’s better than ever, if that’s possible. We highly recommend!! The pictures are from our coach and on our walk to the beach on the private trail from the resort.
